name: St. Abercius of Hierapolis
title: Bishop, Equal-to-the-Apostles
bio: Bishop of Hierapolis in Phrygia in the late 2nd century, renowned as a missionary and wonder-worker. His famous epitaph, discovered in 1882, is one of the oldest Christian inscriptions and describes his travels to Rome and Mesopotamia proclaiming the faith.

locations.label: Episcopal see and death — Hierapolis (Pamukkale), Phrygia

name: St. Abibus of Nekresi
title: Bishop and Martyr
bio: One of the Thirteen Syrian Fathers, martyred as Bishop of Nekresi for openly condemning Zoroastrian fire-worship.

name: St. Abo of Tbilisi
title: Martyr
bio: An Arab perfumer converted to Christianity in Georgia and martyred by Muslim authorities in Tbilisi.

name: St. Abraham of Bulgaria
title: Martyr
bio: A wealthy merchant among the Volga Bulgars who converted to Christianity and was known for his generosity to the poor. When he refused to renounce Christ he was tortured and beheaded in the city of Bolghar in 1229; his relics were brought to Vladimir in 1230 and laid in the Dormition (Princess) Monastery.

name: St. Abraham of Kidunaja
title: Venerable
bio: A hermit near Edessa who left his wedding feast for the desert, and later went in disguise to an inn to bring his fallen niece St. Mary back to repentance.

name: St. Abraham of Rostov
title: Venerable, Monastic Founder
bio: A monk who, according to his Life, smashed an idol of Veles at Rostov with a staff given to him by St. John the Theologian, and founded the Monastery of the Theophany on the spot.

name: St. Abraham of Smolensk
title: Venerable
bio: A 12th–13th-century monk and priest of Smolensk, famed for his preaching, his study of the Scriptures and the Fathers, and his icon painting. Slandered and forbidden to serve by envious clergy, he was vindicated when his prayers ended a drought, and spent his last years leading a monastery in the city.

name: St. Abraham the Forefather
title: Righteous, Forefather
bio: Called by God from Ur of the Chaldees, he became through faith the father of many nations; he received the three angels at the Oak of Mamre — the image of the Holy Trinity in Orthodox iconography — and was ready to offer his son Isaac.

locations.label: Oak of Mamre and tomb — Hebron

name: St. Acacius of Mount Athos, New Martyr
title: Martyr
bio: A young Athonite monk who returned to Constantinople to confess Christ publicly and was martyred as a result.

name: St. Acacius of Sinai
title: Venerable
bio: A monk celebrated by St. John Climacus for his perfect obedience even after death.

name: St. Acacius the Centurion
title: Martyr
bio: A Cappadocian centurion who confessed Christ in Thrace under Maximian, was marched in chains to Byzantium and beheaded around 303; Constantine the Great later built a church over his relics.

name: St. Acepsimas of Persia
title: Hieromartyr
bio: A Persian bishop martyred at over one hundred years old during a wave of persecution under Shapur II.

name: St. Achilles of Larissa
title: Bishop
bio: Fourth-century bishop of Larissa renowned for his defense of Orthodoxy at the First Ecumenical Council.

name: St. Adalbert of Prague
title: Hieromartyr, Bishop
bio: Bishop of Prague who, meeting resistance to his reforms at home, became a missionary to the Hungarians, Poles and Prussians and was killed by pagan Prussians in 997; his relics were taken to Gniezno.

name: St. Adomnán of Iona
title: Abbot
bio: Ninth abbot of Iona and biographer of St. Columba, whose 'Law of the Innocents' (697) protected women, children and clergy from violence in war.

name: Sts. Adrian and Natalia
title: Martyrs
bio: Adrian, a pagan officer at Nicomedia, was so moved by the courage of tortured Christians that he declared himself one of them and was martyred; his wife Natalia encouraged him to the end and buried his relics near Byzantium.

name: St. Adrian of Poshekhonye
title: Monastic Founder and Martyr
bio: Founder of a monastery in the Poshekhonye forests who was martyred by robbers seeking the monastery's treasures.

name: St. Æthelwold of Winchester
title: Bishop
bio: Monk of Glastonbury, abbot of Abingdon and bishop of Winchester, a leader with St. Dunstan of the 10th-century monastic revival in England; he died in 984.

name: St. Afra of Augsburg
title: Martyr
bio: A woman of Augsburg in the province of Raetia who, according to tradition, had led a sinful life before her conversion to Christ. During the persecution of Diocletian (c. 304) she refused to sacrifice and was burned at the stake on an island in the river Lech; her grave became the site of the Basilica of Sts. Ulrich and Afra.

name: Apostle Agabus
title: Apostle of the Seventy, Prophet
bio: A prophet who foretold at Antioch the great famine under Claudius and at Caesarea bound his own hands and feet with St. Paul's belt to foretell the apostle's arrest in Jerusalem.

name: St. Agafia (Agatha) of Rome
title: Virgin Martyr
bio: A young noblewoman of Sicily martyred under Emperor Decius around 250 AD for refusing to renounce her Christian faith and her vow of virginity. She is venerated as the patron saint of Catania and of Sicily, and is invoked against fire and breast diseases.

name: Sts. Agape, Irene and Chionia
title: Virgin Martyrs
bio: Three sisters of Thessalonica who fled to the mountains with Christian books; Agape and Chionia were burned in 304, and Irene, who had hidden the books, was put to death soon after.

name: St. Agapetus of the Kiev Caves
title: Venerable, Unmercenary Physician
bio: A monk of the Kiev Caves who healed the sick with prayer and herbs from the monastery garden without payment, curing even Prince Vladimir Monomakh in the 11th century.

name: St. Agapius of Caesarea
title: Martyr
bio: A Palestinian martyr thrown to wild beasts at Caesarea after years of imprisonment during the Diocletianic persecution.

name: St. Agathangel of Yaroslavl, Confessor
title: Metropolitan and Confessor
bio: Metropolitan of Yaroslavl who endured Soviet imprisonment and exile while resisting schismatic pressures on the Church.

name: St. Agatho of Rome
title: Pope
bio: Bishop of Rome (678–681) whose dogmatic letter, confessing two wills in Christ, was received at the Sixth Ecumenical Council in Constantinople.

name: St. Agathonicus of Nicomedia
title: Martyr
bio: A Nicomedian nobleman martyred with his companions along the imperial road during the persecution of Maximian.

name: Sts. Agathopodes and Theodulus
title: Martyrs
bio: A deacon and a reader of Thessalonica who refused to surrender the Scriptures under Diocletian and were thrown into the sea with stones tied to their necks around 303.

name: St. Agnes of Rome
title: Virgin Martyr
bio: A young Roman girl martyred for her consecrated virginity, venerated as a model of purity and courage.

name: St. Agrippina of Rome
title: Virgin Martyr
bio: A young Roman noblewoman who dedicated herself to Christ and was beaten and tortured to death in the 3rd century. Three Christian women carried her relics to Sicily, where they rest at Mineo and became renowned for healings.

name: St. Aidan of Lindisfarne
title: Bishop, Enlightener of Northumbria
bio: Irish monk from Iona sent to found the monastery of Lindisfarne, from which he evangelized the kingdom of Northumbria with gentleness and simplicity of life.

name: St. Akakios of Kavsokalyvia
title: Venerable
bio: An 18th-century ascetic of the Kavsokalyvia skete on Mount Athos, famed for his severe asceticism and for the spiritual guidance he gave to New Martyrs, several of whom he prepared for martyrdom.

name: St. Akilina of Byblos
title: Virgin Martyr
bio: A twelve-year-old girl of Byblos in Phoenicia, baptized at five, who drew her friends to Christ; after cruel tortures she was condemned to be beheaded but gave up her spirit before the sword fell, around 293.

name: St. Akylina of Zagliveri
title: New Martyr
bio: A young girl of Zagliveri in Macedonia whose father had converted to Islam. When she steadfastly refused to do the same, she was cruelly flogged by order of the Ottoman authorities in Thessaloniki and died of her wounds in 1764, at about eighteen years of age.

name: St. Alban of Britain
title: Protomartyr of Britain
bio: The first recorded Christian martyr of Britain, executed for sheltering a persecuted priest and taking his place at the executioner's block.

name: St. Aldhelm of Sherborne
title: Bishop
bio: Abbot of Malmesbury and first bishop of Sherborne, a learned scholar and Latin poet who is said to have sung religious songs on a bridge to draw people to church; he died in 709.

name: St. Alexander Hotovitzky
title: Priest and Martyr
bio: A missionary priest of the American diocese who helped build Orthodox parishes before being martyred in Stalinist Russia.

name: St. Alexander Nevsky
title: Grand Prince, Righteous
bio: Prince of Novgorod and Grand Prince of Vladimir who defended Rus' from Swedish and Teutonic invasion while preserving peace with the Golden Horde, later taking monastic vows.

name: St. Alexander of Alexandria
title: Archbishop of Alexandria
bio: Archbishop of Alexandria who convened the local synod that first condemned Arianism, then led the Orthodox delegation to the First Ecumenical Council of Nicaea in 325 AD alongside his deacon Athanasios. He is venerated for his defense of the full divinity of Christ before it was formally defined.

name: St. Alexander of Constantinople
title: Patriarch
bio: Bishop of Byzantium who took part in the First Ecumenical Council at Nicaea; tradition holds that Arius died suddenly on the eve of his planned reinstatement after Alexander prayed all night in the Church of Holy Peace.

name: St. Alexander of Jerusalem
title: Hieromartyr, Bishop
bio: A bishop in Cappadocia who, after imprisonment for the faith, came to Jerusalem on pilgrimage around 212 and was made coadjutor to the aged bishop Narcissus. He founded a library in Jerusalem, befriended and ordained Origen, and died in prison at Caesarea during the persecution of Decius around 251.

name: St. Alexander of Svir
title: Venerable
bio: Northern Russian hermit and abbot, remembered for a vision of the Holy Trinity and for the monastery he founded near the river Svir.

name: St. Alexander of the Unsleeping Ones
title: Venerable, Monastic Founder
bio: A former officer who founded the community of the 'Akoimetoi' monks near Constantinople, organized into choirs so that the praise of God continued without ceasing day and night.

name: Sts. Alexander Peresvet and Andrew Oslyabya
title: Venerable, Warrior-Monks
bio: Monks of the Holy Trinity Monastery and former boyars of Bryansk, whom St. Sergius of Radonezh blessed to join Grand Prince Dmitry Donskoy against the Golden Horde. At the Battle of Kulikovo in 1380 Peresvet fell in single combat with the Tatar champion Chelubey, who died with him; Oslyabya also fought there, and both rest at the Old Simonov Monastery in Moscow.

locations.label: Monastic tonsure — Holy Trinity Lavra, Sergiev Posad

name: St. Alexander Schmorell of Munich
title: Martyr
bio: Born in Orenburg to a Russian Orthodox mother and German father, he grew up in Munich and co-founded the White Rose student resistance against the Nazi regime. Arrested in 1943 and beheaded at Stadelheim prison, he was glorified by the Russian Orthodox Church Outside Russia in 2012.

name: St. Alexander the Charcoal-Burner
title: Hieromartyr, Bishop
bio: A learned man who hid his gifts by working as a charcoal-burner at Comana until St. Gregory the Wonderworker discovered him and made him bishop of the city; he was burned for the faith under Decius around 251.

locations.label: Episcopal see and martyrdom — Comana Pontica

name: St. Alexios, Man of God
title: Venerable
bio: Born to a noble Roman family, Alexios fled his arranged marriage on his wedding night, lived as a beggar in Edessa for seventeen years, then returned to Rome and lived unknown under the staircase of his own family's house until his death. He is a celebrated model of radical humility and voluntary poverty.

locations.label: Seventeen years as a beggar — Edessa (Sanlıurfa)

name: St. Alexis Mechev
title: Righteous, Priest
bio: A Moscow parish priest of the Church of St. Nicholas on Maroseyka who, after his wife's death, devoted himself to consoling the suffering and became one of the city's most beloved confessors; he died in 1923.

locations.label: Church of St. Nicholas on Maroseyka — Moscow

name: St. Alexis of Moscow
title: Metropolitan
bio: Metropolitan of Moscow who served as regent for the young Prince Dmitri Donskoi and healed the Tatar khan's mother.

name: St. Alexis Toth
title: Confessor
bio: A priest who led the return of many Carpatho-Rusyn parishes in America to Orthodoxy, called the 'Father of the Orthodox Church in America.'

name: St. Alphege of Canterbury
title: Hieromartyr, Archbishop
bio: Monk of Deerhurst and Bath, later Bishop of Winchester and Archbishop of Canterbury. Captured by Danish raiders in 1011, he refused to let his impoverished people pay a ransom for him and was killed by his captors at Greenwich in 1012.

name: St. Alypius the Iconographer
title: Venerable
bio: The first known iconographer of Rus', a monk of the Kiev Caves who learned from the Greek masters decorating the Dormition church and painted icons without payment; tradition says angels completed an icon for him when he fell ill.

name: St. Alypius the Stylite
title: Venerable
bio: Paphlagonian ascetic who lived on a pillar for over half a century, with monastic communities of both men and women gathered at its foot.

name: St. Amand of Maastricht
title: Bishop, Missionary
bio: Born near Nantes around 584, he lived as a monk and recluse before being consecrated a missionary bishop. He preached tirelessly among the pagans of Flanders, founded many monasteries including Elnone (Saint-Amand-les-Eaux), briefly held the see of Maastricht, and died around 675.

name: St. Ambrose of Milan
title: Bishop of Milan
bio: Governor of Milan unexpectedly acclaimed as its bishop by the people in 374 AD while still a catechumen. He became one of the great Latin Fathers, championed orthodoxy against Arianism, penned celebrated hymns still sung today, and boldly confronted the Emperor Theodosius over the Massacre of Thessalonica.

name: St. Ambrose of Optina
title: Venerable
bio: A renowned elder of Optina Hermitage who counseled thousands, including Dostoevsky, with humor and spiritual insight.

name: St. Ambrosios of Moschonisia, Metropolitan and Martyr
title: Metropolitan and Martyr
bio: A Greek metropolitan of the Moschonisia islands martyred in the anti-Christian violence following World War I.

name: Holy Prophet Amos
title: Prophet
bio: A herdsman and dresser of sycamore figs from Tekoa, sent to the northern kingdom of Israel to denounce injustice to the poor and empty worship at Bethel.

name: St. Amoun of Nitria
title: Venerable, Monastic Founder
bio: Married against his will, he persuaded his wife to live with him in virginity for eighteen years, then withdrew around 330 to found the monastic settlement of Nitria; he was a friend of St. Anthony.

name: St. Amphilochios of Patmos
title: Venerable
bio: Abbot of the Monastery of St. John on Patmos, known for his love of nature and gift of spiritual counsel.

name: St. Amphilochius of Iconium
title: Bishop of Iconium
bio: Close friend of St. Basil the Great and St. Gregory the Theologian, he served as Bishop of Iconium and was a staunch defender of Trinitarian orthodoxy at the Second Ecumenical Council.

name: St. Amphilochius of Pochaev
title: Venerable, Elder
bio: A monk of the Pochaev Lavra who healed many with herbs and prayer and was confined in a psychiatric hospital under Soviet rule; he died in 1971 and was glorified in 2002.

name: St. Amphilochius' Sister Theosebia
title: Righteous
bio: Sister of St. Amphilochius of Iconium, remembered in the Cappadocian circle of ascetic and pastoral saints.

name: Apostle Ananias of Damascus
title: Apostle of the Seventy, Bishop of Damascus
bio: Disciple at Damascus sent by the Lord to restore the sight of Saul and baptize him; he later preached in Syria and was stoned to death at Eleutheropolis.

name: St. Anastasia of Serbia
title: Venerable
bio: Ana, wife of Grand Župan Stefan Nemanja and mother of St. Sava. When Nemanja became the monk Simeon in 1196 she too took the monastic habit as Anastasia, living at the Monastery of the Theotokos in Toplica; she died around 1200 and was buried at Studenica beside her husband's tomb.

locations.label: Nun — Monastery of the Theotokos, Kuršumlija

name: St. Anastasia the Great Martyr
title: Great Martyr, Deliverer from Potions
bio: A Roman noblewoman who used her wealth to minister to Christians imprisoned under Emperor Diocletian, traveling from prison to prison to care for confessors. She was martyred in Sirmium around 304 AD and is venerated across the Orthodox world with the epithet “Deliverer from Potions” for her healing intercessions.

name: St. Anastasia the Patrician
title: Ascetic of Scetis
bio: A noblewoman of the imperial court of Constantinople who fled worldly honors, settled near Alexandria, and later lived disguised as a monk in the desert of Scetis.

name: St. Anastasia the Roman
title: Venerable Martyr
bio: An orphan raised in a convent near Rome by the abbess Sophia, she was arrested as a young nun under Decius and, refusing to deny Christ, was cruelly tortured and beheaded around 250.

name: St. Anastasios of Nafplio, New Martyr
title: New Martyr
bio: A young painter of Nafplio who, during a period of mental derangement, was made a Muslim by the Ottoman authorities. When he recovered his reason he openly declared that he was a Christian and refused both flattery and threats before the judge; he was tortured and put to death in 1655 and is the patron saint of Nafplio.

name: St. Anastasios of Naupaktos
title: Bishop
bio: A modern Greek bishop of Naupaktos remembered for pastoral care and defense of the faith amid social upheaval.

name: St. Anastasius of Sinai
title: Venerable
bio: A 7th-century monk and abbot of the monastery on Mount Sinai who defended Orthodox Christology against the Monophysites. His works include the Hodegos ("Guide"), a handbook against heresy, and collections of edifying tales of the desert fathers.

locations.label: Monastery of St. Catherine — Mount Sinai

name: St. Anastasius the Persian
title: Venerable Martyr
bio: A former Persian soldier who converted to Christianity, became a monk, and was martyred for destroying idols.

locations.label: Place of martyrdom — near Caesarea, Palestine

name: St. Anatolius of Constantinople
title: Patriarch
bio: Patriarch of Constantinople at the time of the Fourth Ecumenical Council at Chalcedon in 451, which confessed Christ as one Person in two natures; hymns attributed to him are still sung in the Octoechos.

name: St. Anatoly of Optina
title: Venerable, Elder
bio: Optina Elder celebrated for his humility, comforting counsel, and care for the many pilgrims and monastics who sought his guidance.

name: St. Anatoly the Younger of Optina
title: Elder
bio: The last of the great Optina elders before the monastery's closure, who died shortly after being forced from his cell.

name: St. Andrei Șaguna
title: Metropolitan
bio: Born in Miskolc to an Aromanian family, he became Orthodox bishop of Transylvania in 1848 and restored the Metropolis of Transylvania in 1864. He founded hundreds of schools, a seminary and a printing press at Sibiu and championed the rights of the Romanian people; he reposed in 1873 and was glorified by the Romanian Church in 2011.

name: St. Andrew Bogolyubsky
title: Prince and Martyr
bio: Grand Prince of Vladimir who brought the Vladimir Icon of the Theotokos from Kiev, built the Dormition Cathedral and the Church of the Intercession on the Nerl, and was murdered by conspirators at Bogolyubovo in 1174.

name: St. Andrew in Krisis
title: Venerable Martyr
bio: A Cretan monk who travelled to Constantinople to rebuke Emperor Constantine V for persecuting the holy icons; he was scourged and dragged through the streets, dying in 767 in the quarter of Krisis, where his relics were kept.

name: St. Andrew of Crete
title: Archbishop
bio: Archbishop of Crete and hymnographer, best known for composing the Great Canon of Repentance.

name: St. Andrew Rublev
title: Venerable, Iconographer
bio: Russian monk and the greatest medieval icon painter of Russia, best known for his icon of the Holy Trinity, painted in honor of St. Sergius of Radonezh.

name: St. Andrew Stratelates
title: Great Martyr
bio: A Roman military commander in Syria under Emperor Maximian (c. 300) who led his outnumbered soldiers to victory over the Persians after calling on Christ, and was then baptized with them by Bishop Peter of Tarsus. Denounced as Christians, Andrew and his 2,593 soldiers were beheaded in a gorge of the Taurus mountains in Cilicia.

name: Apostle Andrew the First-Called
title: Apostle
bio: Brother of Peter and the first disciple called by Christ, later crucified on an X-shaped cross in Patras.

name: St. Andrew the Fool-for-Christ
title: Fool-for-Christ
bio: A Constantinopolitan slave who feigned madness for Christ's sake and witnessed the vision of the Theotokos's veil.

name: Sts. Andronicus and Junia
title: Apostles of the Seventy
bio: Kinsfolk and fellow prisoners of St. Paul, whom he greeted as 'of note among the apostles'; they preached in Pannonia and beyond, and their relics were later found in Constantinople.

name: St. Andronicus of Moscow
title: Venerable, Abbot
bio: A disciple of St. Sergius of Radonezh from his youth, he was chosen by Metropolitan Alexis around 1357 to be the first abbot of the Monastery of the Saviour on the Yauza in Moscow. The monastery, later named Andronikov after him, became a centre of icon painting where St. Andrew Rublev lived; he died around 1395.

name: St. Andronik of Perm, Hieromartyr
title: Archbishop and Martyr
bio: Archbishop of Perm and former missionary to Japan, buried alive by Bolshevik forces in 1918.

name: Sts. Andronikos and Athanasia
title: Venerable
bio: A married couple of Antioch who, after the death of their two children, mutually agreed to live in consecrated celibacy. Andronikos became a monk in Egypt; Athanasia, unknown to him, also became a monk disguised as a man. They met again years later, and Andronikos only discovered her identity after her death.

name: St. Angelina of Serbia
title: Righteous
bio: Wife of the blind, exiled Despot Stefan Branković, whom she cared for through years of exile in Albania and Italy; widowed, she settled in Srem, became a nun and with her son St. Maksim founded the Krušedol Monastery.

name: Sts. Angelis, Manuel and Companions of Chios
title: Martyrs
bio: A group of Chian laymen martyred together for their steadfast confession of the Orthodox faith under Ottoman rule.

name: St. Angelis, New Martyr of Constantinople
title: Martyr
bio: A young Constantinopolitan martyred for reclaiming his Christian identity after a coerced conversion in his youth.

name: St. Anianus of Orléans
title: Bishop
bio: Bishop of Orléans who in 451 sustained the besieged city against Attila and the Huns with prayer and encouragement until the Roman general Aetius arrived to relieve it. He reposed around 453 and is venerated as the city's protector (Saint Aignan).

locations.label: Episcopal see and siege of 451 — Orléans

name: Sts. Anicetus and Photius
title: Martyrs
bio: An uncle and nephew martyred together at Nicomedia after Photius overturned an idol during a pagan festival.

name: St. Anna of Kashin
title: Righteous, Princess
bio: Wife of St. Michael of Tver, who was martyred in the Golden Horde, and mother of princes also killed by the Horde; she became a nun in Tver and Kashin, and her veneration, once suspended, was later restored.

name: St. Anna of Novgorod
title: Righteous, Princess
bio: Ingegerd, daughter of King Olof of Sweden, wife of Yaroslav the Wise and mother of St. Vladimir of Novgorod; she ended her life as the nun Anna and is buried in the St. Sophia Cathedral of Novgorod.

name: St. Anna of Thessaloniki, Mother of Theodora
title: Righteous
bio: Mother of St. Theodora of Thessaloniki, remembered for raising her daughter in devout monastic piety.

name: St. Anna the New Martyr of Cappadocia
title: New Martyr
bio: A young Cappadocian woman martyred by Ottoman authorities for refusing to abandon her Christian faith.

name: St. Anna the Prophetess
title: Righteous, Prophetess
bio: Elderly widow who served God with fasting and prayer in the Temple and, present at the Presentation of Christ, recognized and proclaimed Him as the Messiah.

name: St. Ansgar of Hamburg
title: Bishop, Missionary
bio: A monk of Corbie who preached in Denmark and built the first church in Sweden at Birka; as Archbishop of Hamburg-Bremen he became known as the Apostle of the North, dying in 865.

name: St. Anthimos of Chios
title: Venerable
bio: Simple Chian monk and confessor of souls who founded a convent on the island and was widely sought for healing prayer.

name: St. Anthimus of Nicomedia
title: Hieromartyr
bio: Bishop of Nicomedia martyred during Diocletian's persecution after refusing to abandon his flock.

name: St. Anthony Kauleas
title: Patriarch
bio: Raised in a monastery from the age of twelve, he became Patriarch of Constantinople in 893. He devoted his patriarchate to ending the long division between the followers of Patriarchs Photios and Ignatios, reconciling the Ignatian party around 899, and was loved for his care for the poor and for monastics. He reposed in 901.

name: St. Anthony of Optina
title: Elder
bio: Brother of St. Moses of Optina, a monk celebrated for cheerful endurance of chronic illness and pastoral warmth.

name: St. Anthony of the Kiev Caves
title: Venerable
bio: Founder of the Kiev Caves Lavra, bringing the monastic tradition of Mount Athos to the Rus' lands.

name: St. Anthony the Great
title: Venerable, Father of Monasticism
bio: Born to a wealthy family in Egypt, he sold his possessions to follow Christ's call to the poor and withdrew into the desert, becoming the leader of the Desert Fathers and the model for all later Christian monasticism.

locations.label: Monastery and relics — Eastern Desert, Egypt

name: St. Anthony the Roman
title: Venerable, Monastic Founder
bio: Born in Rome to Orthodox parents, he became a hermit by the sea and, according to his Life, was carried on a rock to Novgorod in 1106, where he founded the Monastery of the Nativity of the Theotokos.

name: Sts. Anthony, John and Eustathius of Vilnius
title: Martyrs
bio: Three courtiers of Grand Duke Algirdas of Lithuania who refused to renounce the Orthodox faith and were hanged on an oak in Vilnius in 1347; their relics rest in the city's Monastery of the Holy Spirit.

locations.label: Relics — Monastery of the Holy Spirit, Vilnius

name: St. Antim Ivireanul
title: Metropolitan of Wallachia, Hieromartyr
bio: Georgian-born printer, preacher and metropolitan who gave Wallachia liturgical books in Romanian and was killed on the way to exile.

name: St. Antipa of Pergamon
title: Hieromartyr, Bishop
bio: Bishop of Pergamon in Asia Minor, mentioned in the Book of Revelation (2:13) as “my faithful witness who was killed among you.” He was martyred under Emperor Domitian, traditionally by being cast into a red-hot bronze bull used for pagan sacrifices. He is invoked for toothaches.

name: St. Antony of Siya
title: Venerable, Monastic Founder
bio: A northern Russian peasant who became a monk after the death of his wife and founded the Antoniev-Siysky Monastery near Arkhangelsk in 1520.

name: St. Anysia of Thessaloniki
title: Martyr
bio: Young Thessalonian woman who gave away her inheritance to the poor and was killed by a soldier for refusing to sacrifice to idols.

name: St. Aphrahat of Antioch
title: Venerable
bio: A Persian of noble birth who became an ascetic at Antioch and, though living in a small cell, boldly defended the Orthodox faith before the Arian emperor Valens.

name: St. Apollinaris of Ravenna
title: Hieromartyr, Bishop
bio: Traditionally a disciple of St. Peter the Apostle, he became the first bishop of Ravenna and was martyred after several exiles for refusing to offer sacrifice to pagan gods. The magnificent Byzantine basilicas of Sant’Apollinare in Classe and Sant’Apollinare Nuovo in Ravenna are dedicated to him.

name: Apostle Apollos
title: Apostle of the Seventy
bio: An eloquent Alexandrian Jew, 'mighty in the Scriptures', who was taught the way of God more fully by Aquila and Priscilla at Ephesus and then watered in Corinth what St. Paul had planted.

name: Sts. Aquila and Priscilla
title: Apostles
bio: Jewish Christian tentmakers mentioned repeatedly in the New Testament as close companions of St. Paul the Apostle, who worked alongside him in Corinth and Ephesus. They hosted a church in their home and personally instructed the eloquent Apollos in the Christian faith.

name: St. Archil II of Kakheti
title: King and Martyr
bio: An eighth-century Georgian king martyred by Arab invaders for refusing to renounce Christianity and embrace Islam.

name: St. Arethas of Najran
title: Great Martyr
bio: The aged chieftain of the Christian city of Najran in southern Arabia. When the Himyarite king Dhu Nuwas captured the city around 523, Arethas refused to deny Christ and was beheaded together with many hundreds of the city's Christians, men, women and children.

name: St. Argyra of Constantinople
title: New Martyr
bio: A young married woman imprisoned unjustly and martyred in Constantinople for refusing to convert to Islam.

name: St. Ariadne of Phrygia
title: Martyr
bio: A Christian slave in Prymnessus in Phrygia who refused to take part in pagan festivities and fled her master's persecution; according to her Life, a rock opened to shelter her and became her tomb.

name: St. Aristarchus of Apamea
title: Apostle of the Seventy
bio: One of the Seventy Apostles and a companion of St. Paul, he was ordained bishop of Apamea in Syria and labored there until his repose.

name: St. Aristides of Athens
title: Philosopher, Apologist
bio: An Athenian philosopher who became a Christian and around 125 presented to Emperor Hadrian one of the earliest surviving defences of the faith. His Apology contrasts the worship of the one true God with the errors of the pagans and praises the pure life of the Christians.

name: Apostle Aristobulus of Britain
title: Apostle of the Seventy, Bishop of Britain
bio: Greeted by St. Paul in his Epistle to the Romans, he was, according to Byzantine tradition, ordained bishop by St. Barnabas and sent to preach in Britain, where he reposed.

name: St. Arsenije I of Serbia
title: Archbishop
bio: Second Archbishop of the Serbian Church who continued St. Sava's work strengthening Serbian Orthodoxy.

name: St. Arsenios of Cappadocia
title: Priest-Confessor, Wonderworker
bio: Beloved priest of Farasa, Cappadocia, known for his ascetic life and miracles; he baptized and blessed St. Paisios of Mount Athos as an infant.

name: St. Arsenios of Kerkyra
title: Archbishop
bio: A monk born in Bethany who became archbishop of Corfu in the 10th century and was loved for his care of prisoners and the poor.

name: St. Arsenios of Paros
title: Venerable
bio: A monk and spiritual father on the island of Paros known for his gift of foresight and healing.

name: St. Arsenios the Great
title: Venerable, Desert Father
bio: A highly educated Roman deacon who served as tutor to the imperial princes Arcadius and Honorius in Constantinople, then at the age of forty renounced everything and became a monk in the Egyptian desert. He is remembered for his maxim: “I have often repented of having spoken, but never of having been silent.”

name: St. Arsenius (Matseevich) of Rostov
title: Hieromartyr, Metropolitan
bio: Metropolitan of Rostov who in 1763 protested against the confiscation of monastic and church lands by Empress Catherine II. Deposed, defrocked and imprisoned under the name "Andrew the Liar," he died in a cell of the fortress of Reval (Tallinn) in 1772; the Russian Church glorified him as a hieromartyr in 2000.

name: St. Arsenius (Zhadanovsky) of Serpukhov
title: Bishop and Confessor
bio: A Russian bishop and diarist who survived Soviet imprisonment and continued clandestine ministry in hiding.

name: St. Arsenius of Konevits
title: Monastic Founder
bio: A monk of Mount Athos who founded a monastery on Konevits Island in Lake Ladoga after receiving an icon of the Theotokos.

name: St. Arsenius of Tver
title: Bishop
bio: A monk of the Kiev Caves who became bishop of Tver in 1390. He built churches, cared for the poor and founded the Zheltikov Monastery of the Dormition near the city, where he retired and was buried after his death in 1409.

name: Apostle Artemas
title: Apostle of the Seventy
bio: A trusted co-worker of the Apostle Paul, who planned to send him to Titus in Crete (Titus 3:12). Tradition counts him among the Seventy and makes him bishop of Lystra in Lycaonia, the city where Paul had once been stoned and where Timothy was born.

name: St. Artemios of Antioch
title: Great Martyr
bio: A Roman general martyred under Emperor Julian the Apostate for protesting the persecution of Christians.

name: St. Artemius of Verkola
title: Righteous
bio: A devout twelve-year-old boy of Verkola on the Pinega River who was killed by lightning in 1545; his body was found incorrupt decades later and many healings followed.

name: St. Asaph
title: Bishop, Abbot
bio: A 6th-century disciple of St. Kentigern at the monastery of Llanelwy in north Wales, known for his holiness even as a boy. He succeeded Kentigern as abbot and bishop, and the cathedral city of St Asaph bears his name.

name: St. Athanasia of Aegina
title: Abbess of Aegina
bio: A ninth-century abbess of Aegina who founded a monastery and became known for her charity to the poor and her gift of prophecy.

name: St. Athanasios Diakos
title: Deacon and Martyr
bio: A deacon-turned-fighter of the Greek War of Independence, impaled by Ottoman forces after the Battle of Alamana.

name: St. Athanasios of Athos
title: Venerable
bio: Founder of the Great Lavra, the oldest and most prestigious monastery on Mount Athos, established in 963 AD with the patronage of Emperor Nikephoros Phokas. He organized cenobitic monastic life on the Holy Mountain and shaped Athonite monasticism for centuries to come.

locations.label: Foundation of the Great Lavra — Mount Athos

name: St. Athanasios of Meteora
title: Venerable
bio: Born in Hypati in 1305, he became a monk on Mount Athos before settling on the rock pillars of Meteora in Thessaly, where he founded the Great Meteoron Monastery of the Transfiguration and gave the monastic community its rule. He reposed around 1380.

name: St. Athanasios Parios
title: Venerable
bio: Teacher and theologian of the Kollyvades movement who taught for many years at the school of Chios during the Ottoman period.

name: St. Athanasios the Great
title: Archbishop of Alexandria
bio: Archbishop of Alexandria who championed Nicene orthodoxy against Arianism throughout his life, enduring five exiles at the hands of Arian emperors. His phrase “Athanasios contra mundum” captures his solitary defense of the full divinity of Christ.

locations.label: Birthplace, episcopal see, and relics — Alexandria
Exile and support of the Western Church — Rome

name: St. Athanasius I of Constantinople
title: Patriarch
bio: A strict monk born in Adrianople who served twice as Patriarch of Constantinople (1289–1293 and 1303–1309), reforming the clergy and organizing relief for the poor and refugees of the capital.

name: St. Athanasius of Brest
title: Hieromartyr
bio: Hegumen of the Monastery of St. Simeon in Brest who tirelessly defended Orthodoxy against the Union of Brest in the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth. Repeatedly imprisoned for his stand, he was tortured and executed by Polish authorities in 1648.

name: St. Athenogenes of Sebaste
title: Hieromartyr, Bishop
bio: Bishop near Sebaste in Armenia martyred with ten disciples under Diocletian; St. Basil the Great records that he left the Church a hymn as he went to the fire, sometimes identified with 'O Gladsome Light'.

name: St. Augustine of Canterbury
title: Apostle to the English, first Archbishop of Canterbury
bio: Roman monk sent by Pope Gregory the Dialogist to evangelize the Anglo-Saxons, becoming the first Archbishop of Canterbury.

name: St. Augustine of Hippo
title: Bishop of Hippo
bio: North African bishop and prolific theologian, author of the Confessions, whose writings shaped Western Christian thought.

locations.label: See and place of death — Hippo Regius (Annaba, Algeria)

name: St. Auxentios of Bithynia
title: Hermit of Bithynia
bio: A Syrian-born officer of the imperial guard who withdrew to a mountain in Bithynia to live as a hermit, later called Mount Auxentios in his honor.

name: St. Auxentius of Sebaste
title: Martyr
bio: One of the martyrs of Sebaste who suffered with Eustratius, Auxentius, Eugenius, Mardarius and Orestes.

name: St. Auxibius of Soli
title: Bishop
bio: A convert of the Apostles Barnabas and Mark who became the first bishop of Soli in Cyprus.

name: St. Babylas of Antioch
title: Hieromartyr
bio: Bishop of Antioch who barred an emperor from entering the church for shedding innocent blood and was martyred.

name: St. Barbara the Great Martyr
title: Great Martyr
bio: Daughter of a wealthy pagan of Nicomedia who was locked in a tower by her father to keep her from suitors, she secretly embraced Christianity and had a third window added to her bathhouse in honor of the Trinity. She was tortured and beheaded by her own father after refusing to renounce her faith.

name: St. Barbara the Martyred Nun of Moscow
title: Nun and Martyr
bio: A cell-attendant of the Grand Duchess Elizabeth who chose to share her martyrdom rather than abandon her at Alapayevsk.

name: St. Barbarus the Myrrh-streaming
title: Venerable
bio: A repentant former bandit who lived the rest of his life in prayer and penance, his relics later streaming myrrh.

name: Sts. Barlaam and Josaphat
title: Ascetics
bio: A monk and the Indian prince he converted to Christianity, whose legendary story of renunciation and asceticism became one of the most popular tales of the medieval Christian world.

name: St. Barlaam of Antioch
title: Martyr
bio: An elderly countryman of Antioch who, forced to hold incense and burning coals over a pagan altar, let his hand burn away rather than drop the incense as an offering; Sts. Basil the Great and John Chrysostom preached his praises.

name: Apostle Barnabas
title: Apostle of the Seventy
bio: A Cypriot Levite and close companion of the Apostle Paul on his early missionary journeys, and the first bishop of Cyprus, martyred at Salamis.

name: Sts. Barnabas and Sophronius of Sumela
title: Venerable, Monastic Founders
bio: Two monks of Athens who, guided by the Theotokos in the late 4th century, brought an icon of her attributed to the Apostle Luke to Mount Mela in Pontus. In a cave in its cliff face they founded the Monastery of Panagia Soumela, for centuries a spiritual centre of Pontic Hellenism.

name: St. Barnabas of Gethsemane
title: Monk
bio: A Russian monk-elder of the Gethsemane Skete near the Trinity-Sergius Lavra known for spiritual counsel to pilgrims.

name: St. Barsanuphius of Kazan
title: Bishop
bio: A former captive among the Tatars who became bishop of Tver, celebrated for his missionary compassion.

name: St. Barsanuphius of Optina
title: Venerable, Elder
bio: One of the renowned Optina Elders, a former military officer who became a monk and spiritual father noted for his gift of discernment and pastoral wisdom.

name: St. Barsanuphius the Great of Gaza
title: Ascetic
bio: A sixth-century recluse of Gaza whose spiritual correspondence with St. John the Prophet forms a classic of Orthodox ascetic literature.

name: Apostle Bartholomew
title: Apostle
bio: One of the Twelve Apostles who preached in Armenia, where he was martyred by flaying.

name: St. Bartholomew of Grottaferrata
title: Venerable, Abbot, Hymnographer
bio: A Greek monk born at Rossano in Calabria who became the beloved disciple of St. Nilus. As abbot of Grottaferrata near Rome he completed its church, wrote the Life of St. Nilus and many hymns, and kept the Byzantine rite alive there; he died around 1055.

name: Holy Prophet Baruch
title: Prophet
bio: Scribe and faithful disciple of the Prophet Jeremiah, who wrote down the prophet's words at his dictation and read the scroll aloud in the Temple. He shared Jeremiah's sufferings during the fall of Jerusalem, and the Book of Baruch, read in the Orthodox Old Testament, bears his name.

name: St. Basil of Amasea
title: Hieromartyr, Bishop
bio: Bishop of Amasea in Pontus who sheltered Glaphyra, a Christian serving woman fleeing the Emperor Licinius; for this he was beheaded and thrown into the sea around 322, and his body was recovered at Sinope.

name: St. Basil of Ancyra
title: Hieromartyr, Presbyter
bio: A presbyter of Ancyra who opposed both the Arians and the paganism revived by Emperor Julian the Apostate. Arrested and repeatedly tortured for confessing Christ, he was martyred in 362.

name: St. Basil of Mangazeya
title: Righteous Martyr
bio: A young Siberian merchant's assistant falsely accused and martyred, later glorified as protector of the Mangazeya region.

name: St. Basil of Ostrog
title: Bishop, Wonderworker
bio: Bishop of Herzegovina who withdrew to the cliffs of Ostrog; his relics there remain one of the most visited pilgrimage sites in the Balkans.

name: St. Basil of Parium
title: Bishop and Confessor
bio: Bishop of Parium on the Hellespont in the 8th century, who refused to sign the iconoclast decrees of Emperor Leo III. Driven from his see, he endured persecution and wandering for the sake of the holy icons and died in peace.

name: St. Basil of Poiana Mărului
title: Hesychast Elder
bio: A Moldavian hesychast elder who revived Athonite spiritual traditions and mentored St. Paisius Velichkovsky.

name: St. Basil the Blessed, Fool-for-Christ
title: Fool-for-Christ
bio: A Moscow holy fool who fearlessly rebuked Ivan the Terrible, giving his name to the famous cathedral on Red Square.

name: St. Basil the Elder and St. Emmelia
title: Righteous
bio: The parents of St. Basil the Great, St. Gregory of Nyssa, and St. Macrina, who together raised a remarkable family of saints in Cappadocia.

name: St. Basil the Great
title: Archbishop of Caesarea, one of the Three Holy Hierarchs
bio: Bishop of Caesarea in Cappadocia and a leading 4th-century theologian, he defended Orthodoxy against Arianism and founded the Basiliad, a combined poorhouse, hospital, and hostel for the destitute outside his city.

locations.label: Birthplace, episcopal see, and death — Caesarea, Cappadocia

name: St. Basil the Younger
title: Venerable
bio: A 10th-century ascetic of Constantinople who was first seized as a suspected spy and tortured before being released. Living among the people of the capital, he became famous for clairvoyance and wonders; through him his disciple Gregory learned of the vision of the soul's passage after death granted to Basil's servant Theodora. He reposed around 944.

name: St. Basiliscus of Comana
title: Martyr
bio: A soldier martyred at Comana, buried near the same place where St. John Chrysostom later reposed.

name: St. Basiliscus' Companion Eutropius
title: Martyr
bio: A companion martyr venerated with Sts. Eutropius and Cleonicus of Comana Pontica under Emperor Maximian.

name: St. Bathild of Chelles
title: Venerable, Queen
bio: An Anglo-Saxon slave girl who became queen of the Franks as wife of Clovis II, worked to end the slave trade and founded the abbeys of Chelles and Corbie, retiring to Chelles as a nun.

name: St. Bavo of Ghent
title: Venerable, Hermit
bio: A nobleman of Hesbaye who led a dissolute life until the death of his wife moved him to repentance under the guidance of St. Amand. He gave away his wealth, became a monk at Ghent and spent his last years as a hermit, dying around 659; Ghent's cathedral bears his name.

name: St. Beatus of Beatenberg
title: Venerable, Hermit
bio: Revered as an early apostle of Switzerland, a hermit who according to legend drove a dragon out of a cave above Lake Thun and lived there in prayer. The Beatus Caves, where pilgrims visited his tomb throughout the Middle Ages, still bear his name.

locations.label: Hermitage and tomb — St. Beatus Caves, Lake Thun

name: St. Bede the Venerable
title: Venerable
bio: Monk of Jarrow and historian of the English Church, whose learning earned him the title of the last of the Latin Fathers.

name: St. Bega of St Bees
title: Venerable, Anchoress
bio: According to tradition an Irish princess who fled an arranged marriage and crossed the sea to the coast of Cumbria in the 7th century. She lived there as an anchoress, and the priory and village of St Bees grew up around the place of her hermitage.

name: St. Benedict Biscop
title: Abbot
bio: A Northumbrian nobleman who founded the twin monasteries of Wearmouth and Jarrow, furnishing them with books and icons brought from Rome; he was the teacher of St. Bede.

name: St. Benedict of Aniane
title: Venerable, Abbot
bio: A Visigothic noble who served at the court of Charlemagne before becoming a monk and founding the monastery of Aniane in Languedoc in 782. Under Louis the Pious he led the reform of monastic life throughout the Frankish realm, and died in 821 at the monastery of Inden near Aachen.

locations.label: Monastery and repose — Inden (Kornelimünster), near Aachen

name: St. Benedict of Nursia
title: Abbot, Father of Western Monasticism
bio: Italian abbot whose monastic Rule shaped Western monasticism, founding the community at Monte Cassino.

name: St. Benjamin of Irkutsk, Apostle of Alaska
title: Missionary Bishop
bio: A nineteenth-century missionary bishop who evangelized the Aleutian Islands and coastal Alaska with tireless zeal.

name: St. Benjamin of Petrograd
title: Metropolitan and Martyr
bio: Metropolitan of Petrograd executed by Soviet authorities in 1922 following a show trial over church valuables.

name: St. Bernice (Veronica)
title: Righteous
bio: Venerated in tradition as the woman healed of a hemorrhage by touching Christ's garment.

name: St. Bessarion of Larissa
title: Archbishop
bio: Archbishop of Larissa in the 16th century who built bridges, schools and churches in Thessaly and founded the Dousiko Monastery near Trikala, where he rests.

locations.label: Monastery and relics — Dousiko, near Trikala

name: St. Bessarion the Wonderworker
title: Venerable, Wonderworker
bio: A disciple of Sts. Anthony and Macarius who owned nothing, slept standing and wandered the deserts of Egypt; among his recorded wonders, he made sea water sweet for a thirsting disciple.

name: St. Beuno of Clynnog
title: Abbot
bio: A 7th-century Welsh abbot who founded the monastery of Clynnog Fawr on the Llŷn Peninsula and, according to tradition, restored his niece St. Winifred to life.

name: St. Birinus of Dorchester
title: Bishop, Apostle of the West Saxons
bio: Missionary bishop sent from Rome who converted the West Saxons, baptized King Cynegils in 635 and founded his see at Dorchester-on-Thames.

name: St. Blaise of Sebaste
title: Hieromartyr
bio: Bishop of Sebaste in Armenia and a physician who was said to heal both people and wild animals, he withdrew to a cave during a persecution where he continued his healing ministry. He was arrested, tortured with iron combs, and beheaded, and is invoked to this day against ailments of the throat.

name: St. Boniface of Mainz
title: Archbishop of Mainz, Apostle of Germany
bio: English missionary known as the Apostle of Germany, who organized the Church among the Germanic peoples and was martyred while evangelizing in Frisia.

name: St. Boniface of Tarsus
title: Martyr
bio: A Roman servant of dissolute life who was sent by his mistress Aglaida to collect the relics of martyrs in the East, he was so moved by witnessing their courage under torture in Tarsus that he confessed Christ himself and was executed. His own relics were then brought back to Rome by the astonished servants who had accompanied him.

name: Sts. Boris and Gleb
title: Passion-Bearers, Princes
bio: Sons of St. Vladimir of Kiev, princes who accepted death without resistance rather than take up arms against their brother, becoming Russia's first canonized saints.

locations.label: Martyrdom of St. Gleb — near Smolensk

name: St. Boris-Michael of Bulgaria
title: Equal-to-the-Apostles, Prince
bio: Khan of Bulgaria who was baptized in 864 taking the name Michael, made Christianity the faith of his people, welcomed the disciples of Sts. Cyril and Methodius, and ended his life as a monk.

name: St. Botolph of Iken
title: Venerable, Abbot
bio: A 7th-century abbot who founded a monastery at Icanho, probably Iken in Suffolk; many English churches by town gates, and the town of Boston ('Botolph's town'), bear his name.

name: St. Brendan the Navigator
title: Abbot
bio: Irish abbot of Clonfert, famed for founding monasteries and for the legendary seven-year sea voyage in search of the Isle of the Blessed.

name: St. Bretanion of Tomis
title: Bishop and Confessor
bio: Bishop of Tomis on the Black Sea, chief city of Scythia Minor, in the 4th century. When the Arian Emperor Valens came to the city around 369, Bretanion refused communion with him and led his flock to another church; Valens exiled him but soon had to allow his return for fear of the faithful.

name: St. Brigid of Kildare
title: Abbess of Kildare
bio: One of Ireland's most beloved saints, founder of the monastery at Kildare and renowned for her charity toward the poor.

name: St. Brynach of Nevern
title: Venerable
bio: A 5th–6th-century hermit of Irish birth in Pembrokeshire, friend of St. David, who founded the church at Nevern. He is said to have conversed with angels on Carn Ingli, the "mount of angels" above the village, and his churchyard keeps one of the finest early Christian crosses in Wales.

name: St. Bucolus of Smyrna
title: Bishop
bio: A disciple of the Apostle John the Theologian, who made him the first bishop of Smyrna. He shepherded the young church there, ordained St. Polycarp as his successor and died in peace around the end of the 1st century; a myrtle tree is said to have grown over his grave.

name: St. Cadfan of Bardsey
title: Abbot, Monastic Founder
bio: A Breton monk who came to Wales in the 6th century with a band of companions and founded the church at Tywyn and the monastery on Bardsey Island, known as the "island of twenty thousand saints" for the many holy monks buried there.

name: St. Cadoc of Llancarfan
title: Abbot
bio: A Welsh abbot who founded the monastery of Llancarfan in Glamorgan in the 6th century, a famous centre of learning.

name: St. Caesarius of Arles
title: Bishop of Arles
bio: A reforming bishop of Gaul who gave away church treasures to ransom captives and the poor, and worked to strengthen ecclesiastical discipline against Semi-Pelagianism.

name: St. Caesarius of Nazianzus
title: Righteous
bio: Brother of St. Gregory the Theologian, a court physician renowned for his integrity who was baptized shortly before his death.

name: St. Calinic of Cernica
title: Bishop of Râmnic
bio: Romanian abbot and bishop known for his asceticism and almsgiving, who rebuilt churches and cared for the poor of his diocese.

name: St. Callinicus of Gangra
title: Martyr
bio: A Cilician Christian who preached boldly in Galatia and Paphlagonia; forced to walk in nailed iron shoes to Gangra, he was burned there around 250.

name: Sts. Callistratus and his Companions
title: Martyrs
bio: A soldier of Carthaginian descent serving in Rome under Diocletian, Callistratus was overheard praying at night and denounced as a Christian. Sewn into a sack and thrown into the water, he was brought safely to shore; forty-nine fellow soldiers came to faith through the miracle, and all were martyred together around 304.

name: St. Callistus I of Constantinople
title: Patriarch
bio: A hesychast monk of Mount Athos who became Patriarch of Constantinople and defended the teaching of St. Gregory Palamas.

name: St. Canice of Aghaboe
title: Abbot
bio: An Irish abbot and friend of St. Columba who founded the monastery of Aghaboe and gave his name to Kilkenny, 'the church of Canice'.

name: Apostle Carpus
title: Apostle of the Seventy, Bishop of Berea
bio: Companion of St. Paul, at whose house in Troas the apostle left his cloak and books; he became bishop of Berea (Veria) in Macedonia.

locations.label: House of the apostle's cloak — Troas

name: Sts. Carpus, Papylus, Agathodorus and Agathonica
title: Martyrs
bio: Carpus, bishop of Thyatira, his deacon Papylus, Papylus's sister Agathonica and their servant Agathodorus were brought before the Roman proconsul at Pergamum. Refusing to sacrifice, they were tortured and burned in the amphitheatre in the 2nd or 3rd century; an early account of their trial survives.

name: St. Carthage (Mochuda) of Lismore
title: Abbot, Bishop
bio: A 7th-century Irish monk who founded a large monastery at Rahan and wrote a Rule for his monks. Expelled from Rahan around 636, he led his community south and founded the monastery of Lismore in County Waterford, which became a renowned school; he died there in 637.

name: St. Cataldus of Taranto
title: Bishop
bio: An Irish monk and teacher of the 7th century, associated with the school of Lismore, who was shipwrecked near Taranto in southern Italy on his way back from pilgrimage to Jerusalem. The people made him their bishop, and he is the city's patron; his relics rest in its cathedral.

locations.label: Episcopal see and relics — Taranto Cathedral

name: St. Catherine of Alexandria
title: Great Martyr
bio: A learned and noble young woman of Alexandria who confounded fifty pagan philosophers sent to refute her Christian faith and was martyred under Emperor Maximinus; her relics were later found at the monastery bearing her name on Mount Sinai.

name: St. Cecilia
title: Martyr
bio: A Roman noblewoman martyred for her faith, traditionally venerated as patroness of church music.

name: St. Cedd of Essex
title: Bishop
bio: A monk of Lindisfarne and brother of St. Chad who became bishop of the East Saxons, building the chapel of St. Peter-on-the-Wall at Bradwell, which still stands; he died at Lastingham in 664.

name: St. Celestine of Rome
title: Pope
bio: Bishop of Rome (422–432) who supported St. Cyril of Alexandria against Nestorius and sent legates to the Third Ecumenical Council at Ephesus.

name: St. Ceolfrith of Wearmouth-Jarrow
title: Abbot
bio: Abbot of the twin monasteries of Wearmouth and Jarrow and teacher of St. Bede. He enlarged their great library and had three giant Bibles copied; setting out for Rome in 716 to present one of them to the pope — the Codex Amiatinus, the oldest surviving complete Latin Bible — he died on the way at Langres in Burgundy.

name: St. Chad of Mercia
title: Bishop of Lichfield
bio: English bishop known for his humility and pastoral zeal, traveling on foot throughout his diocese to preach and founding the see of Lichfield.

name: St. Charalambos
title: Hieromartyr
bio: An elderly bishop of Magnesia who, at over a hundred years old, was seized during the persecutions of Septimius Severus for continuing to preach Christ. He endured his flesh being flayed with iron hooks without complaint, converting the very soldiers and governor sent to torment him.

name: St. Charitina of Amisus
title: Virgin Martyr
bio: An orphan raised as a daughter by a devout Christian named Claudius at Amisus on the Black Sea. Arrested under Diocletian, she endured terrible tortures without denying Christ and died in prayer around 304.

name: St. Chariton the Confessor
title: Venerable Confessor
bio: Confessor under the persecutions who founded the first lavras of the Judean desert, shaping Palestinian monasticism.

name: St. Christina the Great Martyr
title: Great Martyr
bio: A young woman of Tyre who smashed her father's golden idols and distributed the metal to the poor, she was subjected by him and later by Roman governors to a horrific series of tortures, including being thrown into the sea, all of which she miraculously survived before her eventual martyrdom.

name: St. Christodoulos of Patmos
title: Venerable
bio: Founder of the Monastery of St. John the Theologian on Patmos, obtaining imperial protection for the island's monks.

name: St. Christopher the Martyr
title: Martyr
bio: A martyr of the persecution of Decius, remembered in the East as a fearsome barbarian soldier who was baptised and gave his life for Christ in Lycia.

locations.label: Place of martyrdom — Lycia, Asia Minor

name: St. Chrysanthos, New Martyr of Cyprus
title: Martyr
bio: A Cypriot new martyr executed by Ottoman authorities for openly reaffirming his Christian faith after a false accusation.

name: Sts. Chrysanthus and Daria
title: Martyrs
bio: Chrysanthus, son of an Alexandrian senator, and Daria, a Greek priestess of Minerva whom he led to Christ, lived in chaste marriage in Rome and brought many to the faith; under Numerian they were buried alive in a sandpit on the Via Salaria.

name: St. Chrysostomos of Smyrna
title: Metropolitan and Martyr
bio: Metropolitan of Smyrna martyred by a mob in 1922 during the destruction of the city, refusing to abandon his flock.

name: St. Ciarán of Clonmacnoise
title: Venerable, Monastic Founder
bio: A carpenter's son and pupil of St. Finnian of Clonard who founded the monastery of Clonmacnoise on the River Shannon around 545 and died young that same year; it became one of Ireland's great centres of learning.

name: St. Ciarán of Saighir
title: Bishop, Monastic Founder
bio: Called the "first-born of the saints of Ireland", he is said to have been a Christian in Ossory even before St. Patrick's mission. He lived as a hermit at Saighir, where a monastery grew around him, and became the first bishop of the region in the 5th–6th century.

name: St. Clement of Ancyra
title: Hieromartyr, Bishop
bio: Bishop of Ancyra who endured many years of imprisonment and torture in successive persecutions and was finally beheaded, with his companion Agathangelus, around 312.

name: St. Clement of Ohrid
title: Bishop
bio: A disciple of Cyril and Methodius who became the first Slavic-speaking bishop, founding a great literary school at Ohrid.

locations.label: Mission with Sts. Cyril and Methodius — Great Moravia
Sent out from the Bulgarian court — Pliska

name: St. Clement of Rome
title: Hieromartyr, Pope of Rome
bio: A disciple of the Apostles Peter and Paul who became the fourth Bishop of Rome, he authored an epistle to the Corinthians that is among the earliest surviving Christian writings outside the New Testament. Exiled to Crimea for his preaching, he was drowned in the Black Sea with an anchor tied to his neck.

name: St. Cleonicus of Amasea
title: Martyr
bio: A soldier of Amasea martyred alongside Eutropius and Basiliscus for their steadfast Christian confession.

name: Apostle Cleopas
title: Apostle of the Seventy
bio: One of the two disciples to whom the risen Christ appeared on the road to Emmaus and was made known in the breaking of bread; tradition says he was later martyred in Emmaus.

locations.label: Appearance of the risen Christ — Emmaus

name: St. Clodoald (Cloud)
title: Venerable
bio: A grandson of King Clovis who alone escaped when his uncles murdered his brothers to seize their inheritance in 524. Renouncing his claim to the throne, he cut his hair, became a monk and priest, and founded a monastery at Nogent on the Seine near Paris, where he reposed around 560; the town is now called Saint-Cloud.

locations.label: Monastery and repose — Saint-Cloud, near Paris

name: St. Clotilde, Queen of the Franks
title: Righteous, Queen
bio: A Burgundian princess and wife of King Clovis, whose faith and prayers led to his baptism; widowed, she lived in prayer and charity at Tours, where she died in 545.

name: St. Colman of Lindisfarne
title: Bishop
bio: An Irish monk and bishop of Lindisfarne who defended the Irish reckoning of Easter at Whitby in 664, then withdrew with his monks to Inishbofin off the west coast of Ireland, where he died around 675.

name: St. Columba of Iona
title: Apostle to the Picts, Abbot of Iona
bio: Irish monk who founded the monastery of Iona, from which he evangelized the Picts of Scotland.

name: St. Columbanus of Luxeuil
title: Abbot and Missionary
bio: Irish monk who spread monasticism across continental Europe, founding the abbeys of Luxeuil in Gaul and Bobbio in Italy, where he died.

name: St. Comgall of Bangor
title: Abbot
bio: Irish abbot who founded the great monastery of Bangor, which sent out missionaries including St. Columbanus.

name: St. Conon of Iconium
title: Martyr
bio: A gardener of Iconium martyred for his faith, venerated for his simplicity and devotion to prayer.

name: Sts. Constantine Brâncoveanu and his Sons
title: Martyrs
bio: Prince of Wallachia (1688–1714), builder of churches and patron of Orthodox printing across the East, who was beheaded in Constantinople with his four sons and his counsellor Ianache Văcărescu for refusing to convert to Islam.

name: St. Constantine of Hydra, New Martyr
title: Martyr
bio: A sailor of Hydra martyred at Rhodes for reasserting his Christian faith before an Ottoman judge.

name: St. Constantine the Great
title: Equal-to-the-Apostles
bio: The first Christian Roman Emperor, who legalized Christianity and founded Constantinople as the new capital.

name: St. Corbinian of Freising
title: Bishop
bio: A Frankish hermit from near Paris who was consecrated bishop in Rome and became the first bishop of Freising in Bavaria around 724. Legend tells that a bear which killed his packhorse was made to carry his baggage over the Alps — the bear still appears in Freising's coat of arms. He died in 730.

name: St. Corentin of Quimper
title: Bishop
bio: A 5th-century hermit of Plomodiern in Brittany who, according to legend, fed on a single fish that renewed itself each day in his spring. He was chosen as the first bishop of Quimper, whose cathedral bears his name.

name: St. Cornelius of Komel
title: Monastic Founder
bio: Founder of a coenobitic monastery in the Komel forest, author of a monastic rule adopted widely in northern Russia.

name: St. Cornelius the Centurion
title: Righteous
bio: A Roman centurion in Caesarea who became the first Gentile convert baptized by the Apostle Peter.

name: Sts. Cosmas and Damian of Rome
title: Unmercenary Healers
bio: Brothers and physicians in Rome who healed people and animals without taking payment. Under Emperor Carinus (283–284) they were arrested and then released after their prayers healed the emperor, but their jealous former teacher lured them into the hills and stoned them to death. Orthodox tradition distinguishes them from the Asian and Arabian saints of the same names.

name: Sts. Cosmas and Damian the Unmercenaries
title: Unmercenary Healers
bio: Brothers and physicians of Asia Minor, raised in the faith by their widowed mother St. Theodota, who healed people and animals without payment. Unlike the Roman and Arabian saints of the same names, they were not martyred but reposed in peace and were buried together at Pheremane. Orthodox tradition distinguishes the three pairs.

name: St. Cosmas of Aetolia
title: Hieromartyr, Equal-to-the-Apostles
bio: A monk of Mount Athos who spent 25 years traveling on foot throughout Greece and Albania, founding over 200 schools and preaching to villagers left without churches or priests after centuries of Ottoman rule, before being martyred on charges brought against him.

name: St. Cosmas the Hymnographer
title: Bishop of Maiuma
bio: Adoptive brother of St. John of Damascus and bishop of Maiuma, author of canons for the great feasts of the Church.

locations.label: Monastery of St. Sabbas, near Jerusalem

name: Apostle Crescens
title: Apostle of the Seventy
bio: A companion of St. Paul who, according to the Second Epistle to Timothy, went to Galatia; tradition says he preached there and in Gaul and was martyred under Trajan.

name: The Ten Martyrs of Crete
title: Martyrs
bio: Ten Christians from various Cretan cities martyred together under Emperor Decius for refusing to sacrifice to idols.

name: St. Cuthbert of Lindisfarne
title: Bishop of Lindisfarne
bio: Beloved bishop and hermit of Northumbria, celebrated for his miracles and his love of solitude on the Farne Islands.

name: St. Cybi of Holyhead
title: Abbot
bio: A 6th-century Cornish monk who, after travels that tradition says took him as far as Jerusalem, settled on Anglesey. There he founded a monastery inside the walls of a Roman fort at Holyhead, still called Caer Gybi in Welsh, and was a friend of St. Seiriol.

name: Sts. Cyprian and Justina
title: Hieromartyrs
bio: A renowned pagan sorcerer of Antioch hired to ensnare the Christian maiden Justina, Cyprian found his magic powerless against her prayers and, astonished, converted and burned his books of spells before becoming a bishop. He and Justina were later arrested together and beheaded under Diocletian.

name: St. Cyprian of Carthage
title: Hieromartyr
bio: Bishop of Carthage martyred under Emperor Valerian, celebrated for his writings on Church unity.

name: St. Cyprian of Cyprus, Ethnomartyr
title: Archbishop and Martyr
bio: Archbishop of Cyprus executed by Ottoman authorities in 1821 for allegedly conspiring in the Greek War of Independence.

name: St. Cyprian of Kiev and Moscow
title: Metropolitan
bio: A Bulgarian-born metropolitan who unified the Russian Church and translated important liturgical texts into Slavonic.

name: St. Cyriacus the Anchorite
title: Hermit of the Judean Desert
bio: A disciple of St. Euthymios the Great who lived a long ascetic life as a hermit in the Judean desert, renowned for his humility and gift of healing.

name: Sts. Cyril and Methodius
title: Equal-to-the-Apostles
bio: Brothers from Thessaloniki who created the Slavic alphabet and translated Scripture, evangelizing the Slavic peoples.

name: St. Cyril of Alexandria
title: Archbishop of Alexandria
bio: Archbishop of Alexandria who presided over the Third Ecumenical Council of Ephesus (431 AD), which confirmed the title Theotokos (“God-bearer”) for the Virgin Mary against the teaching of Nestorius. His prolific theological writings earned him the title “Seal of the Fathers.”

name: St. Cyril of Belozersk
title: Venerable
bio: Monk formed in the tradition of St. Sergius who founded a great monastery on the White Lake, a centre of book-copying and northern monasticism.

name: St. Cyril of Gortyna
title: Hieromartyr, Bishop
bio: Bishop of Gortyna in Crete who in old age was condemned to be burned; when the flames did not harm him, he was beheaded, according to tradition around 300.

locations.label: Episcopal see and martyrdom — Gortyna, Crete

name: St. Cyril of Jerusalem
title: Archbishop of Jerusalem
bio: Fourth-century Archbishop of Jerusalem whose catechetical lectures remain foundational teachings on Christian doctrine and the sacraments.

name: St. Cyril of Kazan, Hieromartyr
title: Metropolitan and Martyr
bio: Metropolitan of Kazan and locum tenens candidate executed in Soviet exile for refusing to compromise Church independence.

name: St. Cyril of Novoezersk
title: Monastic Founder
bio: A hermit who founded a monastery on an island of Lake Novoye, living for decades in silence and prayer.

name: St. Cyril of Turov
title: Bishop, Preacher
bio: Medieval bishop and hymnographer of Kievan Rus', celebrated as one of its most gifted preachers and writers.

name: Sts. Cyrus and John the Unmercenaries
title: Unmercenary Healers
bio: A physician and a soldier who healed the sick without payment and were martyred together in Egypt.

name: St. Damasus of Rome
title: Pope of Rome
bio: Bishop of Rome from 366 to 384, a staunch defender of Nicene Orthodoxy. He commissioned St. Jerome to revise the Latin Bible and restored the tombs of the martyrs in the catacombs, adorning them with verse inscriptions of his own composition.

name: Holy Prophet Daniel
title: Prophet
bio: Prophet of the Babylonian captivity, preserved unharmed in the lions' den, whose visions of the Ancient of Days and the Son of Man are read at the Nativity feast.

name: St. Daniel of Moscow
title: Prince
bio: The first Prince of Moscow, celebrated for his peaceful rule, humility, and the monastery he founded, later becoming the patron saint of the city.

name: St. Daniel of Pereslavl
title: Venerable, Monastic Founder
bio: Abbot who founded the Holy Trinity Monastery at Pereslavl-Zalessky and devoted himself to burying the destitute and unknown dead; in 1530 he was godfather to the future Tsar Ivan IV.

name: St. Daniel the Hermit of Voroneț
title: Venerable
bio: A Moldavian hermit (Daniil Sihastrul) who lived in a cell carved into the rock near Putna and counselled Prince Stephen the Great, who on his advice founded the Voroneț Monastery, where Daniel became abbot.

name: St. Daniel the Stylite
title: Venerable
bio: Inspired by St. Symeon the Stylite whom he visited as a young monk, Daniel took up the ascetic discipline of pillar-standing near Constantinople, enduring decades of exposure to the elements. Emperors and patriarchs sought his counsel, and he was even ordained a priest atop his own pillar.

name: St. Danilo II of Serbia
title: Archbishop
bio: A monk and abbot of Hilandar who became Archbishop of Serbia (1324–1337), wrote the Lives of the Serbian kings and archbishops and built churches at the Patriarchate of Peć and elsewhere.

name: St. Dasius of Durostorum
title: Martyr
bio: A Roman soldier at Durostorum on the lower Danube who was chosen by lot to play the "king" of the pagan Saturnalia festival, a role that ended in his own sacrifice. Refusing to take part in its rites and declaring himself a Christian, he was beheaded in 303; his relics were later carried to Ancona in Italy.

name: Sts. David and Constantine of Argveti
title: Martyrs, Princes
bio: Brothers and princes of Argveti in western Georgia who led resistance to the Arab invasion of Marwan the Deaf in the 8th century. Captured, they refused to renounce Christ and were tortured and thrown into the Rioni River; their relics rest in Motsameta Monastery near Kutaisi.

name: St. David Garejeli
title: Monastic Founder
bio: One of the Thirteen Syrian Fathers who founded the great cave monastery complex of David Gareja in the Georgian desert.

name: St. David of Euboea
title: Venerable
bio: A hermit of Euboea known for his prophetic gifts, foretelling the recapture of Constantinople.

name: St. David of Thessaloniki
title: Venerable
bio: A monk who lived for years in the branches of an almond tree outside Thessaloniki as an extreme act of asceticism, praying exposed to sun and frost. He later left his tree to intercede successfully with the Emperor in Constantinople on behalf of his city, before returning to his monastery to die in peace.

name: St. David of Wales
title: Patron of Wales, Archbishop of Menevia
bio: Ascetic monk-bishop and founder of monasteries across Wales, revered ever since as the nation's patron saint.

name: St. David V the Builder
title: King
bio: A great medieval Georgian king who unified the country, expelled invaders, and richly endowed the Church and monasteries.

name: St. Declan of Ardmore
title: Bishop
bio: An early missionary to the Déisi of Munster, said to have preached there even before St. Patrick, who founded the monastery of Ardmore by the sea.

name: St. Deiniol of Bangor
title: Bishop, Monastic Founder
bio: A 6th-century Welsh monk who founded the monastery of Bangor in Gwynedd and became its first bishop. Bangor Cathedral, which stands on the site of his monastery, is among the oldest episcopal sees in Britain; he died around 584.

name: St. Demetrian of Chytri
title: Bishop
bio: A native of Cyprus who, after the death of his young wife, became a monk and later abbot, and was then made Bishop of Chytri (modern Kythrea) in the late 9th or early 10th century. When Arab raiders carried many Cypriots into captivity, the aged bishop travelled to Baghdad and successfully pleaded with the caliph for their release.

name: St. Demetrios of Tripoli
title: New Martyr
bio: A young man of Tripolitsa in the Peloponnese who had converted to Islam in his youth, repented on Mount Athos and returned to confess Christ in his home town, where he was beheaded in 1803.

name: St. Demetrios the New of Basarabi
title: Venerable
bio: A Bulgarian shepherd whose relics, discovered incorrupt, became the patron protector of Bucharest.

name: St. Demetrius of Chios, New Martyr
title: Martyr
bio: An eighteenth-century Chian martyred in Constantinople for openly renouncing a forced conversion to Islam.

name: St. Demetrius of Thessaloniki
title: Great Martyr, Myrrh-streamer
bio: A high-ranking Christian official martyred under Emperor Galerius, he is venerated as the patron and protector of Thessaloniki, where a miraculous flow of fragrant myrrh was later found at his tomb.

locations.label: Place of martyrdom and relics — Thessaloniki

name: St. Denis of Paris
title: Hieromartyr
bio: First bishop of Paris, beheaded on the hill of Montmartre; the abbey raised over his grave gave its name to Saint-Denis.

name: St. Diadochus of Photiki
title: Bishop
bio: A 5th-century bishop of Photiki in Epirus and defender of Chalcedon, whose 'Hundred Chapters on Spiritual Knowledge' on the prayer of the heart are included in the Philokalia.

name: St. Dimitri of Priluki
title: Monastic Founder
bio: A disciple of St. Sergius who founded the Priluki Monastery near Vologda, known for gentleness and humility.

name: St. Dimitry of Rostov
title: Metropolitan of Rostov
bio: Preacher and metropolitan who compiled the great collection of Lives of the Saints used throughout the Russian Church.

name: St. Diomedes the Physician
title: Unmercenary Martyr
bio: A physician from Tarsus who healed the sick without payment and preached Christ in Nicaea; he was beheaded under Diocletian around 298.

name: St. Dionysios of Olympus
title: Venerable
bio: A hermit and founder of a monastery on Mount Olympus, celebrated for his austere life of prayer.

name: St. Dionysios of Zakynthos
title: Archbishop, Venerable
bio: Born Draganigos Sigouros, he became a monk and later Archbishop of Aegina before retiring to a monastery on his native Zakynthos; he is remembered above all for forgiving the man who, unknowingly, had killed his own brother.

locations.label: Birthplace, monastic life, and relics — Zakynthos

name: St. Dionysius Exiguus
title: Venerable
bio: A learned monk from Scythia Minor (today's Dobruja) who settled in Rome around 500 and translated Greek canons and patristic writings into Latin. In compiling tables for the date of Pascha he counted the years from the Incarnation of Christ rather than from Diocletian, introducing the Anno Domini era still used worldwide.

name: St. Dionysius of Glushitsa
title: Monastic Founder and Iconographer
bio: An icon-painter turned monk who founded two monasteries in the Glushitsa river valley of northern Russia.

name: St. Dionysius of Radonezh
title: Archimandrite
bio: Archimandrite of the Trinity–St. Sergius Lavra during the Time of Troubles, who nursed the wounded and starving and sent letters rallying the nation to free Moscow in 1612; he died in 1633.

name: St. Dionysius the Areopagite
title: Hieromartyr
bio: A judge of the Areopagus court in Athens who was converted by hearing the Apostle Paul's sermon on the “Unknown God”, he became the first bishop of Athens. Tradition holds he later traveled west to preach the Gospel and was martyred in Lutetia (Paris).

name: St. Dionysius the Great of Alexandria
title: Archbishop of Alexandria
bio: Pupil of Origen and head of the catechetical school, then Archbishop of Alexandria (248–264), who guided his flock through the Decian persecution and the plague and wrote widely on the reception of the lapsed.

name: St. Dmitry Donskoy
title: Grand Prince
bio: Grand Prince of Moscow who, blessed by St. Sergius of Radonezh, defeated the Golden Horde at the Battle of Kulikovo in 1380 and built the first stone Kremlin of Moscow.

name: St. Dmitry of Uglich
title: Tsarevich, Passion-bearer
bio: Youngest son of Tsar Ivan IV, who died at Uglich at the age of eight in 1591 in circumstances still disputed; he is venerated as a passion-bearer, and his relics were moved to the Moscow Kremlin.

name: St. Dometian of Melitene
title: Bishop
bio: Bishop of Melitene in Armenia and a kinsman and trusted adviser of Emperor Maurice. He served as an envoy to the Persian king Khosrow II and worked for peace between the empires; he died in Constantinople in 602 and was buried in his see.

name: St. Domnica of Constantinople
title: Venerable
bio: A founder of a women's monastery in Constantinople renowned for her ascetic virtue and gift of prophecy.

name: St. Donatus of Euroea
title: Bishop, Wonderworker
bio: Bishop of Euroea in Epirus in the late 4th century, whom the historian Sozomen praises for his miracles: he slew a dragon that devoured flocks and travellers by making the sign of the Cross over it, and brought forth water in a time of drought. His relics were later taken to Kassiopi in Corfu; he is the patron of Paramythia.

name: St. Donatus of Fiesole
title: Bishop
bio: An Irish scholar-monk who, returning from pilgrimage to Rome around 829, arrived at Fiesole just as the people were choosing a bishop and was acclaimed by them. He served for nearly fifty years, founded a hospice for Irish pilgrims at Piacenza and wrote Latin verse, including a description of Ireland.

name: St. Dorotheos of Gaza
title: Venerable
bio: Sixth-century monk and abbot whose collected spiritual instructions on humility and obedience became a classic guide to monastic and Christian life.

name: St. Dorotheus of Tyre
title: Bishop of Tyre, Hieromartyr
bio: Bishop of Tyre who wrote on the lives of the apostles, endured exile under Licinius, and was martyred in old age under Julian the Apostate.

name: St. Dositheus of Gaza
title: Ascetic
bio: A young disciple of St. Dorotheos of Gaza celebrated for his rapid spiritual growth through humble obedience before an early death.

name: St. Dosoftei of Moldavia
title: Metropolitan
bio: Metropolitan of Moldavia and scholar who rendered the Psalter into Romanian verse and brought the Romanian language into the Divine Liturgy; he died in exile at Żółkiew in Poland in 1693.

name: St. Dovmont-Timothy of Pskov
title: Prince
bio: A Lithuanian prince who fled to Pskov, was baptized as Timothy and for 33 years defended the city against the Teutonic Knights; his sword is kept in Pskov's Trinity Cathedral.

name: St. Drosis of Antioch
title: Martyr
bio: Daughter of Emperor Trajan who secretly buried martyrs and was burned alive when her faith was discovered.

name: St. Dunstan of Canterbury
title: Archbishop
bio: Abbot of Glastonbury who revived monastic life in England and, as Archbishop of Canterbury from 959, reformed the Church together with King Edgar; he was also a skilled metalworker and musician.

name: St. Dwynwen of Llanddwyn
title: Venerable, Nun
bio: One of the many holy children of King Brychan of Brycheiniog in the 5th century. After an unhappy love she prayed to be freed from it and to devote her life to God, and lived as a nun on the tidal island of Llanddwyn off Anglesey; she is remembered in Wales as the patron saint of lovers.

name: St. Dyfrig of Ergyng
title: Bishop
bio: An early Welsh bishop in Ergyng who founded monasteries and is said to have ordained St. Samson; he died on Bardsey Island around 550.

name: St. Dymphna of Geel
title: Virgin Martyr
