bio: According to tradition the daughter of a pagan Irish king who, after her Christian mother's death, fled her father's unnatural advances with the priest Gerebernus. They took refuge at Geel in Brabant, where her father found them and killed them both in the 7th century; Geel became famous for its care of the mentally ill.

name: St. Eanswythe of Folkestone
title: Venerable, Abbess
bio: Granddaughter of King Ethelbert of Kent who founded at Folkestone around 630 one of the first convents in England; her relics were rediscovered in the parish church in 1885.

name: St. Eata of Hexham
title: Bishop, Abbot
bio: One of the twelve English boys trained by St. Aidan at Lindisfarne, he became abbot of Melrose, where the young Cuthbert was his monk, and later abbot and bishop of Lindisfarne and bishop of Hexham. Known for his gentleness, he died in 686.

name: St. Ebba of Coldingham
title: Venerable, Abbess
bio: Sister of St. Oswald and abbess of the double monastery of Coldingham on the Berwickshire coast, a friend of St. Cuthbert; she died around 683.

name: St. Edith of Wilton
title: Venerable, Nun
bio: Daughter of King Edgar of England, raised from infancy in the convent of Wilton where her mother was a nun. She took the veil, refused offers to become abbess of other houses, and devoted herself to prayer and the care of the poor until her death at the age of 23 in 984.

locations.label: Nun and repose — Wilton Abbey, Wiltshire

name: St. Edmund the Martyr
title: King and Martyr
bio: King of East Anglia martyred by invading Danes for refusing to renounce Christ or rule as a vassal of a pagan overlord, venerated as a patron of England.

name: St. Edward the Martyr
title: King and Passion-bearer
bio: King of England from 975, he was murdered as a youth at Corfe in 978, reportedly at the instigation of his stepmother, and soon venerated as a martyr. His relics were rediscovered at Shaftesbury in 1931 and are now kept in the Orthodox church of St. Edward at Brookwood.

name: St. Edwin of Northumbria
title: King and Martyr
bio: King of Northumbria baptized by St. Paulinus at York in 627, who was killed in battle against the pagan Penda and Cadwallon at Hatfield Chase in 633.

name: St. Eleazar of Anzer
title: Venerable
bio: A monk of Solovki who founded a skete on Anzer Island in the White Sea in 1620 and was spiritual father to the future Patriarch Nikon; he died in 1656.

name: St. Eleftherios of Illyricum
title: Hieromartyr, Bishop
bio: Born in Rome to a Christian mother, St. Anthia, he was consecrated Bishop of Illyricum at a young age. Under Emperor Hadrian he was brought back to Rome and, after enduring many torments, was beheaded together with his mother in the 2nd century.

name: St. Elesbaan of Ethiopia
title: King, Venerable
bio: Kaleb, Christian king of Axum, who around 525 crossed the Red Sea to defeat Dhu Nuwas and avenge the martyrs of Najran. Afterwards he sent his crown to Jerusalem to be hung before the Holy Sepulchre and withdrew to live as a monk in a cell until his death.

name: St. Elias Ardounis
title: New Martyr
bio: A barber from Kalamata who, after renouncing his faith under pressure, repented, confessed Christ again and was burned alive by the Ottomans in 1686.

name: St. Elias the Younger of Enna
title: Venerable
bio: Born at Enna in Sicily around 823, he was twice captured by Arab raiders and sold as a slave in North Africa, where he converted many. Freed, he visited Jerusalem and Sinai, then founded a monastery in Calabria; summoned by Emperor Leo VI, he died at Thessaloniki in 903 on the way to Constantinople.

name: St. Eligius of Noyon
title: Bishop
bio: A goldsmith and master of the mint for the Frankish kings who used his wealth to ransom slaves and found monasteries, and later became bishop of Noyon, preaching in Flanders.

name: Holy Prophet Elijah
title: Prophet
bio: The zealous prophet of Israel who confronted the priests of Baal on Mount Carmel and was taken up in a fiery chariot, honoured in the Orthodox Church as a forerunner of monastic zeal.

locations.label: Contest with the priests of Baal — Mount Carmel

name: Holy Prophet Elisha
title: Prophet
bio: Disciple and successor of the Prophet Elijah, who received a double portion of his master's spirit and worked many wonders of healing and provision in Israel.

name: St. Elizabeth the New Martyr
title: New Martyr, Grand Duchess
bio: Grand Duchess of Russia who founded a convent of mercy after her husband's assassination and was cast alive into a mineshaft by Bolsheviks for her faith.

name: St. Elizabeth the Wonderworker
title: Venerable
bio: Abbess of the convent of Sts. Cosmas and Damian in Constantinople in the 5th century, born at Heraclea in Thrace, who is said to have slain a dragon by her prayer and was renowned for her healings, especially of women.

name: St. Elizbar of Ksani
title: Martyr
bio: A Georgian duke martyred with his companion Shalva by Shah Abbas of Persia for refusing to convert to Islam.

name: St. Emilian of Cyzicus
title: Bishop and Confessor
bio: Bishop of Cyzicus exiled for defending the veneration of icons during the second period of iconoclasm.

name: St. Emilian of Durostorum
title: Martyr
bio: A young man of Durostorum on the Danube who, under Julian the Apostate, entered the pagan temple and smashed its idols. When an innocent man was about to be punished for it, he gave himself up and was burned alive around 362.

name: St. Emilian of La Cogolla
title: Venerable, Hermit
bio: A shepherd of La Rioja who became a hermit in the 6th century and lived for some forty years in the mountains. Ordained priest, he gave the goods of his church to the poor; disciples gathered around his cave at Suso, the origin of the monastery of San Millán de la Cogolla, where the earliest known written words in Spanish were later penned. He reposed in 574.

locations.label: Hermitage and monastery — San Millán de Suso, La Rioja

name: St. Emmeram of Regensburg
title: Bishop and Martyr
bio: A bishop from Poitiers who set out to evangelize the Avars but was kept in Regensburg by the Duke of Bavaria to preach there. Falsely accused of a scandal involving the duke's daughter, he was seized and brutally killed in the 7th century; his relics rest in the abbey of St. Emmeram in Regensburg.

name: St. Enda of Aran
title: Venerable, Monastic Founder
bio: A former warrior-prince of Oriel who founded a monastery on Inishmore in the Aran Islands around 484, often called a father of Irish monasticism.

name: Apostle Epaenetus
title: Apostle of the Seventy
bio: Called by Paul "my beloved Epaenetus, the first convert in Asia for Christ" (Romans 16:5; the Byzantine text reads "Achaia"), he was among the first believers of the Roman province of Asia. Tradition counts him among the Seventy and makes him bishop of Carthage.

name: St. Ephraim of Katounakia
title: Venerable, Elder of Mount Athos
bio: An Athonite elder of the desert of Katounakia, a disciple of St. Joseph the Hesychast known for his obedience and for the gift of discernment shown to those who visited him.

name: St. Ephraim of Nea Makri
title: New Martyr
bio: A monk martyred by Ottoman forces in the 15th century, whose relics were revealed near Athens in the 20th century.

name: St. Ephraim of Selenginsk, Hieromartyr
title: Bishop and Martyr
bio: A Siberian bishop shot by Bolshevik authorities in 1918 for refusing to cease his episcopal ministry.

name: St. Ephraim the Syrian
title: Venerable
bio: A deacon and prolific hymnographer of Nisibis and later Edessa, he composed hundreds of hymns and homilies in Syriac defending Orthodox teaching against heresy, many of which remain in liturgical use. His Lenten prayer, “O Lord and Master of my life,” is recited throughout Great Lent in Orthodox churches.

name: Sts. Epictetus and Astion
title: Martyrs
bio: Epictetus, a priest, and his young disciple Astion, a monk, came from Asia Minor to Halmyris near the mouths of the Danube in Scythia Minor, where they preached and healed the sick. Arrested under Diocletian, they were beheaded around 290; relics identified as theirs were discovered in the crypt of the fortress basilica of Halmyris in 2001.

name: St. Epimachus of Pelusium
title: Martyr
bio: An Egyptian ascetic of Pelusium who went to Alexandria during the persecution of Decius and publicly tore down the imperial edict ordering sacrifice. He was tortured and beheaded around 250; it is said that a woman blind in one eye was healed by drops of his blood.

name: St. Epiphanius of Cyprus
title: Bishop
bio: Bishop of Salamis in Cyprus, a staunch defender of Orthodoxy against heresies of his time.

locations.label: Birthplace and first monastery — near Eleutheropolis, Palestine

name: St. Erasmus of Formia
title: Hieromartyr, Bishop
bio: A bishop who survived tortures under Diocletian, preached in Illyricum and reposed at Formia in Italy around 303; he is the 'St. Elmo' invoked by sailors.

name: Apostle Erastus
title: Apostle of the Seventy
bio: Treasurer of the city of Corinth who became a co-worker of the Apostle Paul (Romans 16:23) and was sent with Timothy into Macedonia (Acts 19:22). Tradition counts him among the Seventy and makes him bishop of Paneas (Caesarea Philippi) at the foot of Mount Hermon.

name: St. Erkenwald of London
title: Bishop
bio: Bishop of London from 675 who founded abbeys at Chertsey and at Barking, the latter for his sister St. Ethelburga; he was long venerated at old St. Paul's Cathedral.

name: St. Ethelbert of Kent
title: King
bio: King of Kent who welcomed St. Augustine's mission in 597, was baptized and became the first Christian English king, giving Canterbury as the seat of the new Church.

name: St. Ethelburga of Barking
title: Venerable, Abbess
bio: Sister of St. Erkenwald and first abbess of the double monastery he founded for her at Barking around 666, which she guided through a deadly plague; she died around 675.

name: St. Etheldreda of Ely
title: Venerable, Abbess
bio: An East Anglian princess, also known as Audrey, who remained a virgin through two marriages and became a nun. In 673 she founded a double monastery at Ely, which she ruled as abbess until her repose in 679; her body was later found incorrupt.

name: St. Eucherius of Lyon
title: Bishop
bio: A Gallo-Roman senator who, with his wife Galla, withdrew to the islands of Lérins to live as ascetics. There he wrote "In Praise of the Desert" and other spiritual works, and around 434 he was chosen bishop of Lyon, which he governed until his death around 449.

name: St. Eudocia the Empress
title: Righteous, Empress
bio: Athenais, daughter of an Athenian philosopher, who became the wife of Emperor Theodosius II; after years at court she settled in Jerusalem, where she built churches and hospices, and died in 460.

name: St. Eudokia of Heliopolis
title: Venerable Martyr
bio: A wealthy Samaritan courtesan of Heliopolis (Baalbek) in Phoenicia, converted after overhearing a monk reading of the Last Judgement. She was baptized, gave away her fortune, became a nun and later abbess, and was beheaded for her faith in the 2nd century.

name: St. Eudokimos the Righteous
title: Righteous
bio: A Cappadocian nobleman and officer under Emperor Theophilus in the 9th century, appointed governor of the Charsianon district, who kept a pure life, defended widows and orphans and helped the poor in secret. He died at the age of 33; his body, found incorrupt, was translated to Constantinople and laid in a church of the Theotokos built by his parents.

name: St. Eugene of Sebaste
title: Martyr
bio: A companion martyr of Sebaste, commemorated with Eustratius and the other confessors of Armenia.

name: St. Eugenia of Rome
title: Martyr
bio: Daughter of a Roman prefect of Egypt, she disguised herself as a man to enter a monastery near Alexandria, eventually being chosen as its abbot without her true identity being known. She was later falsely accused, revealed her identity to clear herself, and was ultimately martyred in Rome under Valerian.

name: St. Eugenios of Trebizond
title: Martyr
bio: Martyr under Diocletian who became the patron saint of Trebizond, where a great monastery church was raised in his honour.

name: St. Eulalia of Mérida
title: Virgin Martyr
bio: A twelve-year-old girl of Mérida in Spain who went before the governor to protest the persecution and was burned around 304; the poet Prudentius sang her praises.

name: Sts. Eulampius and Eulampia
title: Martyrs
bio: A brother and sister of Nicomedia during the persecution of Maximian. When Eulampius was arrested and tortured for the faith, his sister Eulampia ran to him through the crowd, declared herself a Christian too, and shared his sufferings; both were put to death around 310, and many onlookers came to believe.

name: St. Eulogius of Alexandria
title: Patriarch
bio: A priest of Antioch who became Patriarch of Alexandria (580–608), a learned defender of Chalcedonian Orthodoxy and a friend and correspondent of St. Gregory the Dialogist.

name: St. Eulogius of Córdoba
title: Priest and Martyr
bio: A learned priest of Córdoba under the Umayyad emirs who encouraged the Christians martyred there in the 850s and wrote down their stories. Elected archbishop of Toledo but never consecrated, he was beheaded in 859 for sheltering St. Leocritia, a young convert to Christianity.

name: St. Eumenios of Gortyna
title: Bishop, Wonderworker
bio: A 7th-century bishop of Gortyna in Crete, renowned for his charity, his wonders and his defence of Orthodoxy; he died in exile and his relics were brought back to Gortyna.

name: St. Euphemia the Great Martyr
title: Great Martyr
bio: A martyr of Chalcedon whose tomb miraculously confirmed the Orthodox faith at the Fourth Ecumenical Council.

name: St. Euphrosyne of Alexandria
title: Venerable
bio: Daughter of a wealthy Alexandrian, she fled an arranged marriage and lived for 38 years disguised as the monk Smaragdus in a monastery near the city, revealing herself only to her grieving father on her deathbed.

name: St. Euphrosyne of Moscow
title: Venerable, Grand Princess
bio: Eudokia, wife of St. Dmitry Donskoy, who founded the Ascension Convent in the Moscow Kremlin, cared for the city when Tamerlane threatened it in 1395 and became the nun Euphrosyne shortly before her death in 1407.

name: St. Euphrosyne of Polotsk
title: Abbess, Enlightener of Belarus
bio: Princess turned abbess who founded monasteries and copied manuscripts, revered as the patroness of Belarus.

name: St. Euphrosyne of Suzdal
title: Venerable
bio: Daughter of St. Michael of Chernigov who, rather than marry, became a nun at the Monastery of the Deposition of the Robe in Suzdal and was renowned for her learning and prayer.

name: St. Euphrosynos the Cook
title: Venerable Monastic Cook
bio: A humble and illiterate monastery cook granted a vision of paradise, whose story teaches that true sanctity lies in quiet obedience rather than outward status.

name: St. Euphrosynus of Pskov
title: Monastic Founder
bio: Founder of the Spaso-Eleazar Monastery near Pskov and originator of a distinct monastic rule for hermits.

name: St. Euplus of Catania
title: Deacon and Martyr
bio: Deacon of Catania in Sicily arrested in 304 for carrying the Gospels; he read from them to his judge and was beheaded with the book hung around his neck.

name: St. Eupraxia of the Thebaid
title: Venerable
bio: A girl of the Constantinopolitan nobility who at seven entered a convent in the Thebaid with her widowed mother, gave away her inheritance and lived in great humility until her death at thirty around 413.

name: St. Eupsychius of Caesarea
title: Martyr
bio: A newly married young nobleman of Caesarea in Cappadocia who took part in pulling down the temple of Fortune and was beheaded under Julian the Apostate in 362; St. Basil the Great kept his feast each year.

name: St. Eusebius of Samosata
title: Hieromartyr, Bishop
bio: Bishop of Samosata and friend of St. Basil the Great, who travelled disguised as a soldier to strengthen the Orthodox against Arianism; he was killed by a roof tile thrown by an Arian woman at Dolikha around 380.

name: St. Eusebius of Vercelli
title: Bishop and Confessor
bio: Born in Sardinia, he became the first bishop of Vercelli in 345 and lived with his clergy in a monastic community. For refusing to condemn St. Athanasius at the Council of Milan in 355 he was exiled to Scythopolis in Palestine, Cappadocia and Egypt; he returned to strengthen Nicene Orthodoxy in Italy and died in 371.

name: St. Eusignius of Antioch
title: Martyr
bio: A veteran soldier who had served under Constantius Chlorus and Constantine the Great. At the age of about 110 he rebuked Julian the Apostate for abandoning the faith, reminding him of Constantine's vision of the Cross, and was beheaded at Antioch around 362.

name: St. Eustathios Placidas
title: Great Martyr
bio: A Roman general known as Placidas who converted to Christianity after seeing a vision of Christ between the antlers of a stag while hunting, taking the name Eustathios at baptism. After enduring the loss of his family and fortune as trials of faith, he was ultimately martyred with his wife and sons by being roasted alive in a bronze bull.

name: St. Eustathius of Antioch
title: Archbishop and Confessor
bio: Archbishop of Antioch and a champion of the Nicene faith at the First Ecumenical Council, who was deposed through Arian slander and exiled to Thrace, where he died around 337.

name: St. Eustathius of Mtskheta
title: Martyr
bio: A Persian convert to Christianity martyred at Mtskheta for refusing to return to Zoroastrianism.

name: St. Eustratius of Sebaste
title: Martyr
bio: One of the Five Martyrs of Sebaste, a military officer burned alive for his unwavering confession of Christ.

name: St. Euthymios of Mount Athos, New Martyr
title: Martyr
bio: An Athonite monk who publicly renounced a forced conversion to Islam and was executed at Constantinople.

name: St. Euthymios of Zela, Metropolitan and Martyr
title: Metropolitan and Martyr
bio: A Pontic Greek hierarch martyred amid the persecutions accompanying the fall of Smyrna in 1922.

name: St. Euthymios the Great
title: Venerable
bio: Born in Melitene in Armenia, he journeyed to the Judean Desert and founded a renowned lavra that became a center of monastic and doctrinal formation, playing a key role in defending Orthodoxy at the Council of Chalcedon. He is honored as one of the great founders of Palestinian monasticism.

locations.label: Foundation of his Lavra — Judean Desert

name: St. Euthymius of Novgorod
title: Archbishop
bio: Archbishop of Novgorod (1429–1458) who built and restored many churches, including the Palace of Facets in the Novgorod kremlin, and was buried at the Vyazhishchi monastery he had renewed.

name: St. Euthymius of Sardis
title: Hieromartyr, Bishop
bio: Bishop of Sardis and a leading defender of the holy icons, who endured repeated exiles and was scourged to death under Emperor Theophilos in 831.

name: St. Euthymius of Suzdal
title: Venerable, Monastic Founder
bio: Abbot who founded the Monastery of the Saviour at Suzdal in 1352 and made it a centre of prayer and charity; he died in 1404.

locations.label: Monastery of the Saviour and St. Euthymius — Suzdal

name: St. Euthymius of Tarnovo
title: Patriarch
bio: The last medieval Patriarch of Bulgaria, a reformer of liturgical texts and defender of the Church before the Ottoman conquest.

name: St. Euthymius the Iberian
title: Venerable
bio: Son of St. John the Iberian and co-founder of the Iviron Monastery on Mount Athos, who translated a great body of Greek patristic and liturgical texts into Georgian; he died in Constantinople in 1028.

name: St. Euthymius the New of Thessaloniki
title: Monk
bio: A ninth-century monk who founded communities on Mount Athos and was known for extreme fasting and stillness.

name: St. Eutychius of Constantinople
title: Patriarch
bio: Patriarch of Constantinople who presided over the Fifth Ecumenical Council in 553; exiled for twelve years to his monastery at Amasea for opposing Justinian's late doctrinal views, he was restored in 577.

name: Holy Prophet Ezekiel
title: Prophet
bio: Priest and prophet among the exiles in Babylon, whose visions of the glory of God, of the dry bones restored to life and of the closed gate of the Temple are read by the Church as foretelling the Resurrection and the Theotokos.

locations.label: Exile — by the river Chebar near Nippur, Babylonia

name: St. Faith of Agen
title: Virgin Martyr
bio: A young girl of Agen in Gaul who was roasted on a brazier and beheaded around 303 for refusing to sacrifice to the gods. In the 9th century her relics were taken to the abbey of Conques, which became a great pilgrimage centre on the road to Santiago.

name: St. Fanourios the Newly-Revealed
title: Great Martyr
bio: Known only from an icon discovered amid the ruins of an ancient church during the excavation of the city walls of Rhodes, depicting scenes of his martyrdom alongside his name, with no other historical record surviving. Devotion to him spread quickly, and to this day the faithful bake “fanouropita” cakes in his honor when seeking help to find lost things.

name: St. Fara of Faremoutiers
title: Venerable, Abbess
bio: A Frankish noblewoman blessed as a child by St. Columbanus, who resisted her father's plan to marry her and around 620 founded the abbey of Faremoutiers near Meaux. She led it for nearly forty years under the rule of Columbanus; her brothers St. Faro and St. Chagnoald became bishops.

name: St. Febronia of Nisibis
title: Martyr
bio: A young nun of Nisibis tortured extensively and martyred for refusing marriage and renouncing Christ.

name: St. Felicula of Rome
title: Virgin Martyr
bio: A Roman virgin martyred for refusing marriage and sacrifice to idols during the early persecutions.

name: Sts. Felix and Regula
title: Martyrs
bio: A brother and sister of the Theban Legion who escaped its massacre and fled across the Alps to Glarus and then to Zurich. There they were arrested and beheaded around 286 for refusing to sacrifice to the gods; the Grossmünster church stands over their tomb, and they are the patron saints of Zurich.

name: St. Felix of Dunwich
title: Bishop
bio: A Burgundian bishop who became the apostle of East Anglia around 630, founding his see at Dunwich and a school with the support of King Sigeberht.

name: St. Felix of Nola
title: Priest and Confessor
bio: A priest of Nola in Campania who was imprisoned and tortured in the persecution of Decius and, according to tradition, freed by an angel to rescue his aged bishop Maximus. He later refused the episcopate and lived in poverty, dying around 260; St. Paulinus of Nola built a great basilica complex over his tomb.

name: St. Ferapont of Belozersk
title: Venerable, Monastic Founder
bio: A Moscow monk and companion of St. Cyril of Belozersk who founded the Ferapontov Monastery in the far north in 1398, later famous for Dionisy's frescoes, and then the Luzhetsky Monastery at Mozhaysk.

name: St. Fiacre of Breuil
title: Venerable, Hermit
bio: An Irish hermit who settled at Breuil near Meaux in Gaul in the 7th century, cultivating a garden and caring for the poor and sick; he is the patron of gardeners.

name: St. Fillan of Strathfillan
title: Abbot
bio: An Irish monk who worked in Scotland in the 8th century, living as a hermit and abbot in Glen Dochart and the glen of Strathfillan, which takes its name from him. His crozier, the Quigrich, and his bell survive in the National Museum of Scotland, and Robert the Bruce is said to have invoked him before Bannockburn.

locations.label: Hermitage and priory — Strathfillan, near Tyndrum

name: St. Filofteia of Curtea de Argeș
title: Virgin Martyr
bio: A Bulgarian girl martyred by her own father for giving alms to the poor, whose relics rest at Curtea de Argeș.

name: St. Finbarr of Cork
title: Bishop
bio: A hermit of Gougane Barra who founded a monastery and school on the banks of the River Lee around 600, from which the city of Cork grew.

name: St. Finnian of Clonard
title: Bishop, Abbot
bio: Irish bishop whose monastic school at Clonard trained many saints, who were later called the Twelve Apostles of Ireland.

name: St. Fintan of Clonenagh
title: Abbot
bio: A 6th-century Irish abbot who founded the monastery of Clonenagh in Laois and led his monks in an austere life of prayer and manual labour, living on vegetables and water and tilling the land by hand. He was renowned for prophecy and miracles and drew many disciples.

name: St. Flacilla the Empress
title: Righteous, Empress
bio: Wife of Emperor Theodosius the Great and a firm upholder of Nicene Orthodoxy, who personally cared for the sick in the hospitals of Constantinople; St. Gregory of Nyssa delivered her funeral oration in 386.

name: St. Flavian of Constantinople
title: Hieromartyr
bio: Patriarch who was beaten and exiled at the 'Robber Council' of Ephesus for upholding Orthodox Christology.

name: St. Florian of Lorch
title: Martyr
bio: A Roman officer in Noricum who came to Lauriacum (Lorch, near Enns) during the persecution of Diocletian to help the Christians imprisoned there and declared himself one of them. He was thrown into the river Enns with a millstone around his neck in 304; the abbey of St. Florian stands over his traditional grave, and he is invoked as a protector against fire.

name: Sts. Florus and Laurus
title: Martyrs
bio: Twin brothers and stonemasons from Byzantium who built a temple at Ulpiana in Illyricum, then turned it into a church and smashed its idols; they were thrown alive into a well. They are honoured as patrons of horses.

name: The Forty-Five Martyrs of Nicopolis
title: Martyrs
bio: Christians of Nicopolis in Armenia, led by Leontius, Maurice, Daniel and Anthony, who gave themselves up to the governor under Licinius and, after tortures, were burned and their remains thrown into a river around 319.

name: The Forty-Two Martyrs of Amorium
title: Martyrs
bio: Byzantine officers and nobles taken captive when the Caliph al-Mu'tasim sacked the city of Amorium in Phrygia in 838. After seven years in prison they still refused to renounce Christ and were beheaded on the banks of the Tigris at Samarra in 845.

name: St. Frideswide of Oxford
title: Venerable, Abbess
bio: An Anglo-Saxon princess and abbess who founded a monastery at Oxford around 700; she is the patron saint of the city and its university.

name: St. Fridolin of Säckingen
title: Abbot, Missionary
bio: An Irish monk of the 6th century who, according to his Life, restored the church of St. Hilary at Poitiers and then carried relics of St. Hilary to the Upper Rhine. There he founded a monastery on an island in the river at Säckingen and preached to the Alemanni; he is the patron of the Swiss canton of Glarus.

locations.label: Restoration of St. Hilary's church — Poitiers

name: St. Fructuosus of Braga
title: Archbishop, Monastic Founder
bio: A Visigothic noble who gave his wealth to found many monasteries in the north-west of Spain, writing Rules for them, and became known as the father of Hispanic monasticism. He was made bishop of Dumio and in 656 archbishop of Braga, where he died in 665.

name: St. Fructuosus of Tarragona
title: Hieromartyr, Bishop
bio: Bishop of Tarragona who, with his deacons Augurius and Eulogius, was burned in the amphitheatre under Valerian in 259; the record of his trial survives and St. Augustine preached on his feast.

name: St. Frumentius of Axum
title: Bishop, Enlightener of Ethiopia
bio: A Christian from Tyre who, shipwrecked as a boy, rose to serve at the royal court of Axum, was consecrated bishop by St. Athanasius the Great and became the enlightener of Ethiopia.

name: St. Fulgentius of Ruspe
title: Bishop
bio: A Roman official in North Africa who, moved by reading St. Augustine, became a monk and later bishop of Ruspe around 508. Twice exiled to Sardinia by the Arian Vandal king Thrasamund, he wrote widely on the Holy Trinity and on grace, and died in 533.

name: St. Fursey of Péronne
title: Abbot
bio: An Irish monk and visionary who founded monasteries in Ireland, at Burgh Castle in East Anglia and at Lagny in Gaul; his visions of the afterlife were widely read. He died around 650 and is buried at Péronne.

name: St. Gabriel (Urgebadze) of Georgia
title: Fool-for-Christ of Georgia
bio: Beloved Georgian elder and fool-for-Christ, famed for his boldness of faith under Soviet rule and his ministry at Samtavro Convent.

name: St. Gabriel of Lesnovo
title: Venerable
bio: An 11th-century hermit of Mount Lesnovo near Kratovo whose relics were honoured at the Lesnovo Monastery before being moved to Tarnovo.

name: Sts. Galaktion and Episteme
title: Martyrs
bio: A married couple of Emesa who by mutual consent embraced monastic life on Mount Publion, and were tortured and beheaded together under Decius.

name: St. Gall of St. Gallen
title: Venerable, Enlightener of Switzerland
bio: Irish disciple of St. Columbanus who remained in the Alps as a hermit and preacher; the Swiss town and monastery of St. Gallen grew up around his cell.

name: St. Genevieve of Paris
title: Patroness of Paris
bio: Fifth-century ascetic credited with saving Paris from Attila the Hun through prayer, venerated ever since as the city's patroness.

name: St. Gennadius Scholarios
title: Patriarch
bio: The first Ecumenical Patriarch under Ottoman rule after the fall of Constantinople, guiding the Church through crisis.

name: St. Gennady of Kostroma
title: Monastic Founder
bio: A disciple of St. Alexander of Svir who founded a monastery in the Kostroma forests, teaching strict poverty.

name: St. George
title: Great Martyr
bio: A Roman soldier martyred for his Christian faith, venerated across the Orthodox world as a symbol of courage and the slayer of the dragon.

name: St. George Karslidis
title: Venerable, Elder
bio: A Pontic Greek elder born near Argyroupolis (Gümüşhane) who, after the population exchange, founded the Monastery of the Ascension at Sipsa (Taxiarches) near Drama and guided countless pilgrims until his death in 1959.

name: St. George of Choziba
title: Venerable
bio: A Cypriot who joined his brother at the cliff-side Monastery of Choziba in the Wadi Qelt in the 6th–7th centuries, known for his strict asceticism and gift of tears.

locations.label: Monastic life — Choziba Monastery, Wadi Qelt

name: St. George of Iviron
title: Venerable
bio: Georgian abbot of Iviron who continued St. Euthymius' translation work, revised the Georgian liturgical books and later laboured in Georgia; he reposed in Constantinople in 1065.

name: St. George of Serbia, New Martyr
title: Martyr
bio: A young Serbian martyred by Ottoman authorities in Sofia for refusing conversion to Islam.

name: St. George the Confessor of Limnos
title: Confessor
bio: A monk and bishop who suffered imprisonment defending icon veneration during the iconoclast persecutions.

name: St. George the New of Ioannina
title: New Martyr
bio: A young Christian craftsman martyred in Ottoman-ruled Ioannina after refusing to convert to Islam.

name: St. George the New of Sofia
title: New Martyr
bio: A young craftsman burned alive in Sofia after refusing to renounce Christianity under Ottoman rule.

name: St. Gerasimos of Kephalonia
title: Venerable, Wonderworker
bio: Born to a noble Byzantine family, he lived as a hermit on Mount Athos, in Jerusalem, Sinai, Egypt, Crete, and Zakynthos before settling in a cave in Kephalonia, where he restored a church and founded a convent; he is now the island's patron saint.

name: St. Gerasimos of the Jordan
title: Venerable
bio: A 5th-century abbot near the Jordan River famed for taming a lion that became his devoted companion.

name: St. Gerasimus of Vologda
title: Venerable, Monastic Founder
bio: A monk of the Kiev Caves who came north and founded a Holy Trinity monastery at Vologda; his Life dates his arrival to 1147, the traditional founding year of the city.

name: St. Gereon of Cologne
title: Martyr
bio: According to tradition, an officer of the Theban Legion who with his companions was put to death at Cologne in the early 4th century for refusing to sacrifice to the gods. The Basilica of St. Gereon, built over their tomb in late Roman times, is one of the oldest churches in Germany.

name: St. Germanus of Auxerre
title: Bishop of Auxerre
bio: Bishop of Gaul who twice crossed to Britain to strengthen the Church there against the Pelagian teaching.

name: St. Germanus of Constantinople
title: Patriarch
bio: Patriarch deposed for opposing iconoclasm, whose hymns are still sung in Orthodox services today.

name: St. Germanus of Paris
title: Bishop
bio: Abbot of Saint-Symphorien at Autun who became bishop of Paris around 555, famed for his charity, his ransoming of captives and his rebukes of the violence of the Merovingian kings.

name: St. Gertrude of Nivelles
title: Venerable, Abbess
bio: Daughter of Pepin of Landen and abbess of the double monastery of Nivelles in Brabant, known for her learning and her hospitality to Irish monks; she died in 659.

name: St. Gheorghe of Cernica
title: Venerable, Abbot
bio: Born in Transylvania in 1730, he became a monk on Mount Athos and a disciple of St. Paisius Velichkovsky. Sent to Wallachia, he restored the monasteries of Cernica and Căldărușani near Bucharest, introducing the Paisian tradition of the Jesus Prayer; he died in 1806.

name: St. Gildas the Wise
title: Abbot
bio: A 6th-century British monk, author of "On the Ruin of Britain," which rebukes the kings and clergy of his day and is a key source for post-Roman Britain. He later crossed to Brittany and founded a monastery at Rhuys, where he reposed around 570.

name: St. Giles the Hermit
title: Venerable, Abbot
bio: According to his Life, a Greek from Athens who sailed to Provence and lived as a hermit near the mouth of the Rhône, nourished by the milk of a hind. When a royal hunting party wounded him with an arrow meant for the deer, the king honoured him and built a monastery around which the town of Saint-Gilles grew; he reposed in the early 8th century and became one of the most popular saints of medieval Europe.

name: St. Glyceria of Heraclea
title: Virgin Martyr
bio: A Roman consul's daughter martyred at Heraclea in Thrace after surviving a bear attack and other torments.

name: St. Gobnait of Ballyvourney
title: Venerable, Abbess
bio: A 6th-century Irish woman who lived on Inis Oírr in the Aran Islands until an angel told her to seek the place where she would find nine white deer grazing. She found them at Ballyvourney in County Cork, founded a community of women there and became known as a healer and keeper of bees.

locations.label: Early life — Inis Oírr, Aran Islands

name: St. Gobron (Michael) of Georgia
title: Martyr
bio: A Georgian military commander martyred with a company of soldiers by Arab forces besieging the fortress of Kldekari.

locations.label: Place of martyrdom — Kldekari fortress, Georgia

name: St. Gorazd of Czech Lands and Slovakia
title: Bishop and Martyr
bio: Twentieth-century Orthodox bishop of Czechoslovakia executed by the Nazis for sheltering the assassins of Reinhard Heydrich.

name: St. Gorazd of Moravia
title: Bishop
bio: A disciple and successor of St. Methodius who continued the Slavic liturgical mission in Great Moravia.

name: St. Gordius of Caesarea
title: Martyr
bio: A Roman centurion of Cappadocian Caesarea who withdrew to the desert and later returned publicly to confess Christ, for which he was executed.

name: St. Gorgonia of Nazianzus
title: Righteous
bio: Sister of St. Gregory the Theologian, celebrated for her piety, hospitality, and remarkable recovery from illness through faith.

name: St. Gregorios of Kydonies, Metropolitan and Martyr
title: Metropolitan and Martyr
bio: A Metropolitan of Kydonies (Ayvalik) martyred during the Asia Minor catastrophe of the early twentieth century.

name: St. Gregory of Agrigento
title: Bishop of Agrigento
bio: Sicilian bishop renowned for his commentary on Ecclesiastes and his steadfastness amid false accusations.

name: St. Gregory of Decapolis
title: Venerable
bio: 8th-century monk from Irenopolis in Isauria who traveled widely across Greece and Italy, defended the holy icons, and reposed in Constantinople.

name: St. Gregory of Khandzta
title: Monastic Founder
bio: Founder of numerous monasteries in medieval Georgian Tao-Klarjeti, a central figure of Georgian monastic revival.

name: St. Gregory of Narek
title: Venerable and Doctor
bio: An Armenian monk, poet, and theologian, celebrated for his 'Book of Lamentations' and profound spiritual depth.

name: St. Gregory of Nyssa
title: Hierarch
bio: Bishop of Nyssa and one of the Cappadocian Fathers, celebrated for his mystical theology and defense of Nicene doctrine.

name: St. Gregory of Sinai
title: Venerable
bio: A monk who revived the practice of hesychasm and spread it among monasteries in Greece and the Balkans.

name: St. Gregory of the Great Lavra
title: Abbot
bio: A revered abbot of the Great Lavra on Mount Athos known for hospitality and defense of monastic tradition.

name: St. Gregory of Tours
title: Bishop
bio: Bishop and historian of Gaul whose writings, including the History of the Franks, preserved the memory of early Western saints venerated before the Great Schism.

name: St. Gregory Palamas
title: Archbishop of Thessalonica
bio: A monk of Mount Athos and later Archbishop of Thessalonica, he defended the hesychast practice of contemplative prayer against the rationalist Barlaam of Calabria, teaching that God's uncreated energies can truly be experienced by the faithful.

name: St. Gregory the Dialogist
title: Pope of Rome
bio: Pope of Rome and prolific author of the 'Dialogues,' who reformed the liturgy and sent missionaries to evangelize England.

name: St. Gregory the Elder of Nazianzus
title: Bishop
bio: Father of St. Gregory the Theologian who served as Bishop of Nazianzus for over four decades.

name: St. Gregory the Illuminator
title: Equal-to-the-Apostles
bio: Apostle to Armenia who converted King Tiridates III and the Armenian nation to Christianity, becoming the first Catholicos of the Armenian Church.

name: St. Gregory the Theologian
title: Archbishop of Constantinople, one of the Three Holy Hierarchs
bio: A close friend of St. Basil the Great, he was chosen Archbishop of Constantinople by the Second Ecumenical Council for his defense of the Trinity against Arianism, before retiring to Nazianzus for the rest of his life.

name: St. Gregory the Wonderworker
title: Bishop of Neocaesarea, Wonderworker
bio: A student of Origen who became bishop of Neocaesarea and, through his miracles and preaching, found seventeen Christians in the city and left only seventeen pagans at his death.

name: St. Gregory V of Constantinople
title: Patriarch and Ethnomartyr
bio: Ecumenical Patriarch hanged by Ottoman authorities at the outbreak of the Greek War of Independence in 1821.

name: St. Grigol Peradze
title: Hieromartyr
bio: A Georgian archimandrite and patristic scholar who taught at the University of Warsaw; arrested by the Nazis, he died at Auschwitz in 1942, according to witnesses after taking upon himself another prisoner's guilt.

name: St. Gudula of Brussels
title: Venerable
bio: A 7th-century noblewoman of Brabant, goddaughter of St. Gertrude of Nivelles, who lived a life of prayer and charity at Moorsel. Legend tells that when the devil blew out her lantern on her way to church before dawn, it was rekindled by her prayer; she is the patroness of Brussels, whose cathedral bears her name with St. Michael.

locations.label: Relics and patronage — Cathedral of Sts. Michael and Gudula, Brussels

name: Sts. Gurias, Samonas and Abibus
title: Martyrs and Confessors
bio: Gurias and Samonas, Christians of Edessa martyred under Diocletian, and the deacon Abibus, burned under Licinius; together they are invoked as protectors of marriage.

name: St. Gury of Kazan
title: Archbishop
bio: First Orthodox archbishop of Kazan, a missionary who established schools and translated texts for the Volga peoples.

name: St. Guthlac of Crowland
title: Venerable, Hermit
bio: A Mercian nobleman and warrior who became a monk and lived as a hermit in the fens at Crowland, where an abbey later grew up around his cell; he died in 714.

name: Holy Prophet Habakkuk
title: Prophet
bio: Minor prophet whose canticle — 'God shall come from Teman' — inspires the fourth ode of the Orthros canon; tradition says an angel carried him to Babylon to feed Daniel in the lions' den.

name: Holy Prophet Haggai
title: Prophet
bio: Minor prophet who, after the return from Babylon, urged Zerubbabel and the people to rebuild the Temple in 520 BC, promising that its glory would surpass that of the former house.

name: St. Hallvard of Oslo
title: Martyr
bio: A young Norwegian, kinsman of St. Olaf, who in 1043 tried to save a woman accused of theft by taking her into his boat. Her pursuers shot them both and sank his body with a millstone, but it floated to the surface; he became the patron of Oslo, whose seal still shows him holding a millstone and arrows.

locations.label: Shrine — St. Hallvard's Cathedral, Old Oslo

name: St. Helen of Anjou, Queen of Serbia
title: Righteous, Queen
bio: A French-born queen, wife of King Stefan Uroš I and mother of Kings Dragutin and Milutin, who founded Gradac Monastery, opened schools for girls and became a nun before her death in 1314.

name: St. Helen, Equal-to-the-Apostles
title: Equal-to-the-Apostles
bio: Mother of Emperor Constantine who discovered the True Cross in Jerusalem and built many churches.

locations.label: Church of the Nativity founded — Bethlehem

name: St. Heraclides of Cyprus
title: Bishop
bio: A companion of the Apostle Barnabas consecrated as the first bishop of Tamassus in Cyprus.

name: St. Herbert of Derwentwater
title: Venerable, Hermit
bio: A 7th-century hermit who lived on an island in the lake of Derwentwater and visited his close friend St. Cuthbert each year. At their last meeting he asked to die on the same day as Cuthbert, and St. Bede records that both reposed on 20 March 687.

name: St. Herman of Alaska
title: Venerable
bio: A Russian monk missionary to Alaska who defended the native Aleut people and lived in ascetic simplicity on Spruce Island.

name: St. Herman of Kazan
title: Archbishop
bio: Abbot of the Sviyazhsk monastery who became the second archbishop of Kazan, laboured to enlighten the newly conquered region and was removed for rebuking Ivan the Terrible; he died in Moscow in 1567.

name: St. Herman of Solovki
title: Monastic Founder
bio: Co-founder with Sts. Zosimas and Savvatii of the great Solovki Monastery in the White Sea.

name: St. Hermenegild of Seville
title: Martyr, Prince
bio: A Visigothic prince who embraced the Orthodox faith over Arianism and rose against his father King Leovigild; refusing Communion from an Arian bishop, he was put to death at Tarragona in 585.

name: St. Hermias of Comana
title: Martyr
bio: An aged soldier who had served many years in the Roman army and openly confessed his faith at Comana in Pontus in the 2nd century. He endured many tortures unharmed, converting the executioner Mamerchus who was martyred before him, and was finally beheaded.

name: St. Hermione of Ephesus
title: Martyr
bio: Daughter of the Apostle Philip who had the gift of healing and was martyred under Emperor Trajan.

name: St. Hermogenes of Ekaterinburg's Companions
title: Martyrs
bio: A group of Russian clergy and laity martyred together with Bishop Hermogenes near Tobolsk during the Civil War.

name: St. Hermogenes of Moscow
title: Patriarch of Moscow, Hieromartyr
bio: Patriarch during the Time of Troubles who refused to bless the Polish claim to the throne and, imprisoned in the Kremlin, called Russia to resistance until he died of starvation.

name: St. Hermogenes of Tobolsk, Hieromartyr
title: Bishop and Martyr
bio: Bishop of Tobolsk drowned by Bolshevik forces in the Tura River in 1918 for his outspoken defense of the Church.

name: St. Hermolaus of Nicomedia
title: Priest-Martyr
bio: A priest who instructed St. Panteleimon in the faith and was martyred alongside two companions in Nicomedia.

name: Sts. Hermylus and Stratonicus
title: Martyrs
bio: Hermylus, a deacon, and his friend Stratonicus, a prison guard who wept at his torture and then confessed Christ himself, were drowned together in the Danube at Singidunum (Belgrade) under Licinius.

name: Apostle Herodion
title: Apostle of the Seventy, Bishop of Patras
bio: A kinsman of St. Paul, greeted by him in the Epistle to the Romans, and one of the Seventy Apostles. He became bishop of Patras, where his preaching converted many; he was beaten and stabbed to death by those who opposed the Gospel.

name: St. Hesychios of Jerusalem
title: Presbyter and Theologian
bio: 5th-century priest and biblical commentator in Jerusalem, a disciple of Gregory the Theologian. His writings include sermons and scriptural commentaries.

name: The Hieromartyrs of Cherson
title: Hieromartyrs
bio: Seven bishops — Basil, Ephraim, Eugene, Agathodorus, Elpidius, Aetherius and Capito — sent in the 4th century to preach the Gospel in Chersonesus in the Crimea. Most were killed by the pagans of the region; Capito is said to have come out of a burning furnace unharmed, leading many to baptism.

name: St. Hierotheos of Athens
title: Bishop of Athens, Hieromartyr
bio: First Bishop of Athens, converted by the Apostle Paul through the Areopagus preaching and the teacher of St. Dionysius the Areopagite. Tradition holds that he was present at the Dormition of the Theotokos, where he led the divine hymnody.

name: St. Hilarion (Troitsky)
title: Hieromartyr, Archbishop
bio: Archbishop of Vereya, a brilliant theologian and close aide of St. Tikhon of Moscow, who was imprisoned in the Solovki camp and died of typhus in Leningrad in 1929.

name: St. Hilarion of Kiev
title: Metropolitan
bio: A priest of Berestovo who prayed in a small cave later enlarged into the Kiev Caves Lavra; made the first native Metropolitan of Kiev in 1051, he wrote the 'Sermon on Law and Grace'.

name: St. Hilarion of Moglena
title: Bishop
bio: Bishop of Moglena in Macedonia in the 12th century who opposed the Bogomil and Armenian heresies; his relics were carried to Tarnovo by Tsar Kaloyan.

name: St. Hilarion of Optina
title: Elder
bio: One of the renowned elders of the Optina Hermitage tradition, a spiritual guide to pilgrims from across Russia.

name: St. Hilarion the Georgian
title: Venerable
bio: Son of a Georgian nobleman who lived as a hermit at David Gareji, then on Mount Athos, Mount Olympus in Bithynia and in Rome; he died in Thessaloniki in 875, where Emperor Basil I had him honourably buried.

name: St. Hilarion the Great
title: Venerable
bio: A disciple of Anthony the Great who brought monasticism from Egypt to Palestine.

locations.label: Discipleship under Anthony the Great — Eastern Desert, Egypt

name: St. Hilary of Arles
title: Bishop of Arles
bio: A young Gallo-Roman noble who was drawn by his kinsman St. Honoratus to the monastery of Lérins and succeeded him as bishop of Arles in 429. He lived in great austerity, worked with his hands, preached tirelessly and ransomed captives, dying in 449.

name: St. Hilary of Poitiers
title: Bishop of Poitiers
bio: Bishop of Gaul exiled for opposing Arianism, whose treatise On the Trinity defended the divinity of Christ in the Latin West.

name: St. Hilda of Whitby
title: Abbess
bio: Northumbrian abbess whose double monastery at Whitby trained bishops and sheltered the poet Caedmon.

name: St. Hippolytus of Rome
title: Hieromartyr
bio: Roman presbyter and writer against the heresies of his day, exiled to the mines of Sardinia where he died reconciled to the Church.

name: The Holy Myrrhbearing Women
title: Myrrhbearers
bio: The women disciples who came to anoint Christ's body and were the first to learn of His Resurrection.

name: St. Honoratus of Arles
title: Bishop, Monastic Founder
bio: Founder around 410 of the monastery on the island of Lérins, which became a nursery of bishops and saints for Gaul; he was made Archbishop of Arles shortly before his death in 429.

name: Holy Prophet Hosea
title: Prophet
bio: First of the twelve minor prophets, who preached in the northern kingdom of Israel and portrayed God's faithful love for His unfaithful people through his own marriage; St. Matthew applies his words 'Out of Egypt have I called my son' to Christ.

name: Sts. Hripsime, Gaiane and Companions
title: Virgin Martyrs
bio: Consecrated virgins who fled persecution to Armenia, where King Tiridates III had them killed at Vagharshapat around 301; their martyrdom preceded the king's conversion through St. Gregory the Illuminator.

name: St. Hubert of Liège
title: Bishop, Enlightener of the Ardennes
bio: A Frankish nobleman who, after the death of his wife, became a disciple of St. Lambert and succeeded him as bishop of Maastricht around 705. He moved his see to Liège, where Lambert had been martyred, and evangelized the pagans of the Ardennes until his death in 727.

name: St. Hyacinth of Amastris
title: Martyr
bio: A young Christian of Amastris in Paphlagonia who cut down a tree worshipped by the pagans of the city. He was beaten, stoned and thrown into prison, where he died of his wounds and hunger in the early 2nd century.

name: St. Hypatius of Gangra
title: Hieromartyr, Bishop
bio: Bishop of Gangra in Paphlagonia who attended the First Ecumenical Council; returning from Constantinople, he was stoned to death by Novatian heretics around 326.

name: St. Hypatius of Rufinianae
title: Abbot
bio: Abbot of a monastery near Chalcedon renowned for exorcisms and strict monastic discipline in the fifth century.

name: St. Hypomone (Helen Dragaš)
title: Venerable, Empress
bio: Helen Dragaš, Serbian-born wife of Emperor Manuel II Palaiologos and mother of the last two Byzantine emperors, who became the nun Hypomone ('Patience') and founded a home for the elderly in Constantinople; she died in 1450.

name: St. Iakovos (Jacob) Tsalikis
title: Venerable
bio: Abbot of Saint David Monastery in Euboea, revered in modern Greece for his humility and visions of saints.

name: St. Ignatios of Mount Athos, New Martyr
title: Martyr
bio: A Bulgarian monk of Mount Athos executed at Constantinople for reaffirming his Christian faith before Ottoman judges.

name: St. Ignatius Brianchaninov
title: Bishop of the Caucasus and Black Sea
bio: Officer turned monk and bishop whose ascetical writings interpret the Fathers for Christians living in the modern world.

name: St. Ignatius of Antioch
title: Hieromartyr
bio: Bishop of Antioch and disciple of the Apostles, thrown to wild beasts in Rome, whose letters to the early Church remain foundational Christian writings.

name: St. Ignatius of Constantinople
title: Patriarch
bio: Son of Emperor Michael I, made a monk after his father's deposition; as Patriarch of Constantinople he was deposed in 858 in favour of St. Photios and later restored, the two being reconciled before his death in 877.

name: St. Ignatius of Mariupol
title: Metropolitan
bio: Born on the island of Kythnos in 1716, he became Metropolitan of Gothia and Kafa in the Crimea. Fearing for his flock under the Crimean Khanate, in 1778 he led the Orthodox Greeks of the Crimea to the northern shore of the Sea of Azov, where they founded the city of Mariupol; he reposed there in 1786.

locations.label: Resettlement of his flock and burial — Mariupol

name: St. Igor of Chernigov and Kiev
title: Prince and Martyr
bio: Grand Prince of Kiev who, deposed in 1146, became a monk in Kiev; the following year a mob dragged him from church during the Divine Liturgy and murdered him.

name: St. Ildefonsus of Toledo
title: Archbishop
bio: Monk and archbishop of Toledo (657–667) who wrote a treatise on the perpetual virginity of the Theotokos; tradition tells of her appearing to him to bestow a vestment.

name: St. Ilia the Righteous (Chavchavadze)
title: Righteous
bio: Poet, writer and public figure who led the Georgian national revival of the 19th century and defended the Georgian Church; he was assassinated near Tsitsamuri in 1907 and glorified in 1987.

name: Sts. Ilie Iorest and Sava Brancovici
title: Metropolitans and Confessors
bio: Two 17th-century Metropolitans of Transylvania who defended Orthodoxy against Calvinist pressure and were deposed and imprisoned for it.

name: St. Illtud of Llantwit
title: Abbot
bio: Founder around 500 of the monastic school of Llanilltud Fawr (Llantwit Major) in Glamorgan, where Sts. David, Samson and Gildas are said to have been taught.

name: St. Ilya of Murom
title: Venerable
bio: A warrior from near Murom, celebrated in Russian epic songs as the bogatyr Ilya Muromets, who ended his life as a monk of the Kiev Caves; his relics rest in the Near Caves.

name: Sts. Indes, Domna and Companions of Nicomedia
title: Martyrs
bio: Members of the imperial court at Nicomedia burned alive in their church on the day of the Nativity feast.

name: St. Innocent of Alaska
title: Enlightener of the Aleuts and Apostle to America
bio: A missionary priest and later Metropolitan of Moscow who evangelized Alaska and the peoples of the Russian Far East.

name: St. Innocent of Irkutsk
title: Bishop
bio: The first Orthodox bishop of Irkutsk, a missionary to the peoples of Siberia and Mongolia.

name: Holy Innocents of Bethlehem
title: Martyrs
bio: The infants of Bethlehem and its surroundings killed on the orders of King Herod in his attempt to destroy the newborn Christ; the Church honours them as the first martyrs for Christ.

name: St. Ioan of Prislop
title: Venerable
bio: A 15th-century hermit and abbot of Prislop Monastery in Transylvania who lived in a small cell carved into the rock above the monastery.

name: St. Ioannikios the Great
title: Venerable
bio: Soldier turned hermit of Bithynian Olympus, a defender of the holy icons whose prayer 'My hope is the Father' entered the daily services.

name: St. Irenaeus of Lyons
title: Hieromartyr
bio: Bishop of Lyons and student of Polycarp, whose writings against heresies shaped early Christian theology.

name: St. Irenaeus of Sirmium
title: Hieromartyr, Bishop
bio: Young bishop of Sirmium who refused to sacrifice to idols despite the pleas of his family; he was beheaded and thrown from the bridge into the Sava in 304.

locations.label: Episcopal see and martyrdom — Sirmium (Sremska Mitrovica)

name: St. Irene Chrysovalantou
title: Venerable Abbess
bio: Byzantine abbess of the Chrysovalantou Monastery in Constantinople, noted for her humility, visions and wonder-working. She is venerated for the three fragrant apples of Paradise sent to her by St. John the Theologian through a sailor, and for the cypress trees said to have bowed during her prayer.

name: St. Irene the Great Martyr
title: Great Martyr
bio: A young woman converted by St. Timothy and martyred for destroying her family's idols and preaching Christ.

name: St. Irinarch of Rostov
title: Venerable, Recluse
bio: A peasant's son who became a monk at the Borisoglebsky Monastery near Rostov and lived there as a recluse for 38 years, bound in heavy chains. During the Time of Troubles he boldly rebuked the Polish invaders and in 1612 blessed Prince Pozharsky's militia on its way to liberate Moscow; he died in 1616.

name: St. Irinej of Novi Sad
title: Bishop and Confessor
bio: A twentieth-century Serbian bishop imprisoned and persecuted for defending the Church against fascist occupation.

name: St. Isaac the Confessor of Constantinople
title: Venerable, Confessor
bio: A Syrian hermit who rebuked the Arian emperor Valens and foretold his death at Adrianople, then founded one of the first monasteries of Constantinople, later known as that of Dalmatus.

name: St. Isaac the Recluse of the Kiev Caves
title: Venerable
bio: A wealthy merchant of Toropets named Chern, he gave away his goods and became a monk at the Kiev Caves, shutting himself in a cave cell for seven years. Deceived by demons who appeared to him as Christ and angels, he was left near death and nursed back to health by Sts. Anthony and Theodosius; he later overcame the demons through humility, living as a fool-for-Christ until his repose around 1090.

locations.label: Seclusion and repose — Kiev Caves Lavra

name: St. Isaac the Syrian
title: Venerable
bio: A bishop who resigned to live as a hermit, whose ascetic homilies remain treasured across Christian traditions.

name: Holy Prophet Isaiah
title: Prophet
bio: Prophet of Jerusalem whose foretelling of the Virgin who would bear Emmanuel and of the suffering Servant earned him the name of the evangelist among the prophets.

name: St. Isaiah of Rostov
title: Bishop
bio: A monk of the Kiev Caves who became bishop of Rostov in 1078 and travelled through the region preaching to the pagans and building churches; he died in 1090.

name: St. Isidora the Fool-for-Christ
title: Fool-for-Christ
bio: An Egyptian nun who feigned madness and endured mockery in a monastery kitchen, later revealed as a great saint by St. Piteroum.

name: St. Isidore I of Constantinople
title: Patriarch
bio: A hesychast monk elevated to the patriarchal throne, a close ally of St. Gregory Palamas during the Palamite disputes.

name: St. Isidore of Chios
title: Martyr
bio: An Alexandrian serving in the Roman fleet at Chios who refused to sacrifice to the gods and was beheaded in 251; his relics were later taken to Constantinople and, in part, to Venice.

name: St. Isidore of Pelusium
title: Venerable
bio: Egyptian ascetic and admirer of St. John Chrysostom, remembered for thousands of short letters of spiritual counsel.

name: St. Isidore of Rostov
title: Fool-for-Christ
bio: A foreigner who became a fool-for-Christ in Rostov in the 15th century, living in a hut of brushwood and praying through the nights; he was called 'Tverdislov' for the firmness of his words.

name: St. Isidore of Seville
title: Archbishop of Seville, Theologian
bio: Encyclopedist and Archbishop of Seville whose writings preserved classical learning for medieval Europe and helped unite the Visigothic kingdom in the Christian faith.

name: St. Ita of Killeedy
title: Venerable, Abbess
bio: A 6th-century Irish abbess who founded a community at Killeedy in Limerick and fostered young boys, among them, by tradition, St. Brendan the Navigator.

name: St. Ivan of Bohemia
title: Venerable, Hermit
bio: A 9th-century hermit who lived in a cave near the Berounka river; according to legend he was discovered during a hunt by Prince Bořivoj, the first Christian ruler of Bohemia.

name: St. Ivan of Rila's Disciple Luke
title: Monk
bio: A disciple of St. John of Rila who helped preserve the hesychast tradition of the Rila wilderness after his teacher's repose.

name: St. Jacob Netsvetov
title: Enlightener of the Peoples of Alaska
bio: First Alaska Native ordained to the priesthood, who translated the services into native languages and served the missions for decades.

name: St. James of Nisibis
title: Bishop
bio: Bishop of Nisibis and participant in the First Ecumenical Council, defender of the city against Persian siege through prayer.

name: St. James the Persian
title: Great Martyr
bio: A Persian courtier who denied Christ under pressure, then repented and endured being cut apart limb by limb for his faith.

locations.label: Place of martyrdom — Beth Lapat, Persia

name: Apostle James, Brother of the Lord
title: Apostle, First Bishop of Jerusalem
bio: Called the Brother of the Lord and 'the Just', he led the church of Jerusalem, presided over the Apostolic Council and wrote the Epistle of James; the oldest surviving Divine Liturgy bears his name. He was thrown from the pinnacle of the Temple and martyred around 62.

name: Apostle James, Son of Alphaeus
title: Apostle
bio: One of the Twelve Apostles who preached the Gospel in Judea and Egypt, where he was crucified for his faith.

name: Apostle James, Son of Zebedee
title: Apostle
bio: Brother of John the Theologian and one of the Twelve, the first Apostle to be martyred, beheaded in Jerusalem.

name: St. Januarius of Benevento
title: Hieromartyr, Bishop
bio: Bishop of Benevento beheaded at Pozzuoli under Diocletian around 305 after visiting imprisoned Christians; his relics, kept in Naples, are greatly venerated there.

name: St. Jarlath of Tuam
title: Bishop, Monastic Founder
bio: A 6th-century Irish abbot who founded a monastery and school at Tuam in Connacht, where St. Brendan of Clonfert and St. Colman are said to have studied under him. He is honoured as the first bishop of Tuam and its patron.

name: Sts. Jason and Sosipater
title: Apostles of the Seventy
bio: Kinsmen of St. Paul — Jason, bishop of Tarsus, and Sosipater of Iconium — who brought the Gospel to Corfu, where they converted Kerkyra, daughter of the island's ruler, who was martyred; they are honoured as the island's apostles.

name: Holy Prophet Jeremiah
title: Prophet
bio: One of the four major prophets, called as a youth at Anathoth, who warned Jerusalem of its coming fall to Babylon and lamented its destruction; tradition holds that he was stoned by his own people in Egypt.

name: St. Jerome of Stridon
title: Priest, Translator of Scripture
bio: Biblical scholar and ascetic renowned for translating the Scriptures into Latin while living near the grotto of the Nativity.

name: Sts. Joachim and Anna
title: Ancestors of God
bio: The righteous parents of the Theotokos, who, after years of childlessness, received the Virgin Mary as a gift from God in their old age.

name: St. Joachim of Osogovo
title: Venerable
bio: One of the 11th-century hermits of the region, together with Sts. Prochorus of Pčinja and Gabriel of Lesnovo; the Osogovo Monastery near Kriva Palanka grew up around his cave.

name: St. Joanikije of Devič
title: Venerable
bio: A 15th-century hermit who settled in the Drenica hills of Kosovo, where the Devič Monastery grew up around his cell and his healing relics.

name: St. Joasaph of Belgorod
title: Bishop
bio: An 18th-century Russian bishop renowned for his ascetic life, care for the poor, and incorrupt relics.

name: St. Joasaph of Meteora
title: Venerable
bio: John Uroš Palaiologos, son of the Serbian ruler Simeon Uroš, who briefly governed Thessaly before renouncing his throne around 1381 to become a monk under St. Athanasios at the Great Meteoron. He enlarged and endowed the monastery, which he led as its second founder until his death in the early 15th century.

locations.label: Monk and second founder — Great Meteoron

name: St. Joasaph of Tarnovo
title: Metropolitan
bio: A Bulgarian metropolitan and hesychast writer who continued the theological legacy of Patriarch Euthymius.

name: St. Joasaph, Bishop of Tver
title: Bishop
bio: A medieval bishop of Tver remembered in the Russian Church calendar for his pastoral diligence and piety.

name: St. Job of Moscow
title: First Patriarch of Moscow
bio: The first Patriarch of Moscow, deposed and exiled by the False Dmitry for refusing to recognise the pretender, ending his days in the monastery of his youth at Staritsa.

name: St. Job of Pochaev
title: Abbot, Wonderworker
bio: Abbot of the Pochaev Lavra who defended Orthodoxy in Ukraine against the pressures of the Union of Brest and is venerated as a great ascetic and wonderworker.

name: St. Job of Ugolsky Monastery
title: Monastic Founder
bio: Founder of a hermitage in the northern forests, remembered for his life of poverty and unceasing prayer.

name: St. Job the Much-Suffering
title: Righteous
bio: Righteous man of the land of Uz who lost his wealth, children and health yet did not curse God, and was restored twofold; the Church reads his book in Holy Week as an image of Christ's suffering.

locations.label: Land of Uz — traditional site at Sheikh Saad, Hauran, Syria

name: Holy Prophet Joel
title: Prophet
bio: Minor prophet who called Judah to fasting and repentance and foretold the outpouring of the Spirit 'upon all flesh', which St. Peter proclaimed fulfilled at Pentecost.

name: St. John 'Big Cap' of Moscow
title: Fool-for-Christ
bio: A fool-for-Christ from the Vologda region who wore heavy chains and a large cap, boldly rebuked Boris Godunov, and died in Moscow in 1589; he is buried in St. Basil's Cathedral.

name: St. John Calybites
title: Venerable
bio: Son of a wealthy Constantinopolitan family who secretly became a monk among the Akoimetoi and, returning home unrecognized, lived as a beggar in a hut by his parents' gate until his death in the 5th century.

locations.label: Hut by his parents' house — Constantinople

name: St. John Cassian
title: Venerable
bio: A monk who studied under the Desert Fathers and brought Egyptian monastic teaching to the Latin West.

locations.label: Ordained deacon by St. John Chrysostom — Constantinople

name: St. John Chrysostom
title: Archbishop of Constantinople
bio: Renowned preacher and Archbishop of Constantinople, celebrated for his eloquence and his liturgy still used in the Orthodox Church today.

name: St. John Chrysostom, New Confessor of Etna
title: Bishop
bio: A twentieth-century American hierarch remembered for his defense of the traditional Orthodox calendar and ascetic life.

name: St. John Climacus
title: Venerable
bio: Abbot of Sinai and author of 'The Ladder of Divine Ascent,' a foundational text of Orthodox spirituality.

name: St. John Jacob the Chozebite
title: Venerable
bio: A Romanian monk of Neamț Monastery who settled in the Holy Land in 1936 and lived as a hermit near the Monastery of St. George of Choziba; his body, found incorrupt in 1980, rests there.

locations.label: Hermitage and relics — Choziba Monastery, Judean Desert

name: St. John Kochurov, Protopriest and Martyr
title: Priest and Martyr
bio: A Russian priest who served missions in America before returning to Russia, becoming the first clergy martyr of the Bolshevik era.

name: St. John Koukouzelis
title: Hymnographer
bio: A gifted Byzantine chanter who left the imperial court to become a monk on Mount Athos, composing hymns still sung today.

name: St. John Lampadistis
title: Venerable, Wonderworker
bio: An 11th-century ascetic born in the lost village of Lampadou near present-day Galata in the Marathasa valley of Cyprus. Refusing the marriage arranged by his parents, he devoted himself to prayer and asceticism, lost his sight, and died young. His relics are venerated at the Monastery of St. John Lampadistis in Kalopanagiotis, whose painted churches are a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and he is widely invoked for healing.

name: St. John of Beverley
title: Bishop
bio: Bishop of Hexham and then of York, renowned for his healings and care for the poor, who ordained St. Bede and founded the monastery at Beverley, where he died in 721.

name: St. John of Damascus
title: Venerable
bio: A monk and hymnographer of Mar Saba whose writings defended icons and systematized Orthodox theology.

name: St. John of Gothia
title: Bishop and Confessor
bio: Bishop of Gothia in the Crimea who defended the holy icons during the iconoclast period, led his people in a revolt against Khazar rule and died in exile at Amastris around 790.

name: St. John of Kronstadt
title: Righteous
bio: A married parish priest renowned for his fervent liturgical life, healings, and care for the poor of Kronstadt.

locations.label: Burial — St. John Convent, St. Petersburg

name: St. John of Lycopolis
title: Venerable
bio: A hermit who lived walled into a cell near Lycopolis in the Thebaid for some fifty years, renowned for his gift of prophecy; he foretold victory to Emperor Theodosius the Great and died around 394.

name: St. John of Novgorod
title: Archbishop
bio: Archbishop of Novgorod (1163–1186), through whose prayers before the Icon of the Sign the city was delivered from a Suzdalian siege in 1170; folk tradition tells of his journey to Jerusalem on the back of a demon he had bound.

name: St. John of Rila
title: Venerable
bio: Bulgaria's patron saint, a hermit whose cave and later monastery became the spiritual heart of Bulgarian monasticism.

name: St. John of Shanghai and San Francisco
title: Wonderworker of Shanghai and San Francisco
bio: Ascetic bishop of the Russian diaspora renowned for his humility and miracles, who cared for orphans in Shanghai and led the Church in Western Europe and San Francisco.

name: St. John of Tobolsk
title: Metropolitan
bio: A Ukrainian-born metropolitan of Siberia known for missionary outreach and theological writings among the Siberian peoples.

name: St. John of Ustyug, Fool-for-Christ
title: Fool-for-Christ
bio: A fifteenth-century ascetic of Veliky Ustyug renowned for enduring extreme cold and heat as feats of asceticism.

name: St. John of Zedazeni
title: Monastic Founder
bio: Leader of the Thirteen Syrian Fathers who came to Georgia in the sixth century to strengthen monastic life in the region.

name: St. John the Almsgiver
title: Patriarch of Alexandria
bio: Patriarch of Alexandria renowned for his extraordinary generosity to the poor, distributing the wealth of his see to the needy and refugees of his time.

name: St. John the Baptist
title: Prophet, Forerunner, Baptist
bio: The last of the Old Testament prophets and Forerunner of Christ, he proclaimed repentance in the Judean desert, baptized Jesus in the Jordan, and was martyred by Herod Antipas at the request of Salome. He holds the unique liturgical title “Greater than the prophets.”

locations.label: Baptism of Christ — Qasr al-Yahud, Jordan River

name: St. John the Dwarf
title: Venerable
bio: Desert father of Scetis famous for his obedience — watering a dry stick daily at his elder's word — and for many sayings preserved in the Gerontikon.

name: St. John the Faster
title: Patriarch
bio: Patriarch of Constantinople (582–595), renowned for his strict fasting and almsgiving; a penitential rule long attributed to him shaped the Byzantine practice of confession.

name: St. John the Hesychast
title: Bishop and Monk of Palestine
bio: A bishop of Colonia in Armenia who relinquished his see to become a silent monk at the Great Lavra of St. Sabbas near Jerusalem.

locations.label: Monastic life — Great Lavra of St. Sabbas

name: St. John the Iberian
title: Venerable, Monastic Founder
bio: A Georgian nobleman who left his family to become a monk, settled on Mount Athos with his son St. Euthymius and founded the Iviron Monastery around 980 with the help of the general John Tornikios.

name: St. John the Much-Suffering
title: Venerable
bio: A monk of the Kiev Caves who fought for many years against temptations of the flesh, at one point burying himself up to the shoulders in the earth of the cave through Great Lent; he died around 1160.

name: St. John the New Martyr of Epirus
title: Martyr
bio: A young Epirote executed for confessing Christianity after a period of forced conversion to Islam.

name: St. John the New of Suceava
title: Merchant and Martyr
bio: A Trapezuntine merchant martyred at Cetatea Albă whose relics are enshrined at Suceava in Romania.

name: St. John the Prophet of Gaza
title: Ascetic
bio: A recluse of Gaza and spiritual collaborator of St. Barsanuphius, renowned for discernment and prophetic counsel.

name: St. John the Russian
title: Confessor
bio: A Russian soldier enslaved by the Ottomans who kept his faith secretly in Asia Minor, later revered for many miracles.

name: St. John the Tailor of Thassos
title: Martyr
bio: A Thassian tailor martyred at Thessaloniki after boldly renouncing his coerced conversion to Islam.

name: Apostle and Evangelist John the Theologian
title: Apostle, Evangelist and Theologian
bio: Beloved disciple of Christ, author of the Fourth Gospel, three Epistles and the Book of Revelation, who reposed peacefully in old age at Ephesus.

name: St. John the Wallachian
title: New Martyr
bio: A young Wallachian taken captive by Ottoman troops in 1662 who, in Constantinople, resisted his master's advances and refused to deny Christ, and was hanged.

name: St. John Vladimir of Serbia
title: Martyr Prince
bio: A pious ruler of Duklja betrayed and beheaded, venerated across the Balkans for his mercy toward his enemies.

name: Holy Prophet Jonah
title: Prophet
bio: Prophet from Gath-hepher in Galilee who fled God's call, spent three days in the belly of the great fish — a sign Christ applied to His own burial and Resurrection — and then preached repentance to Nineveh.

name: St. Jonah of Hankou
title: Bishop
bio: A Russian émigré bishop who served the Orthodox community of Hankou, China, in the early twentieth century.

name: St. Jonah of Moscow
title: Metropolitan
bio: The first Metropolitan of Moscow elected independently of Constantinople, establishing the autocephaly of the Russian Church.

name: St. Joseph of Alaverdi
title: Venerable, Monastic Founder
bio: One of the Thirteen Syrian Fathers who came to Georgia in the 6th century with St. John of Zedazeni. He settled in the empty Alaverdi steppe of Kakheti, where he lived as a hermit, gathered disciples and founded a monastery; he reposed around 570, and the great Alaverdi Cathedral was later built on the site.

name: St. Joseph of Arimathea
title: Righteous
bio: A secret disciple of Christ who donated his own tomb for the Lord's burial after the Crucifixion.

locations.label: Donated tomb for Christ's burial — Jerusalem

name: St. Joseph of Damascus
title: Priest and Martyr
bio: A married priest, scholar and teacher who led the Orthodox school of the Patriarchate of Antioch in Damascus. During the massacre of Christians in July 1860 he sheltered his flock in the cathedral, gave them Communion and was killed while encouraging them; he was glorified by the Church of Antioch in 1993.

name: St. Joseph of Optina
title: Elder
bio: Cell-attendant and successor of St. Ambrose of Optina, revered as a wise and gentle spiritual father.

name: St. Joseph of Volokolamsk
title: Abbot and Theologian
bio: Founder of Volokolamsk Monastery and defender of monastic land ownership and rigorous communal discipline.

name: St. Joseph the Betrothed
title: Guardian of the Theotokos
bio: The righteous carpenter of Nazareth entrusted with the care of the Virgin Mary and the Christ Child.

name: St. Joseph the Hesychast
title: Venerable
bio: A 20th-century Athonite elder whose disciples revitalized many monasteries of Mount Athos.

name: St. Joseph the Hymnographer
title: Venerable
bio: Sicilian-born monk of Constantinople who composed a vast number of canons still sung in the Orthodox services.

name: St. Joseph the New of Partoș
title: Bishop
bio: A Metropolitan of Timișoara known for his ascetic life and miracles attributed to his incorrupt relics.

name: St. Joshua, Son of Nun
title: Righteous
bio: Successor of Moses who led Israel across the Jordan into the Promised Land, took Jericho and divided the land among the tribes; his name is the Hebrew form of 'Jesus'.

locations.label: Crossing of the Jordan — near Jericho

name: Apostle Jude, Brother of the Lord
title: Apostle
bio: Author of the Epistle of Jude, counted among the Twelve and called the Brother of the Lord, who preached in Judea, Mesopotamia and Persia and, according to tradition, was crucified in Armenia.

locations.label: Martyrdom by tradition — Ararat region, Armenia

name: Sts. Julian and Basilissa
title: Martyrs
bio: A married couple of Antinoë in Egypt who lived in virginity, turned their home into a refuge for the sick and needy and led monastic communities; Basilissa reposed in peace and Julian was martyred under Diocletian.

name: St. Julian of Emesa
title: Martyr
bio: A Syrian martyr of Emesa dragged through the city by a wild horse for his confession of Christ.

name: St. Julian of Le Mans
title: Bishop
bio: The first bishop of Le Mans, sent according to tradition to preach the Gospel to the Cenomani of Gaul in the 3rd or 4th century. He is honoured as the apostle of the region, and the city's great cathedral is dedicated to him.

name: St. Julian of Tarsus
title: Martyr
bio: A young Cilician Christian who was tortured for a year and drowned in the sea at Aegae for refusing to renounce Christ.

name: St. Julian Saba
title: Venerable
bio: A hermit of Osrhoene who lived in a cave near Edessa on bread and salt and in old age travelled to Antioch to strengthen the Orthodox against the Arians; he died around 377.

locations.label: Visit to strengthen the Orthodox — Antioch

name: St. Juliana Lazarevskaya
title: Righteous
bio: A pious sixteenth-century Russian noblewoman renowned for her charity to the poor during years of famine.

name: St. Juliana of Nicomedia
title: Great Martyr
bio: A young Christian woman tortured and beheaded at Nicomedia after refusing to marry a pagan official and to renounce her faith.

name: Sts. Julitta and Cyricus
title: Martyrs
bio: A mother and her young son martyred together at Tarsus during the persecution of Diocletian.

name: St. Julitta of Caesarea
title: Martyr
bio: A wealthy widow of Caesarea in Cappadocia who went to court to recover property seized by a powerful man. When he accused her of being a Christian, she refused to sacrifice to the idols and was burned around 304; St. Basil the Great praised her in a homily.

name: Sts. Justa and Rufina
title: Virgin Martyrs
bio: Two sisters, potters of Seville, who refused to sell their wares for a pagan festival and broke an idol of Venus; they were tortured and died in prison around 287.

name: St. Justin (Popović) of Ćelije
title: New Chrysostom of Serbia
bio: Serbian theologian and monk celebrated for his writings on Orthodox dogmatics, who spent his final decades confined to Ćelije Monastery.

name: St. Justin the Philosopher
title: Martyr
bio: A pagan philosopher converted to Christianity who defended the faith in his writings before being martyred in Rome.

name: Apostle Justus (Joseph Barsabbas)
title: Apostle of the Seventy
bio: Joseph called Barsabbas, surnamed Justus, had followed Christ from the baptism of John and was put forward with Matthias to take the place of Judas among the Twelve (Acts 1:23). Tradition counts him among the Seventy and makes him bishop of Eleutheropolis in Judea, where he suffered for the faith.

locations.label: Casting of lots for the Twelfth Apostle — Jerusalem

name: St. Juvenal of Jerusalem
title: Patriarch of Jerusalem
bio: Bishop of Jerusalem from about 422 to 458. At the Council of Chalcedon in 451 his see was raised to the rank of a patriarchate; on his return he was briefly driven out by monks opposed to the council, but was restored and governed the Church of Jerusalem until his death.

name: St. Juvenaly of Alaska
title: Protomartyr of America
bio: Missionary hieromonk of the first Alaskan mission, killed while preaching the Gospel in the interior — the first martyr of the Orthodox Church in America.

locations.label: Place of martyrdom — Lake Iliamna region

name: St. Kallinikos of Edessa
title: Bishop
bio: A twentieth-century Greek metropolitan renowned for pastoral devotion and defense of Orthodoxy in Macedonia.

name: St. Kassiani the Hymnographer
title: Hymnographer
bio: A learned Byzantine abbess and poet, famed for composing the Hymn of Kassiani sung during Holy Week, one of the few works by a woman in the Orthodox liturgical tradition.

name: St. Kenelm of Mercia
title: Prince and Martyr
bio: A young prince of Mercia, son of King Coenwulf, who according to legend was murdered in 811 at the instigation of his jealous sister and buried secretly in the Clent Hills. The finding of his body was attended by miracles, and his shrine at Winchcombe Abbey became one of the most popular pilgrimages of Anglo-Saxon England.

name: St. Kentigern (Mungo) of Glasgow
title: Bishop
bio: Apostle of Strathclyde and first bishop of Glasgow, who evangelized the Britons of southwestern Scotland and Cumbria.

name: St. Ketevan the Queen
title: Great Martyr, Queen of Kakheti
