bio: Queen of Kakheti who was held captive in Persia and tortured to death for refusing to renounce Christ.

name: St. Kevin of Glendalough
title: Abbot of Glendalough
bio: Irish hermit whose life of prayer amid the wilderness of Glendalough attracted disciples and gave rise to a great monastic settlement.

name: St. Kilian of Würzburg
title: Hieromartyr, Bishop
bio: An Irish missionary bishop to Franconia who was martyred at Würzburg around 689 with his companions Colman and Totnan.

name: St. Kornily of Pskov-Caves
title: Abbot and Martyr
bio: Abbot who greatly expanded the Pskov-Caves Monastery and was struck down by Ivan the Terrible, later glorified as a martyr.

name: St. Kuksha of Odessa
title: Venerable, Elder
bio: A monk who spent many years on Mount Athos and at the Kiev Caves, endured Soviet labour camps, and in his last years at the Dormition Monastery in Odessa guided many; he died in 1964.

locations.label: Last years and relics — Dormition Monastery, Odessa

name: St. Kuksha of the Kiev Caves
title: Hieromartyr, Enlightener of the Vyatichi
bio: A monk of the Kiev Caves Lavra who went with his disciple Nikon to preach to the pagan Vyatichi in the forests along the Oka River. He worked many miracles and baptized many, but was beheaded by pagan priests around 1115 near present-day Mtsensk.

name: St. Kyranna of Thessaloniki
title: Martyr
bio: Young Christian woman from Ossa near Thessaloniki, martyred in Thessaloniki in 1751 at the age of 20 after being pressured to renounce Christ.

name: St. Kyriaki the Great Martyr
title: Great Martyr
bio: A young woman of Nicomedia tortured extensively but preserved by God before dying peacefully in prayer.

name: St. Lambert of Maastricht
title: Hieromartyr, Bishop
bio: Bishop of Maastricht who evangelized northern Brabant and was killed at Liège around 705; his shrine made Liège a great place of pilgrimage.

name: St. Laurence of Kaluga
title: Fool-for-Christ
bio: A holy fool who lived by the walls of Kaluga, credited with defending the city from Tatar and Polish raids through prayer.

name: St. Lavrentiy of Chernigov
title: Venerable, Elder
bio: A hieroschemamonk of the Trinity Monastery in Chernigov, a choir director and beloved spiritual father who endured the Soviet persecutions and reopened a convent during the Second World War; he died in 1950.

name: St. Lawrence of Rome
title: Archdeacon and Martyr
bio: A deacon of Rome martyred on a gridiron for distributing the Church's wealth to the poor rather than surrendering it to the state.

name: St. Lazar of Serbia
title: Martyr Prince
bio: Prince of Serbia who fell at the Battle of Kosovo, revered as a martyr for choosing the heavenly kingdom.

name: St. Lazarus of Mount Galesion
title: Venerable, Stylite
bio: An 11th-century stylite who, after a pilgrimage to Jerusalem, stood on pillars for decades on Mount Galesion near Ephesus while guiding the monasteries that grew up around him.

name: St. Lazarus of the Four Days
title: Righteous
bio: Friend of Christ raised from the dead after four days, who later served as bishop of Kition in Cyprus.

name: St. Lazarus the Iconographer
title: Venerable, Iconographer
bio: A monk and painter of Constantinople who kept painting icons under the iconoclast Emperor Theophilus. Tortured and with his palms burned by red-hot iron, he recovered and painted again, including an icon of St. John the Forerunner; after the Triumph of Orthodoxy in 843 he was sent as an envoy to Rome and died on a later journey there around 867.

name: St. Leander of Seville
title: Archbishop of Seville
bio: Elder brother of St. Isidore, he converted the Visigothic royal family from Arianism to Christianity and strengthened the Church in Spain as Archbishop of Seville.

name: St. Lebuin of Deventer
title: Missionary
bio: An English monk who went to the Frisians and Saxons in the 8th century and built a church at Deventer on the IJssel. He boldly preached at the Saxons' assembly at Marklo, escaping death only narrowly, and was buried in Deventer, where the great Lebuinuskerk bears his name.

name: St. Leger of Autun
title: Bishop and Martyr
bio: Abbot of Saint-Maixent near Poitiers and then bishop of Autun, who reformed his diocese and cared for the poor. Caught up in the struggles of the Frankish court, he was blinded and mutilated by the mayor of the palace Ebroin and finally beheaded around 679.

name: St. Leo of Catania
title: Bishop, Wonderworker
bio: Bishop of Catania in Sicily in the 8th century, famed for his charity and for confronting the sorcerer Heliodorus, whom he bound with his omophorion and led to the fire.

name: St. Leo the Great
title: Pope of Rome
bio: Bishop of Rome whose Tome helped define Orthodox Christology at the Council of Chalcedon.

name: St. Leocadia of Toledo
title: Virgin Martyr
bio: A young Christian of Toledo imprisoned under Diocletian who died in her cell around 304 after hearing of the martyrdom of St. Eulalia; she is the patron saint of Toledo.

name: St. Leonard of Noblac
title: Venerable, Hermit
bio: A Frankish nobleman said to have been baptized by St. Remigius, who declined a bishopric and lived as a hermit in the forest near Limoges in the 6th century. Granted land by the king, he founded a monastery at Noblac and was famed for his care for prisoners, becoming their patron saint.

name: St. Leonid of Optina
title: Venerable, Elder of Optina
bio: The first of the great elders of Optina, who despite opposition opened the monastery's doors to crowds of pilgrims seeking counsel and confession.

name: Sts. Leonides and Companions of Corinth
title: Martyrs
bio: Leonides and seven women — Chariessa, Nike, Galina, Kallis, Nunechia, Basilissa and Theodora — who sang hymns as they were cast into the sea off Corinth in the 3rd century.

name: St. Leontios of Arcadia
title: Martyr
bio: An Arcadian villager martyred by Ottoman authorities for defending his Christian faith in the eighteenth century.

name: St. Leontius of Rădăuți
title: Venerable
bio: A 14th-century Moldavian hermit and monastic founder near Rădăuți, whose relics were placed in the Bogdana Church there, the oldest stone church in Moldavia.

name: St. Leonty of Rostov
title: Hieromartyr, Bishop
bio: A monk of the Kiev Caves, Greek by birth, sent as bishop to Rostov, where he preached among the pagan Merya people; he was killed by pagans around 1073, and his incorrupt relics were found in 1164.

name: Apostle Linus
title: Apostle of the Seventy, Bishop of Rome
bio: Greeted by Paul in his Second Epistle to Timothy (4:21), Linus was, according to St. Irenaeus, the one to whom the Apostles Peter and Paul entrusted the church of Rome, making him its first bishop after them. Tradition holds that he ended his life as a martyr.

name: St. Lioba of Tauberbischofsheim
title: Venerable, Abbess
bio: An English nun and kinswoman of St. Boniface who led the convent of Tauberbischofsheim and guided many communities of women in Germany; she died in 782.

name: St. Longinus of Koryazhma
title: Monastic Founder
bio: Founder of a monastery at the confluence of the Koryazhma and Vychegda rivers, known for humility and labor.

name: St. Longinus the Centurion
title: Martyr
bio: The centurion who stood at the Cross and confessed 'Truly this was the Son of God', later preaching Christ in his native Cappadocia, where he was beheaded.

locations.label: Confession at the Cross — Golgotha, Jerusalem

name: St. Luarsab II of Kartli
title: King and Martyr
bio: A seventeenth-century Georgian king martyred in Persian captivity for refusing to abandon Orthodoxy.

name: St. Lucian of Antioch
title: Hieromartyr, Presbyter
bio: Priest and scholar of Antioch who prepared a revised text of the Greek Scriptures used throughout the East; starved and tortured in Nicomedia, he died in 312, and his body, cast into the sea, was recovered at Drepanum (Helenopolis).

name: Sts. Lucillian and Paula
title: Martyrs
bio: Lucillian, an aged pagan priest of Nicomedia, converted to Christ and was imprisoned there under Emperor Aurelian, where he strengthened four young Christians — Claudius, Hypatius, Paul and Dionysius. Taken to Byzantium, the youths were beheaded and Lucillian was crucified; the virgin Paula, who had cared for the imprisoned martyrs, was beheaded there soon after.

name: St. Lucy of Syracuse
title: Virgin Martyr
bio: A young Christian of Syracuse who distributed her dowry to the poor and was denounced by her rejected suitor. She was martyred during the persecution of Diocletian around 304; her relics were later taken to Constantinople and then to Venice.

name: St. Ludger of Münster
title: Bishop
bio: A Frisian pupil of Alcuin who evangelized Frisia and Saxony, founded the abbey of Werden and became the first bishop of Münster; he died in 809.

name: St. Ludmila of Bohemia
title: Right-Believing Princess, Martyr
bio: Bohemian princess who taught the Christian faith to her grandson St. Wenceslaus and was strangled at the instigation of her daughter-in-law.

name: Apostle and Evangelist Luke
title: Apostle and Evangelist
bio: A physician and companion of Paul who wrote the Gospel of Luke and the Acts of the Apostles.

name: St. Luke of Crimea (Voino-Yasenetsky)
title: Bishop and Confessor
bio: A surgeon and archbishop who continued practicing medicine and healing the sick even through Soviet imprisonment and exile.

name: St. Luke of Mytilene, New Martyr
title: Martyr
bio: A young shoemaker of Mytilene martyred for reclaiming his Christian faith before Ottoman judges.

name: St. Luke of Steiris
title: Venerable
bio: A Byzantine hermit whose monastery in Phocis became one of the great architectural treasures of Greece.

name: St. Luke the Stylite
title: Venerable, Stylite
bio: A Byzantine soldier who became a monk after a battle against the Bulgarians and lived for some forty years on a pillar at Chalcedon, dying in 979.

name: St. Lupus of Thessaloniki
title: Martyr
bio: The servant of St. Demetrius who dipped his master's ring and robe in his blood and worked miracles before his own martyrdom.

name: St. Lupus of Troyes
title: Bishop
bio: Bishop of Troyes for over fifty years who went with St. Germanus of Auxerre to Britain to oppose Pelagianism and, by tradition, met Attila the Hun in 451 and saved his city.

name: St. Lydia of Thyatira
title: Equal-to-the-Apostles
bio: A seller of purple cloth from Thyatira who heard the Apostle Paul preach by the river at Philippi and became the first recorded convert in Europe (Acts 16). She was baptized with her household and opened her home to the apostles.

name: St. Macarius of Alexandria
title: Ascetic of the Egyptian Desert
bio: A contemporary and namesake of St. Makarios of Egypt, this Alexandrian priest embraced extreme asceticism in the desert of Nitria and Scetis.

name: St. Macarius of Kalyazin
title: Venerable
bio: A 15th-century nobleman from near Kashin who became a monk after the death of his wife and founded the Holy Trinity Monastery at Kalyazin on the Volga. Known as a wonderworker, he reposed in 1483; his monastery was later flooded by the Uglich Reservoir.

name: St. Macarius of Moscow
title: Metropolitan
bio: Archbishop of Novgorod and then Metropolitan of Moscow (1542–1563), who compiled the Great Menaion Reader of saints' Lives and led councils that glorified many Russian saints.

name: St. Macarius of Optina
title: Venerable
bio: An elder of Optina Hermitage who revived the publication of Patristic texts and guided countless pilgrims.

name: St. Macarius of Unzha
title: Monastic Founder
bio: A monk of the Nizhny Novgorod region who founded monasteries and was revered as a wonderworker among the Volga peoples.

name: Holy Maccabean Martyrs
title: Martyrs
bio: The aged scribe Eleazar, seven brothers and their mother Solomonia, who under the Seleucid king Antiochus IV chose death rather than break the Law of God; the Church honours them as martyrs of the Old Testament.

name: St. Machar of Aberdeen
title: Bishop, Missionary
bio: An Irish companion of St. Columba on Iona who was sent to preach to the Picts of the north-east of Scotland in the 6th century. According to tradition he founded a church by the River Don at a bend shaped like a bishop's crozier, the site of St. Machar's Cathedral in Aberdeen.

locations.label: Mission and church — St. Machar's Cathedral, Aberdeen

name: St. Macrina the Younger
title: Venerable
bio: Elder sister and teacher of Sts. Basil the Great and Gregory of Nyssa, who turned the family estate into a monastic community for women.

locations.label: Monastery and place of repose — Annisa, near Neocaesarea

name: St. Maelrubha of Applecross
title: Abbot, Missionary
bio: An Irish monk of Bangor who sailed to Scotland in 671 and founded the monastery of Applecross on the west coast. For half a century he preached among the Picts of the north-west Highlands and the islands, dying at Applecross in 722.

name: St. Makarios Notaras of Corinth
title: Bishop of Corinth
bio: Bishop who gathered the texts of the Philokalia with St. Nikodemos, a leading figure of the Kollyvades movement for liturgical and patristic renewal.

name: St. Makarios of Egypt
title: Venerable, Desert Father
bio: A disciple of St. Anthony the Great who settled in the Scetis desert of Egypt and became one of the most celebrated Desert Fathers, attracting thousands of monks to the Wadi Natrun. He is the reputed author of the Fifty Spiritual Homilies on the life of inner prayer.

locations.label: Monastic life and relics — Wadi el-Natrun (Scetis)

name: St. Maksim Branković
title: Archbishop
bio: Son of the blind Despot Stefan Branković and St. Angelina, who became a monk and then Archbishop of Wallachia, mediating peace between Wallachia and Moldavia; he founded the Krušedol Monastery, where he rests.

locations.label: Monastery and relics — Krušedol, Fruška Gora

name: Holy Prophet Malachi
title: Prophet
bio: Last of the twelve minor prophets, who foretold the messenger sent to prepare the way of the Lord — a prophecy fulfilled in St. John the Baptist.

name: St. Malo of Aleth
title: Bishop
bio: A monk born in Wales and, according to tradition, a pupil of St. Brendan, who crossed to Brittany and became the first bishop of Aleth, from which the city of Saint-Malo takes its name. Driven out for a time by opponents, he died in exile in Saintonge around 621.

name: St. Mamas of Caesarea
title: Martyr
bio: A shepherd-martyr of Cappadocia said to have lived among wild beasts before his martyrdom under Emperor Aurelian.

name: Sts. Manuel, Sabel and Ismael
title: Martyrs
bio: Three Christian brothers of Persian noble birth, sent by the Persian king as envoys to Emperor Julian the Apostate, who refused to take part in pagan sacrifice and were beheaded near Chalcedon in 362.

name: St. Marcellus the Centurion
title: Martyr
bio: A Roman centurion in Tangier who publicly renounced his military oath rather than honor pagan gods and was executed.

name: St. Marcellus the Unsleeping
title: Venerable, Abbot
bio: Abbot of the Akoimetoi monastery near Constantinople in the 5th century, under whom the community's ceaseless worship flourished; he took part in the synod that condemned Eutyches.

locations.label: Monastery of the Akoimetoi — Gomon on the Bosphorus

name: St. Marcian of Cyrrhus
title: Venerable
bio: A nobleman of Cyrrhus who became a hermit in the desert of Chalcis in Syria, living in a tiny enclosure; Theodoret of Cyrrhus records him among the great ascetics of the 4th century.

name: St. Marcian the Emperor
title: Emperor
bio: Emperor of the East (450–457) and husband of St. Pulcheria, who convened the Fourth Ecumenical Council at Chalcedon in 451 and upheld its definition of faith.

name: St. Marcian the Treasurer
title: Priest
bio: A wealthy priest and imperial treasurer of Constantinople who used his fortune to build and restore churches.

name: St. Mardarije of Libertyville
title: Bishop of America and Canada
bio: First Serbian bishop for America and Canada, who organised the scattered immigrant parishes and founded the monastery of St. Sava at Libertyville, where he is buried.

name: St. Mardarius of Sebaste
title: Martyr
bio: A martyr of Sebaste in Armenia, remembered for his steadfast confession of faith under torture.

name: St. Maria of Paris
title: New Martyr of Paris
bio: Russian émigré nun who sheltered Jews and resistance members in Nazi-occupied Paris, dying in the Ravensbrück concentration camp.

name: St. Marina the Great Martyr
title: Great Martyr
bio: A young woman of Antioch in Pisidia tortured and beheaded for her faith, widely venerated across the Orthodox world.

locations.label: Place of martyrdom — Antioch of Pisidia

name: St. Marina the Monk
title: Venerable
bio: When her widowed father entered a monastery, Marina cut her hair and joined him disguised as the monk Marinos. Falsely accused of fathering an innkeeper's child, she accepted expulsion in silence and raised the boy outside the monastery gate; only at her death did the brethren discover that she was a woman. Lebanese tradition places her life at Qannoubine in the Qadisha Valley.

locations.label: Monastic life (Lebanese tradition) — Qannoubine, Qadisha Valley

name: Apostle and Evangelist Mark
title: Apostle and Evangelist
bio: Author of the Gospel of Mark and founder of the Church of Alexandria, martyred by being dragged through the streets.

name: St. Mark of Arethusa
title: Hieromartyr, Bishop
bio: Bishop of Arethusa in Syria who had torn down a pagan temple under Constantius; under Julian the Apostate the townspeople tortured him, smeared him with honey and left him to the wasps, yet he refused to pay even a coin toward its rebuilding.

name: St. Mark of Ephesus
title: Metropolitan and Confessor
bio: Metropolitan of Ephesus and the sole bishop who refused to sign the union with Rome at the Council of Ferrara-Florence (1439), becoming the champion of Orthodoxy there.

name: St. Mark the Grave-Digger
title: Venerable
bio: A monk of the Kiev Caves in the 11th century who dug the cave tombs of the brethren; his Life tells how even the departed obeyed his word when a grave proved too narrow.

name: St. Markella of Chios
title: Virgin Martyr
bio: A young woman of Chios martyred by her own father when she refused an incestuous proposal, fleeing into the mountains.

name: St. Maron of Syria
title: Venerable
bio: A 4th-century hermit who lived in the open air on a mountain near Cyrrhus in Syria, healing the sick and guiding many disciples; the monastic movement he inspired gave its name to the Maronite tradition.

name: Sts. Martha and Mary of Bethany
title: Righteous
bio: Sisters of Lazarus who hosted Christ in their home in Bethany, models of hospitality and devotion.

name: St. Martial of Limoges
title: Bishop, Enlightener of Aquitaine
bio: First bishop of Limoges in the 3rd century, one of the missionary bishops sent from Rome to evangelize Gaul. His tomb became a great pilgrimage centre around which the Abbey of St. Martial grew.

name: St. Martin of Braga
title: Archbishop of Braga
bio: Pannonian-born monk and Archbishop of Braga who led the conversion of the Suebi kingdom from Arianism and wrote widely read moral treatises.

name: St. Martin of Tours
title: Bishop
bio: A former Roman soldier who became bishop of Tours, famed for cutting his cloak in half to clothe a beggar.

name: St. Martin the Confessor, Pope of Rome
title: Pope and Confessor
bio: Pope of Rome who convened the Lateran Council of 649 condemning Monothelitism; arrested on the emperor's orders, he was tried in Constantinople and exiled to Cherson in Crimea, where he died of hunger in 655.

name: St. Martina of Rome
title: Virgin Martyr
bio: A deaconess and daughter of a Roman consul who gave her inheritance to the poor and, under Alexander Severus, endured many tortures before being beheaded around 228.

name: St. Martinian of Belozersk
title: Venerable, Abbot
bio: A disciple of St. Cyril of Belozersk who founded a monastery on Lake Vozhe, later served as abbot of the Trinity–St. Sergius Lavra and ended his life at the Ferapontov Monastery in 1483.

name: St. Martinian of Caesarea
title: Venerable
bio: A hermit near Caesarea in Palestine who, fleeing temptation, lived for years on a rock in the sea and later wandered until his repose in Athens around 422.

name: St. Marutha of Martyropolis
title: Bishop
bio: Bishop of Maipherqat in Mesopotamia and a skilled physician, he was sent by the Roman emperor as envoy to the Persian shah Yazdegerd I, whose trust he won by healing him. He helped secure freedom of worship for the Church in Persia at the Council of Seleucia-Ctesiphon in 410 and brought back so many relics of Persian martyrs that his city became known as Martyropolis.

name: St. Mary Magdalene
title: Myrrhbearer and Equal-to-the-Apostles
bio: A devoted follower of Christ, first witness of His Resurrection, later a missionary who reposed in Ephesus.

name: St. Mary of Cappadocia, Grandmother of Basil
title: Righteous
bio: Grandmother of St. Basil the Great who preserved the faith through the persecutions of Galerius and Licinius in Pontus.

name: St. Mary of Egypt
title: Venerable
bio: A former sinner who repented and lived decades alone in the desert beyond the Jordan, becoming a model of repentance and asceticism.

locations.label: Desert of repentance — beyond the Jordan
Conversion before the Holy Cross — Jerusalem

name: The Theotokos, Mary the Mother of God
title: Mother of God
bio: The Virgin Mary, Mother of God, whose Dormition (falling asleep) is commemorated as one of the Church's greatest feasts.

locations.label: Nativity of the Theotokos — Jerusalem (Church of St. Anne)

name: St. Mary the Younger of Bizye
title: Righteous Martyr
bio: A pious noblewoman of Thrace who endured domestic abuse with patience and was glorified for miracles after her death.

name: St. Matrona of Chios
title: Nun
bio: Founder of a women's monastery on Chios, celebrated for visions of the Theotokos and a life of strict asceticism.

name: St. Matrona of Moscow
title: Righteous
bio: A blind and paralyzed woman renowned for her prophetic gifts and healings during some of Russia's darkest years.

name: St. Matrona of Perge
title: Venerable
bio: A married woman of Perge in Pamphylia who left for Constantinople, lived disguised as the monk Babylas in the monastery of St. Bassianus and later founded a women's monastery there; she died around 492, nearly a hundred years old.

name: St. Matrona of Thessaloniki
title: Martyr
bio: A Christian servant in Thessaloniki whose mistress beat her to death for secretly going to church to pray, in the 3rd or 4th century; a church was later built over her tomb.

name: Apostle and Evangelist Matthew
title: Apostle and Evangelist
bio: A former tax collector called by Christ to be an Apostle, author of the first Gospel.

name: Apostle Matthias
title: Apostle
bio: Chosen by lot to replace Judas Iscariot among the Twelve, he preached in Judea and Cappadocia before his martyrdom in Jerusalem.

name: Sts. Maurice and the Theban Legion
title: Martyrs
bio: Commander of a Roman legion raised in the Egyptian Thebaid which, according to tradition, refused to take part in persecuting Christians and was put to death at Agaunum in the Alps around 286.

name: St. Maurus
title: Venerable, Abbot
bio: A disciple of St. Benedict, entrusted to him as a boy, who according to St. Gregory the Great walked on the water at Benedict's word to rescue the young monk Placid from drowning. Later tradition credits him with bringing the Benedictine rule to Gaul and founding the abbey of Glanfeuil on the Loire.

name: St. Maximilian of Theveste
title: Martyr
bio: The 21-year-old son of a Roman veteran in Africa who, called up for military service in 295, refused the soldier's oath and the leaden badge, saying "I cannot serve, I am a Christian." He was beheaded at Theveste, and the record of his trial survives as one of the earliest witnesses of Christian conscientious objection.

name: St. Maximinus of Trier
title: Bishop
bio: Bishop of Trier who received St. Athanasius the Great during his exile and defended the Nicene faith; he died around 346.

name: St. Maximos the Greek
title: Monk, Scholar, Translator
bio: Athonite monk sent to Moscow to translate sacred texts, later imprisoned for years yet remembered as an enlightener of Russia.

name: St. Maximus of Kapsokalyvia
title: Hermit
bio: A wandering hermit of Mount Athos noted for humility, ecstatic prayer, and the frequent burning of his own huts.

name: St. Maximus of Moscow
title: Fool-for-Christ
bio: A fool-for-Christ who walked half-clothed through the streets of Moscow in the 15th century, rebuking the powerful in rhymed sayings; he is buried by the church on Varvarka Street near Red Square that was later dedicated to him.

locations.label: Burial — Church of St. Maximus, Varvarka Street, Moscow

name: St. Maximus of Riez
title: Bishop
bio: A monk of Lérins who succeeded St. Honoratus as abbot in 426 and later became bishop of Riez in Provence. He governed his flock while keeping his monastic rule, and his successor Faustus praised him as a model pastor; he reposed around 460.

name: St. Maximus of Turin
title: Bishop
bio: The first known bishop of Turin, active in the early 5th century. Over a hundred of his sermons survive, in which he calls his flock away from pagan customs, urges almsgiving and encourages them during the barbarian invasions of northern Italy.

name: St. Maximus the Confessor
title: Confessor
bio: A monk and theologian who had his tongue and right hand cut off for defending Orthodox Christology, yet never wavered.

name: St. Medard of Noyon
title: Bishop
bio: Bishop of Noyon in the 6th century, renowned for his charity, who received Queen St. Radegund into monastic life.

name: St. Meinrad of Einsiedeln
title: Venerable Martyr
bio: A monk of Reichenau who withdrew as a hermit into the dark forest above Lake Zurich. In 861 he welcomed two strangers who murdered him for the gifts left by pilgrims; according to legend his two ravens pursued the killers until they were caught. Einsiedeln Abbey was later built over his hermitage.

name: St. Mel of Ardagh
title: Bishop
bio: A disciple and, by tradition, a nephew of St. Patrick, who appointed him the first bishop of Ardagh in the 5th century. Tradition holds that he received the monastic veil of St. Brigid; St. Mel's Cathedral in Longford bears his name.

name: St. Melangell of Pennant
title: Venerable
bio: A Welsh hermitess at Pennant Melangell who, according to legend, sheltered a hunted hare beneath her robe, after which Prince Brochwel gave her the valley as a place of sanctuary.

name: St. Melania the Younger
title: Venerable
bio: A wealthy Roman noblewoman who renounced her fortune to found monasteries in Jerusalem and North Africa.

name: St. Meletios of Antioch
title: Bishop
bio: Bishop of Antioch who presided at the opening of the Second Ecumenical Council in Constantinople.

name: St. Meletios the New
title: Venerable
bio: A Byzantine monk and founder of a monastery on Mount Myoupolis renowned for miracles at his tomb.

name: St. Menas of Egypt
title: Great Martyr
bio: An Egyptian soldier martyred for confessing Christ, whose shrine near Alexandria became a major pilgrimage site.

name: Sts. Menas, Hermogenes and Eugraphus
title: Martyrs
bio: Menas, an eloquent Athenian sent by Emperor Maximian to Alexandria to put down unrest among the Christians, instead strengthened them in the faith. Hermogenes, the official sent to judge him, was converted by his courage and became bishop, and with Menas's secretary Eugraphus all three were put to death in the early 4th century.

name: Sts. Menodora, Metrodora and Nymphodora
title: Virgin Martyrs
bio: Three sisters who lived in prayer near the hot springs of Pythia in Bithynia, healing the sick; they were tortured and martyred one after another under Maximian around 305.

locations.label: Ascetic life and martyrdom — Pythia (Yalova), Bithynia

name: St. Mercurius of Caesarea
title: Great Martyr
bio: A Roman soldier martyred for his faith, later venerated for miraculously striking down Julian the Apostate.

name: St. Methodia of Kimolos
title: Venerable
bio: A widow of Kimolos in the Cyclades who became a nun and lived in strict seclusion and prayer for over thirty years, guiding the islanders until her death in 1908.

name: St. Methodius of Constantinople
title: Patriarch of Constantinople
bio: Confessor imprisoned for venerating icons who, as patriarch, presided over the restoration of the icons celebrated on the Sunday of Orthodoxy.

name: St. Methodius of Olympus
title: Hieromartyr, Bishop
bio: Bishop of Olympus in Lycia and an early Christian writer, best known for his dialogue the Symposium in praise of virginity and for his writings against Origen's teachings. He suffered martyrdom around 311 during the last great persecution.

name: St. Metrophanes of Astrakhan, Hieromartyr
title: Bishop and Martyr
bio: Bishop of Astrakhan executed by Bolshevik forces in 1919 for refusing to surrender church treasures during the Civil War.

name: St. Metrophanes of Constantinople
title: Bishop
bio: Bishop of Byzantium in the time of Constantine the Great; too old to travel, he sent his successor St. Alexander to the Council of Nicaea and reposed around 326.

name: Holy Prophet Micah
title: Prophet
bio: Minor prophet from Moresheth who foretold that the ruler of Israel would be born in Bethlehem, a prophecy the scribes cited to Herod at Christ's Nativity.

name: St. Michael Maleinos
title: Venerable
bio: A Byzantine aristocrat who renounced his inheritance to become a monk and founded a lavra on Mount Kyminas in Bithynia; he was the spiritual father of St. Athanasios the Athonite and died in 961.

name: St. Michael Mauroudis of Smyrna
title: Martyr
bio: An eighteenth-century layman of Smyrna martyred for openly confessing Christ before the local Ottoman court.

name: St. Michael of Chernigov
title: Prince and Martyr
bio: A Kievan prince martyred with his boyar Theodore in the Horde for refusing to perform pagan rites.

name: St. Michael of Klopsko
title: Fool-for-Christ
bio: A mysterious monk, later revealed as a kinsman of Prince Dmitry Donskoy, who appeared at the Klopsko Monastery near Novgorod around 1408 and lived there as a fool-for-Christ with a gift of prophecy.

name: St. Michael of Synada
title: Bishop and Confessor
bio: Bishop of Synada in Phrygia and friend of St. Theodore the Studite, who was exiled for defending the holy icons and died in 826.

name: St. Michael of Tver
title: Prince and Martyr
bio: Grand Prince of Tver martyred in the Golden Horde for refusing to surrender his principality's independence.

locations.label: Place of martyrdom — Golden Horde encampment

name: St. Michael Paknanas of Athens
title: New Martyr
bio: A young gardener of Athens who, after confessing Christ in a dispute, refused to convert to Islam and was beheaded below the Acropolis in 1771.

name: St. Michael the Synkellos
title: Confessor
bio: A Palestinian monk and hymnographer of Jerusalem imprisoned for years in Constantinople for defending icon veneration.

name: St. Mildred of Thanet
title: Venerable, Abbess
bio: A Kentish princess educated at Chelles in Gaul who became abbess of Minster-in-Thanet, beloved for her kindness to the poor; she died around 732.

name: St. Milica of Serbia
title: Venerable, Princess
bio: Princess Milica, wife of Holy Prince Lazar, who governed Serbia after his death at Kosovo in 1389, protected her people and founded the Ljubostinja Monastery, where she became the nun Eugenia.

name: St. Mirian III of Georgia
title: King, Equal-to-the-Apostles
bio: The first Christian king of Iberia (Georgia), converted through the preaching of St. Nino in the fourth century.

name: St. Mitrophan of Voronezh
title: Bishop
bio: The first bishop of Voronezh, an ally of Peter the Great in Church reform and renowned for personal austerity.

name: Sts. Mitrophan Tsi Chung and the Martyrs of China
title: Martyrs
bio: Mitrophan Tsi Chung, the first Chinese Orthodox priest, and some 220 Orthodox Christians of Beijing who were killed during the Boxer Rebellion in 1900.

name: St. Mnason of Cyprus
title: Bishop
bio: An early disciple mentioned in the Acts of the Apostles as an old disciple who hosted St. Paul in Jerusalem.

name: St. Mocius of Amphipolis
title: Hieromartyr, Presbyter
bio: A priest of Amphipolis in Macedonia who overturned an altar of Dionysus; after tortures he was beheaded at Byzantium around 295, and Constantine the Great later built a great church in his honour.

name: St. Modestus of Jerusalem
title: Patriarch
bio: Abbot of the monastery of St. Theodosius who, after the Persian capture of Jerusalem in 614, restored the Church of the Holy Sepulchre and other shrines and later became Patriarch of Jerusalem.

locations.label: Restoration of the Holy Sepulchre — Jerusalem

name: St. Molaise of Devenish
title: Abbot, Monastic Founder
bio: Founder of the island monastery of Devenish on Lough Erne in the 6th century and counted among the Twelve Apostles of Ireland who studied under St. Finnian of Clonard. The island's round tower and ruined churches still mark the site of his monastery.

name: St. Moling of Ferns
title: Bishop, Monastic Founder
bio: A 7th-century Irish monk who founded the monastery of Tech Moling (St Mullins) on the River Barrow and later became bishop of Ferns. He persuaded the high king to remit the heavy cattle tribute long imposed on Leinster; a small Gospel book associated with him, the Book of Mulling, survives.

name: St. Moluag of Lismore
title: Abbot, Enlightener of the Picts
bio: An Irish monk trained at Bangor under St. Comgall who crossed to Scotland around 562 and founded a monastery on the island of Lismore. From there he and his monks evangelized the Picts of the north; he died in 592.

name: St. Monica
title: Righteous
bio: Mother of Augustine of Hippo, whose tears and unceasing prayer over many years won her son's conversion, dying at Ostia shortly after.

name: St. Moses of Optina
title: Abbot
bio: Founding abbot who established the renowned line of elders (startsy) at the Optina Hermitage.

name: St. Moses the Black
title: Venerable
bio: A former robber chieftain in Egypt who repented and became a monk in the Skete desert, renowned for his humility and later ordained a priest before being martyred by raiders.

name: Holy Prophet Moses the God-seer
title: Prophet, God-seer
bio: Leader of Israel out of Egypt who beheld God in the burning bush and received the Law on Sinai, honoured in the Orthodox Church as the God-seer.

locations.label: Receiving of the Law — Mount Sinai

name: St. Moses the Hungarian
title: Venerable
bio: Hungarian-born brother of St. George, the servant of St. Boris; taken captive to Poland, he resisted the advances of a noblewoman for years and suffered mutilation, ending his life as a monk of the Kiev Caves around 1043.

name: St. Myron of Crete
title: Bishop, Wonderworker
bio: A farmer of Crete who, finding thieves stealing his grain, helped them load it; later ordained priest and bishop, he became a wonderworker and reposed in peace around 350 at a great age.

name: St. Myrope of Chios
title: Virgin Martyr
bio: A young woman of Chios martyred for secretly gathering the relics of martyrs and tending to imprisoned Christians.

name: Holy Prophet Nahum
title: Prophet
bio: Minor prophet from Elkosh who foretold the fall of Nineveh, proclaiming the Lord as a stronghold in the day of trouble.

name: St. Narcissus of Jerusalem
title: Bishop of Jerusalem
bio: Bishop of Jerusalem in the late 2nd century, remembered by Eusebius for turning water into oil for the lamps of the Paschal vigil. Slandered by enemies, he withdrew into the desert for years before returning to his flock; he lived to well over a hundred, with St. Alexander as his coadjutor.

name: St. Naucratius of Cappadocia
title: Ascetic
bio: A brother of St. Basil the Great who withdrew to a life of solitary asceticism and care for the poor before his early death.

name: St. Naum of Ohrid
title: Venerable
bio: A disciple of Cyril and Methodius who continued their missionary work and founded a monastery at Lake Ohrid.

name: Sts. Nazarius, Gervasius, Protasius and Celsus
title: Martyrs
bio: Early Roman martyrs of Milan whose relics were discovered by St. Ambrose and venerated widely in the West.

name: St. Neagoe Basarab
title: Prince
bio: Prince of Wallachia (1512–1521) who built the cathedral of Curtea de Argeș, generously supported Mount Athos and the Eastern patriarchates, and wrote the 'Teachings of Neagoe Basarab to his son Theodosie'.

name: St. Nectarios of Aegina
title: Metropolitan of Pentapolis, Wonderworker
bio: Born Anastasios Cephalas, he served as Metropolitan of Pentapolis before being unjustly removed from his post; he later founded Holy Trinity Monastery on Aegina, where he spent his final years and is remembered for many posthumous healing miracles.

name: St. Nectarios of Bistrița
title: Bishop
bio: A Moldavian bishop and monastic founder known for his defense of Orthodoxy against Latin pressure in the region.

name: St. Nectarius of Constantinople
title: Archbishop
bio: A senator from Tarsus chosen while still unbaptized to succeed St. Gregory the Theologian as Archbishop of Constantinople in 381; he presided over the Second Ecumenical Council after Gregory's departure.

name: St. Nektarios of Vryoula, Priest and Martyr
title: Priest and Martyr
bio: A parish priest of Vryoula martyred with much of his congregation during the persecutions of the early twentieth century in Asia Minor.

name: St. Nektary of Optina
title: Elder
bio: The final elder of Optina before the Soviet closure of the monastery, who continued to counsel visitors in exile.

name: St. Neophytos the Recluse
title: Venerable
bio: Cypriot hermit who carved the Encleistra out of the rock near Paphos and left writings that are a key witness to medieval Cyprus.

name: St. Neophytus of Nicaea
title: Martyr
bio: A boy of Nicaea in Bithynia who worked wonders from childhood and, led by a dove, withdrew to a cave on Mount Olympus whose lion gave up its den to him. Returning to confess Christ during the persecution of Diocletian, he survived fire and wild beasts and was slain with a sword at the age of fifteen, around 303.

locations.label: Ascetic life — Mount Olympus of Bithynia (Uludağ)

name: St. Nestor of Thessaloniki
title: Martyr
bio: A young Christian of Thessaloniki emboldened by St. Demetrius to defeat the gladiator Lyaeus, for which he was beheaded.

name: St. Nestor the Chronicler
title: Venerable
bio: Monk of the Kiev Caves who wrote the Lives of Sts. Boris and Gleb and of St. Theodosius, traditionally credited with compiling the Primary Chronicle, the foundational history of Kievan Rus'.

name: Apostle Nicanor
title: Apostle of the Seventy, Deacon
bio: One of the seven deacons ordained by the apostles in Jerusalem (Acts 6:5). According to tradition he was martyred in Jerusalem on the same day as the Protomartyr Stephen, together with some two thousand believers.

name: St. Nicephorus of Antioch
title: Martyr
bio: A layman of Antioch who had quarrelled with his friend, the priest Sapricius, and repeatedly begged his forgiveness in vain. When Sapricius was led to execution under Valerian he lost courage and agreed to sacrifice, whereupon Nicephorus confessed Christ in his place and was beheaded around 260.

name: St. Nicetas of Remesiana
title: Bishop, Missionary
bio: Balkan bishop and missionary credited with evangelizing the Dacians and possibly composing the Te Deum hymn.

name: St. Nicetas the Goth
title: Martyr
bio: A Gothic Christian burned alive for his faith during a persecution among the Goths north of the Danube.

name: St. Nicetas the Patrician
title: Confessor
bio: A ninth-century Byzantine patrician and monastic confessor who suffered exile for opposing iconoclasm.

name: St. Nicholas Cabasilas
title: Righteous
bio: A Byzantine theologian and layman of Thessaloniki celebrated for his writings on the Divine Liturgy and life in Christ.

name: St. Nicholas of Chios, New Martyr
title: Martyr
bio: A young farmer of Chios executed by Ottoman authorities in Constantinople in 1754 for confessing Christ.

name: St. Nicholas of Japan
title: Equal-to-the-Apostles, Enlightener of Japan
bio: Russian missionary bishop who founded the Orthodox Church in Japan, translating the Scriptures and services into Japanese over half a century of ministry.

name: St. Nicholas of Myra
title: Archbishop of Myra, Wonderworker
bio: Bishop of Myra in Lycia and participant in the First Ecumenical Council of Nicaea, he is venerated throughout the world for his generosity to the poor and his protection of sailors, children, and the falsely accused. His relics were translated to Bari, Italy in 1087.

locations.label: Episcopal see and death — Myra (Demre), Lycia

name: St. Nicholas of Pskov
title: Fool-for-Christ
bio: A fool-for-Christ who in 1570 offered raw meat during Lent to Ivan the Terrible as a rebuke for his bloodshed, moving him to spare Pskov; he died in 1576.

name: St. Nicholas of Sofia
title: New Martyr
bio: A shoemaker from Ioannina living in Sofia who refused pressure to convert to Islam and was stoned and burned in 1555; his Life was written by the priest Matthew the Grammarian.

name: St. Nicholas Planas
title: Righteous
bio: A humble Athenian parish priest of the 19th–20th century renowned for his tireless liturgical devotion and simplicity.

name: St. Nicholas Sviatosha
title: Venerable, Prince
bio: Prince of Chernigov who in 1106 became the first prince of Rus' to take monastic vows, serving humbly as cook and gatekeeper at the Kiev Caves and building the Trinity Gate Church there.

name: St. Nicholas the New of Karamania
title: Martyr
bio: A layman of Karamania (Cappadocia) martyred at Prusa for refusing to abandon his Christian faith.

name: St. Nicholas the New of Vounaina
title: New Martyr
bio: A young Christian from Epirus stoned to death for defending his faith before Ottoman judges.

name: St. Nicholas the Studite
title: Venerable, Abbot
bio: A Cretan who entered the Studion monastery as a boy, shared St. Theodore the Studite's imprisonments for the holy icons and later became abbot; he died in 868.

name: St. Nicodemus
title: Righteous
bio: A Pharisee who visited Christ by night and later helped prepare His body for burial.

name: St. Nicodemus of Tismana
title: Venerable, Monastic Founder
bio: A monk of Mount Athos of Serbian and Greek descent who in the 14th century founded the monasteries of Vodița and Tismana in Wallachia, reshaping Romanian monastic life on the Athonite model.

name: St. Nikandr of Pskov
title: Hermit
bio: A hermit of the Pskov forests who lived decades alone in prayer, later revered as patron of the region's monasteries.

name: St. Nikanor of Zavorda
title: Venerable
bio: Ascetic of northern Greece who founded the Monastery of Zavorda in Grevena. He is honored for his labors in Epirus and Macedonia.

name: St. Nikephoros of Chios
title: Venerable
bio: A hieromonk of the Kollyvades movement and teacher on Chios who wrote services and Lives of many saints, among them the New Martyrs of the island; he died in 1821.

name: St. Nikephoros of Constantinople
title: Patriarch, Confessor
bio: Patriarch of Constantinople exiled for defending the veneration of icons during the iconoclast persecution.

name: St. Nikephoros the Leper
title: Venerable
bio: A 20th-century Cretan man who endured leprosy with patience and became renowned for his gentle holiness.

name: St. Nikita of Novgorod
title: Bishop
bio: A recluse of the Kiev Caves who became Bishop of Novgorod, renowned for prayer and prophetic gifts.

name: St. Nikita the Stylite of Pereslavl
title: Venerable Martyr
bio: A harsh tax collector of Pereslavl who, struck by the words of Isaiah, repented and lived in chains on a pillar at the monastery of St. Nicetas; he was killed in 1186 by robbers who mistook his chains for silver.

name: St. Nikitas the New Martyr of Nisyros
title: Martyr
bio: A young islander of Nisyros martyred by Ottoman authorities on Rhodes for refusing to abandon Orthodoxy.

name: St. Nikitas the New of Serres
title: Martyr
bio: A young Bulgarian shepherd martyred at Serres for firmly professing Christianity before an Ottoman court.

name: St. Nikodemos the Hagiorite
title: Venerable
bio: A monk of Mount Athos and prolific author who compiled the Philokalia, shaping modern Orthodox spirituality.

name: St. Nikolai Velimirović
title: Bishop
bio: Serbian bishop, theologian, and prisoner at Dachau, celebrated for his writings and pastoral zeal.

name: St. Nikon 'Metanoeite' of Sparta
title: Missionary Monk
bio: A tenth-century monk-missionary called 'Repent' for his constant exhortation, who evangelized Crete and the Peloponnese.

name: St. Nikon of Optina
title: Confessor
bio: The last elder of Optina Hermitage before its closure, who cared for the brotherhood under Soviet persecution and died in exile at Pinega in the far north in 1931.

name: St. Nikon of Radonezh
title: Venerable
bio: Disciple and successor of St. Sergius, who rebuilt the Trinity monastery after its destruction by the Tatars and adorned its church with the work of Andrei Rublev.

name: St. Nil Sorsky
title: Venerable
bio: A Russian monastic reformer who, after studying hesychasm on Mount Athos, promoted a life of poverty and inner prayer among Russian monks.

name: St. Nilus of Rossano
title: Venerable, Monastic Founder
bio: A Greek monk of Calabria who founded monasteries in southern Italy and, in 1004, the Abbey of Grottaferrata near Rome, which still keeps the Byzantine rite; he was also a noted calligrapher and hymnographer.

name: St. Nilus of Sinai
title: Venerable
bio: Former prefect of Constantinople and disciple of St. John Chrysostom who became a monk on Mount Sinai. His writings on prayer and the ascetic life are included in the Philokalia.

locations.label: Monastic life and repose — Mount Sinai, Egypt

name: St. Nilus of Stolobny Island
title: Hermit
bio: A recluse who lived for years standing in prayer on Stolobny Island in Lake Seliger, refusing to lie down to sleep.

name: St. Nilus the Myrrh-gusher
title: Venerable, Myrrh-gusher
bio: A hieromonk from the Peloponnese who lived as a hermit in the cliffs of southern Mount Athos; after his death in 1651 his relics streamed fragrant myrrh.

name: The Nine Martyrs of Cyzicus
title: Martyrs
bio: Theognes, Rufus, Antipater, Theostichus, Artemas, Magnus, Theodotus, Thaumasius and Philemon, Christians of Cyzicus on the Sea of Marmara who were beheaded for their faith in the early persecutions. Their tomb became famous for healings, especially of fevers.

name: St. Ninian of Whithorn
title: Bishop, Enlightener of the Picts
bio: Early bishop in Britain who preached to the southern Picts from his church at Whithorn, remembered as the Candida Casa.

name: St. Nino, Equal-to-the-Apostles
title: Equal-to-the-Apostles
bio: A woman of Cappadocian origin who preached the Gospel in Georgia and, through miracles and her cross of grapevines, brought the Georgian royal court to Christianity.

name: St. Niphon of Constantinople
title: Patriarch
bio: A Wallachian monk who twice served as Patriarch of Constantinople, known for his humility and reforms.

name: St. Niphon of Mount Athos
title: Monk
bio: A monk-patriarch who twice served as Patriarch of Constantinople before returning to a life of stillness on Athos.

name: St. Non of Wales
title: Righteous
bio: Mother of St. David of Wales, who according to tradition gave birth to him during a great storm on the cliffs near what is now St Davids in the 6th century. She later lived a life of prayer and is said to have died in Brittany, at Dirinon, where her tomb is still venerated.

locations.label: Birth of St. David — St Non's Chapel, St Davids

name: St. Nonna of Nazianzus
title: Righteous
bio: The mother of St. Gregory the Theologian, celebrated for leading her husband to Christianity and raising a family of saints.

name: Holy Prophet Obadiah
title: Prophet
bio: Author of the shortest book of the Old Testament, prophesying judgement on Edom; Church tradition identifies him with the steward of King Ahab who hid a hundred prophets from Jezebel, and his tomb was venerated at Sebaste.

name: St. Odile of Alsace
title: Abbess
bio: Born blind to Duke Adalric of Alsace around 662, she was rejected by her father and raised in a convent, receiving her sight at her baptism. Later reconciled with her family, she founded the convent of Hohenburg on the mountain now called Mont Sainte-Odile, and is the patron saint of Alsace.

name: St. Olaf of Norway
title: King and Martyr
bio: King of Norway who worked to establish Christianity throughout his realm. Driven into exile, he returned to reclaim his kingdom and fell at the Battle of Stiklestad in 1030; he was soon venerated as a martyr and his shrine at Nidaros became a major place of pilgrimage.

name: Matushka Olga of Alaska
title: Righteous
bio: A twentieth-century Yup'ik midwife and priest's wife in Alaska renowned for her compassion toward abused women and children.

name: St. Olga, Equal-to-the-Apostles
title: Equal-to-the-Apostles
bio: Grandmother of St. Vladimir and the first ruler of Rus' to embrace Christianity, laying the groundwork for its spread.

name: St. Olympias the Deaconess
title: Deaconess
bio: A wealthy deaconess of Constantinople and close friend of St. John Chrysostom who supported his ministry and endured exile with him in spirit.

name: St. Omer of Thérouanne
title: Bishop
bio: A monk of Luxeuil, the monastery of St. Columbanus, who was made bishop of Thérouanne around 637 to preach to the Morini of the region. With the monks Bertin, Mommolinus and Bertrand he founded the abbey of Sithiu, around which grew the town of Saint-Omer.

name: Apostle Onesimus
title: Apostle of the Seventy, Bishop of Ephesus
bio: Once a runaway slave of Philemon, converted and baptized by St. Paul in Rome, he later became Bishop of Ephesus and was martyred under Emperor Trajan.

name: St. Onouphrios of Chios, New Martyr
title: Martyr
bio: A monk of Chios martyred at Constantinople after publicly renouncing an earlier forced apostasy.

name: St. Onuphrius the Great
title: Venerable
bio: A hermit who spent seventy years alone in the Egyptian desert in extreme asceticism and prayer.

name: St. Orestes of Cappadocia
title: Martyr
bio: One of the Holy Unmercenaries martyred in Cappadocia, venerated together with Sts. Eustratius and companions.

name: St. Oswald of Northumbria
title: King and Martyr
bio: King of Northumbria who raised a wooden cross before his victory at Heavenfield, invited St. Aidan from Iona to evangelize his people, and fell in battle against the pagan Penda at Maserfield in 642.

name: St. Oswald of Worcester
title: Archbishop
bio: Bishop of Worcester and Archbishop of York, founder of Ramsey Abbey and a leader of the monastic revival, who died in 992 while washing the feet of the poor during Lent.

name: St. Oswin of Deira
title: King and Martyr
bio: King of Deira, a humble and generous ruler and friend of St. Aidan, who was betrayed and killed at Gilling on the orders of King Oswiu in 651.

name: St. Othmar of St. Gallen
title: Abbot
bio: An Alemannic priest who in 719 became the first abbot of the community gathered at the hermitage of St. Gall, organizing it as a monastery and founding there a hospice for the poor and a house for lepers. Falsely accused by local counts, he died in exile on the Rhine island of Werd in 759.

locations.label: Exile and repose — Werd island, Rhine

name: St. Ouen of Rouen
title: Bishop
bio: A courtier and friend of St. Eligius under King Dagobert who became bishop of Rouen in 641, founded monasteries and worked against simony; he died in 684.

name: St. Pachomius the Great
title: Venerable
bio: An Egyptian monk who founded the first cenobitic monastery, organizing communal monastic life along the Nile.

name: St. Padarn of Llanbadarn
title: Bishop, Monastic Founder
bio: A 6th-century monk, probably from Brittany, who founded the monastery and see of Llanbadarn Fawr near Aberystwyth in Wales. Tradition makes him a companion of Sts. David and Teilo on their pilgrimage to Jerusalem.

name: St. Paisios of Mount Athos
title: Venerable, Elder
bio: Born Arsenios Eznepidis, his family fled Asia Minor for Greece in his infancy; he became a monk of Mount Athos known for his gentle counsel to the thousands of pilgrims who sought him out, and was canonized in 2015.

locations.label: Death and relics — Souroti, near Thessaloniki

name: St. Paisius of Hilendar
title: Venerable
bio: Athonite monk whose Slavonic-Bulgarian History awakened the national and spiritual revival of the Bulgarian people.

name: St. Paisius the Great
title: Venerable, Desert Father
bio: An Egyptian monk of the Scetis desert and disciple of St. Pambo, whose prayers were said to have won God's mercy even for a disciple who had denied Christ.

name: St. Paisius Velichkovsky
title: Venerable
bio: A Ukrainian-born monk who revived hesychast spirituality in Moldavia and translated the Philokalia into Slavonic.

locations.label: Monastic years — Skete of St. Elias, Mount Athos

name: St. Pambo of Nitria
title: Venerable, Desert Father
bio: One of the earliest monks of the Nitrian desert and a disciple of St. Anthony, renowned for his silence and for guarding his tongue, having spent years putting into practice a single verse of Psalm 38.

name: St. Pamphilus of Caesarea
title: Priest and Martyr
bio: A scholar-priest of Caesarea who assembled a great theological library and was martyred alongside his disciples.

name: St. Panagis Basias of Cephalonia
title: Monk and Ascetic
bio: A nineteenth-century Cephalonian monk celebrated for extreme humility, hospitality to the poor, and gift of healing.

name: St. Pancras of Taormina
title: Hieromartyr, Bishop
bio: By tradition a disciple of St. Peter, who sent him as the first bishop of Taormina in Sicily, where he converted many before being stoned by pagans.

locations.label: Episcopal see and martyrdom — Taormina, Sicily

name: St. Panteleimon
title: Great Martyr, Unmercenary Healer
bio: A physician of Nicomedia who treated the poor and sick without charge in the name of Christ, he was martyred under Emperor Maximian after healing a paralyzed man before the emperor's own eyes; he is invoked among the unmercenary healer-saints.

name: St. Paphnutius of Borovsk
title: Monastic Founder
bio: Founder of the Nativity Monastery at Borovsk, teacher of St. Joseph of Volokolamsk and renowned ascetic elder.

name: St. Paphnutius the Confessor
title: Bishop and Confessor
bio: A bishop of the Upper Thebaid who lost an eye and was lamed in the persecution of Maximinus; honoured by Constantine the Great at the First Ecumenical Council, he argued that married men need not give up their wives on ordination.

name: St. Paraskeva of Iconium
title: Great Martyr
bio: A virgin of Iconium who dedicated her life to Christ and to preaching the faith, martyred under Emperor Diocletian. Known in Slavic lands as Paraskeva Pyatnitsa ("Friday"), she is venerated as a protector of family life and trade.

name: St. Paraskeva the New of Epivates
title: Righteous
bio: A pious ascetic of Epivates near the Black Sea, revered across the Balkans and enshrined in Iași, Romania.

name: St. Paraskevi of Rome
title: Martyr
bio: A Roman virgin martyred for her faith, widely venerated as a healer, especially of eye ailments.

name: St. Parthenius of Lampsacus
title: Bishop, Wonderworker
bio: A deacon's son from Melitopolis who healed the sick by prayer and became bishop of Lampsacus on the Hellespont, where under Constantine the Great he cleared the pagan temples and built a church.

name: St. Patapios of Thebes
title: Venerable
bio: An Egyptian ascetic from Thebes who settled in Constantinople and healed many by his prayers; his incorrupt relics rest in a cave convent above Loutraki, near Corinth.

name: St. Patrick of Ireland
title: Equal-to-the-Apostles
bio: A Romano-British missionary who brought Christianity to Ireland after years of captivity there as a youth.

name: St. Patrick of Prusa
title: Hieromartyr, Bishop
bio: Bishop of Prusa in Bithynia who, brought before the governor at the hot springs, preached Christ as the true source of their healing warmth and was beheaded with three priests.

name: Apostle Paul
title: Chief Apostle
bio: Former persecutor of Christians converted on the road to Damascus, becoming the great Apostle to the Gentiles.

name: St. Paul Aurelian of Léon
title: Bishop
bio: A Welsh monk and disciple of St. Illtud who sailed to Brittany in the 6th century with twelve companions. He settled on the Île de Batz and became the first bishop of Léon, whose town is now called Saint-Pol-de-Léon after him.

name: St. Paul of Latros
title: Venerable
bio: A 10th-century hermit of Mount Latros near Miletus who lived in caves and on a pillar; his fame reached Emperor Constantine VII and Tsar Peter of Bulgaria, who corresponded with him.

name: St. Paul of Obnora
title: Venerable, Monastic Founder
bio: A disciple of St. Sergius of Radonezh who lived for three years in the hollow of a linden tree in the Komel forest before founding the Holy Trinity Monastery on the Nurma River in 1414.

name: St. Paul of Thebes
title: Venerable
bio: Regarded as the first Christian hermit, who lived nearly a century alone in the Egyptian desert.

name: St. Paul the Confessor of Constantinople
title: Archbishop and Confessor
bio: Archbishop of Constantinople and staunch defender of Nicaea, repeatedly deposed by Arian-minded emperors; exiled to Cucusus in Armenia, he was strangled by Arians around 350.

name: St. Paul the Russian, New Martyr
title: Martyr
bio: A Russian soldier captured by Ottoman forces and martyred at Constantinople for refusing to renounce Christ.

name: St. Paul the Simple
title: Venerable
bio: Disciple of St. Anthony the Great, a guileless farmer who left his wife and took up the ascetic life in the Egyptian desert, receiving the gift of discerning spirits.

name: St. Paulinus of Nola
title: Bishop
bio: A wealthy Gallo-Roman senator and poet who, with his wife Therasia, gave away his fortune and settled at the shrine of St. Felix in Nola, where he became bishop; he corresponded with Sts. Augustine, Jerome and Ambrose.

name: St. Paulinus of York
title: Bishop
bio: A member of the Roman mission to England who accompanied the Christian princess Æthelburh to Northumbria, baptized King Edwin at York in 627 and ended his life as bishop of Rochester.

name: St. Pelagia of Antioch
title: Venerable
bio: A repentant actress of Antioch who became a hermit on the Mount of Olives disguised as a monk.

name: St. Pelagia of Tarsus
title: Virgin Martyr
bio: A young noblewoman of Tarsus martyred in a heated brazen bull for refusing marriage to the emperor's son.

name: St. Pelagia of Tinos
title: Venerable, Nun
bio: A nun of Kechrovouni Monastery on Tinos who in 1822 was told in repeated visions of the Theotokos where an icon lay buried. The icon of the Annunciation was unearthed in January 1823, and the great church of Panagia Evangelistria, one of Greece's foremost pilgrimage sites, was built over the spot.

locations.label: Finding of the icon — Panagia Evangelistria, Tinos

name: Sts. Perpetua and Felicity
title: Martyrs
bio: A young noblewoman and her servant, martyred together in the arena at Carthage; Perpetua's prison diary is among the earliest writings by a Christian woman.

name: Apostle Peter
title: Chief Apostle
bio: A fisherman called by Christ who became the foremost of the Apostles, martyred by crucifixion upside down in Rome.

name: Sts. Peter and Fevronia of Murom
title: Right-believing Prince and Princess
bio: Prince and his peasant-born wife, honoured in Russia as patrons of marriage and family life.

name: St. Peter II of Cetinje
title: Bishop and Ruler
bio: Prince-Bishop of Montenegro and celebrated poet-philosopher who guided his people through Ottoman-era struggles.

name: St. Peter Mogila
title: Metropolitan
bio: Son of a Moldavian prince who became Metropolitan of Kiev (1633–1646), founded the Kiev-Mohyla Collegium, and prepared an Orthodox Confession of Faith and a widely used Euchologion.

name: St. Peter of Alexandria
title: Hieromartyr, Archbishop
bio: Archbishop of Alexandria during the Great Persecution, who wrote canons on receiving back the lapsed and was the first to warn against Arius; beheaded in 311, he is called the 'Seal of the Martyrs'.

name: St. Peter of Argos
title: Bishop, Wonderworker
bio: A Constantinopolitan who became bishop of Argos in the 10th century, renowned for ransoming captives and feeding the hungry during famine.

name: St. Peter of Atroa
title: Venerable, Wonderworker
bio: Born near Ephesus in 773, he became a monk on Mount Olympus in Bithynia under St. Paul of Crypta and restored the monastery of St. Zacharias at Atroa. Persecuted by the iconoclasts, he moved from place to place, working many miracles of healing, and died in 837.

name: St. Peter of Bulgaria
title: Tsar
bio: Tsar of Bulgaria (927–969) and son of Simeon the Great, who kept peace with Byzantium, supported the Church and St. John of Rila, and is said to have ended his life as a monk.

name: St. Peter of Cetinje
title: Metropolitan of Montenegro
bio: Metropolitan and ruler of Montenegro who reconciled its warring clans, gave it its first laws, and was glorified soon after his repose.

name: St. Peter of Korisha
title: Venerable
bio: A Serbian hermit who lived in a cave near Korisha, renowned for his solitude and gift of healing.

name: St. Peter of Krutitsy
title: Metropolitan and Confessor
bio: Locum tenens of the Russian Patriarchal throne who died in Soviet exile after years of imprisonment for his faith.

name: St. Peter of Moscow
title: Metropolitan
bio: The first Metropolitan to move his see to Moscow, helping establish the city as the spiritual center of Russia.

name: St. Peter of Sebaste
title: Bishop
bio: The youngest brother of St. Basil the Great and St. Gregory of Nyssa, who became Bishop of Sebaste in Armenia.

name: St. Peter the Aleut
title: Martyr
bio: Young Aleut hunter from Kodiak who, according to his companion's account, was tortured to death in California for refusing to abandon the Orthodox faith.

name: St. Peter the Athonite
title: Hermit
bio: Traditionally the first hermit to dwell on Mount Athos, living for decades in a cave in extreme asceticism.

name: St. Petroc of Cornwall
title: Abbot
bio: Welsh prince who became a monk and abbot, founding the monastery of Padstow and numerous churches throughout Cornwall and Devon.

name: St. Philaret of Moscow
title: Metropolitan
bio: Metropolitan of Moscow for nearly half a century (1821–1867), whose Longer Catechism became the standard of Russian Orthodox teaching; he oversaw the Russian translation of the Bible and was a spiritual father to many.

name: St. Philaret the Merciful
title: Righteous
bio: A wealthy landowner of Asia Minor who gave away his fortune to the poor, trusting in Providence, and whose granddaughter became empress of Byzantium.

name: Sts. Philemon, Apphia and Archippus
title: Apostles and Martyrs
bio: Philemon, the Colossian master of Onesimus to whom St. Paul wrote his epistle, his wife Apphia and Archippus, leader of the church that met in their home, were stoned by pagans at Colossae during a festival of Artemis.

name: St. Philibert of Jumièges
title: Abbot, Monastic Founder
bio: Raised at the Frankish royal court, he became a monk and in 654 founded the great Abbey of Jumièges on the Seine. After opposing the mayor of the palace Ebroin he was imprisoned and exiled, and founded a new monastery on the island of Noirmoutier, where he died in 685.

name: Apostle Philip
title: Apostle
bio: One of the Twelve Apostles who brought Nathanael to Christ and was later martyred in Hierapolis.

name: St. Philip of Agira
title: Venerable, Wonderworker
bio: A priest of eastern origin, ordained in Rome and sent to Sicily in the early centuries of the Church, who settled at Agira in the interior of the island and became famous for driving out demons. His tomb at Agira remains a place of pilgrimage, and he has long been venerated by both the Greek and Latin Christians of Sicily.

name: St. Philip of Heraclea
title: Hieromartyr, Bishop
bio: Elderly bishop of Heraclea in Thrace who, with the priest Severus and the deacon Hermes, refused to hand over the sacred books and was burned at Adrianople in 304.

name: St. Philip of Moscow
title: Metropolitan of Moscow, Hieromartyr
bio: Abbot of Solovki and metropolitan who publicly rebuked Ivan the Terrible for his cruelty and was deposed and killed in exile.

locations.label: Place of death — Otroch Monastery, Tver

name: Apostle Philip the Deacon
title: Apostle of the Seventy, Deacon
bio: One of the seven deacons of Jerusalem, who preached in Samaria, baptized the Ethiopian eunuch on the road to Gaza and settled at Caesarea, where he hosted St. Paul with his four prophesying daughters; tradition makes him bishop of Tralles.

name: St. Philo of Karpasia
title: Bishop
bio: A learned contemporary of St. Epiphanius of Salamis, who ordained him Bishop of Karpasia on the Karpas peninsula of Cyprus around the end of the 4th century. He is known for his commentary on the Song of Songs and as a wonderworker; the ruined basilica of Agios Philon marks the site of ancient Karpasia.

name: St. Philothei of Athens
title: Venerable Martyr
bio: Athenian noblewoman who founded a convent to shelter and ransom women enslaved under Ottoman rule, martyred for her charitable works.

name: St. Philotheus Kokkinos
title: Patriarch
bio: Patriarch of Constantinople and biographer of St. Gregory Palamas, an ardent hesychast theologian.

name: St. Philoumenos of Mount Sinai
title: Hieromartyr
bio: A twentieth-century Cypriot monk martyred at Jacob's Well in Nablus by fanatics for his guardianship of the holy site.

name: St. Phocas the Gardener
title: Martyr
bio: A gardener near Sinope on the Black Sea who gave hospitality to the soldiers sent to arrest him, then willingly gave himself up and was beheaded; his garden produce fed the poor.

name: St. Phoebe the Deaconess
title: Righteous, Deaconess
bio: Deaconess of the church at Cenchreae, the eastern port of Corinth, whom Paul commends to the Romans as "a helper of many, and of myself also" (Romans 16:1–2). She is traditionally held to have carried his Epistle to the Romans to Rome.

locations.label: Bearer of the Epistle to the Romans — Rome

name: St. Photini, the Samaritan Woman
title: Equal-to-the-Apostles
bio: The Samaritan woman who met Christ at Jacob's Well, was converted, and became a fervent evangelist, later martyred in Rome under Nero.

name: St. Photios the Great
title: Patriarch
bio: Patriarch of Constantinople and renowned scholar who sent missionaries Cyril and Methodius to the Slavs.

name: St. Photius of Kiev and Moscow
title: Metropolitan
bio: A Greek monk from Monemvasia in the Peloponnese, appointed Metropolitan of Kiev and All Rus' in 1408, who resided in Moscow. He struggled to preserve the unity of the Russian Church when the Lithuanian lands broke away, recovered church property and lived ascetically; he reposed in 1431 and rests in the Dormition Cathedral of the Kremlin.

locations.label: Metropolitan see and burial — Dormition Cathedral, Moscow Kremlin

name: St. Pimen the Much-Ailing
title: Venerable
bio: A monk of the Kiev Caves, ill from birth, who was tonsured when he seemed near death and then lived on in sickness for many years, foretelling the day of his repose in 1110.

name: St. Piran of Cornwall
title: Abbot
bio: Irish-born abbot who settled on the Cornish coast, where he founded a monastery and evangelized the local people; he is the patron saint of Cornwall.

name: St. Pitirim of Tambov
title: Bishop
bio: Second bishop of Tambov (1685–1698), who built the city's cathedral and strengthened the faith on Russia's southern frontier; he was glorified in 1914.

name: St. Plato of Ancyra
title: Martyr
bio: A young man of Ancyra who boldly confessed Christ before the governor and was beheaded after prolonged torture.

name: St. Plato of Sakkoudion
title: Venerable, Abbot
bio: Uncle of St. Theodore the Studite and abbot of the Sakkoudion monastery in Bithynia, who later joined the Studion and was imprisoned for opposing the emperor's adulterous marriage; he died in 814.

name: St. Poemen the Great
title: Venerable, Desert Father
bio: Widely quoted desert father of Egypt's Scetis whose sayings on humility, discretion, and compassion form a large part of the Apophthegmata Patrum.

name: St. Polycarp of Smyrna
title: Hieromartyr
bio: Bishop of Smyrna and disciple of the Apostle John, burned at the stake for refusing to renounce Christ in old age.

name: St. Polydoros of Cyprus, New Martyr
title: Martyr
bio: A young Cypriot martyred at Nicosia for his open confession of Christian faith before Ottoman authorities.

name: St. Polyeuctus of Melitene
title: Martyr
bio: Roman officer at Melitene in Armenia, brought to faith through his friend Nearchus, who tore up the imperial edict of persecution and was beheaded in 259, becoming the first martyr of Melitene.

name: St. Porphyrios of Kafsokalyvia
title: Venerable, Elder
bio: A Greek elder who spent decades as a confessor near Athens, renowned for his gift of clairvoyance and his joyful, Christ-centred spiritual direction. He was canonized in 2013 and his collected conversations have been read by millions across the Orthodox world.

locations.label: Priestly ministry and death — Milesi, near Athens

name: Sts. Porphyrios, Baptus and Companions
title: Martyrs
bio: Roman soldiers converted and martyred alongside St. Charalambos after witnessing his miraculous endurance.

name: St. Porphyrius of Gaza
title: Bishop
bio: A wealthy Thessalonian who became a monk in Egypt and Palestine; as bishop of Gaza from 395 he laboured to convert the largely pagan city, and the Empress Eudoxia funded a great church on the site of its temple of Marnas.

name: Sts. Pothinus, Blandina and the Martyrs of Lyon
title: Martyrs
bio: The ninety-year-old bishop Pothinus, the slave girl Blandina and some forty companions martyred at Lyon in 177; their sufferings are described in a letter preserved by Eusebius.

name: Sts. Processus and Martinian
title: Martyrs
bio: Traditionally the Roman jailers of Sts. Peter and Paul who were converted and later martyred for their faith.

name: Apostle Prochorus
title: Apostle of the Seventy, Deacon
bio: One of the seven deacons ordained in Jerusalem and a disciple of St. John the Theologian, whose Revelation he wrote down on Patmos; he became bishop of Nicomedia and was martyred at Antioch.

name: St. Prochorus of Pčinja
title: Venerable
bio: An 11th-century hermit who settled by the river Pčinja and foretold to the young Romanos Diogenes that he would become emperor; Romanos later built the monastery that bears the hermit's name.

name: St. Prochorus the Orach-Eater
title: Venerable
bio: A monk of the Kiev Caves who lived on bread made from orache (goosefoot); during the famine of 1095 his bread was sweet to the hungry who received it, and ash he blessed served them as salt. He died in 1107.

name: Sts. Proclus and Hilary of Ancyra
title: Martyrs
bio: Christians of Ancyra in Galatia martyred under Trajan in the early 2nd century. Proclus boldly confessed Christ before the governor and was shot with arrows; his nephew Hilary, who had encouraged him, was arrested and beheaded soon after.

name: St. Proclus of Constantinople
title: Patriarch
bio: Patriarch of Constantinople and disciple of St. John Chrysostom, celebrated preacher on the Theotokos.

name: St. Procopios of Iconium, Metropolitan and Martyr
title: Metropolitan and Martyr
bio: Metropolitan of Iconium martyred amid the anti-Greek violence during the Asia Minor catastrophe.

name: St. Procopius of Ustyug
title: Fool-for-Christ
bio: A merchant of foreign origin who took up voluntary poverty and foolishness for Christ in Veliky Ustyug, foretelling calamities.

name: St. Procopius the Great Martyr
title: Great Martyr
bio: An officer sent to persecute Christians who was converted by a vision of the Cross and himself martyred at Caesarea in Palestine under Diocletian.

locations.label: Place of martyrdom — Caesarea in Palestine

name: St. Proterius of Alexandria
title: Hieromartyr, Patriarch
bio: Orthodox Patriarch of Alexandria installed after the Council of Chalcedon, who was murdered in the baptistery by an anti-Chalcedonian mob in 457.

name: Apostle Pudens
title: Apostle of the Seventy
bio: A Roman Christian greeted by St. Paul in his Second Epistle to Timothy and numbered among the Seventy. Tradition holds that he welcomed the Apostles Peter and Paul into his house in Rome, which became one of the city's first churches, and that he was martyred under Nero.

name: St. Pulcheria the Empress
title: Righteous
bio: A Byzantine empress who governed with piety and convened the Fourth Ecumenical Council against heresy.

name: St. Quadratus of Corinth
title: Martyr
bio: A Christian of Corinth who lived in solitude in the countryside and was arrested during the persecution of Decius or Valerian in the mid-3rd century. Together with several companions he was tortured and beheaded at Corinth around 258.

name: Apostle Quartus
title: Apostle of the Seventy
bio: A Christian of Corinth whose greetings Paul sends to the Romans (Romans 16:23). Counted among the Seventy, he is remembered as bishop of Berytus (Beirut), where he brought many pagans to the faith and endured much suffering before reposing in peace.

name: St. Quirinus of Siscia
title: Hieromartyr, Bishop
bio: Bishop of Siscia in Pannonia who fled persecution but was captured and, after refusing to sacrifice, was drowned in the river at Savaria with a millstone around his neck; his relics were later carried to Rome.

name: St. Radegund of Poitiers
title: Venerable, Queen
bio: A Thuringian princess taken captive and forced to marry the Frankish king Chlothar I, whom she left to found the Holy Cross convent at Poitiers; Venantius Fortunatus wrote the hymn 'Vexilla Regis' for its relic of the Cross.

name: St. Raphael of Brooklyn
title: Bishop
bio: The first Orthodox bishop consecrated in North America, serving Arab Orthodox immigrants across the continent.

name: Sts. Raphael, Nicholas and Irene of Lesvos
title: New Martyrs
bio: A priest, a layman, and a young girl martyred by Ottoman raiders on Lesvos, whose relics were revealed in the 20th century.

name: St. Razhden the Protomartyr of Georgia
title: Martyr
bio: A Persian noble convert regarded as the first martyr of the Georgian Church, executed for refusing to abjure Christianity.

name: St. Remigius of Reims
title: Bishop
bio: Bishop of Reims for more than seventy years, who baptized King Clovis together with thousands of Franks around 496, opening the way for the conversion of the Frankish people.

name: St. Roman of Ryazan
title: Prince and Martyr
bio: Prince of Ryazan who was denounced to the Golden Horde for speaking against its faith and, refusing to renounce Christ, was tortured to death in 1270.

name: St. Romanos the Melodist
title: Hymnographer
bio: A deacon of Syrian birth who became the greatest hymnographer of the Byzantine Church, composing the Kontakion of the Nativity and hundreds of other hymns.

name: St. Romanus of Caesarea
title: Deacon and Martyr
bio: A deacon of Caesarea in Palestine who, during the persecution of Diocletian, went to Antioch and urged Christians who were about to sacrifice not to deny Christ. His tongue was cut out, yet he went on speaking and praising God, and he was strangled in prison in 303.

name: St. Romanus of Condat
title: Venerable, Abbot
bio: A monk of Lyon who around 435 withdrew into the forests of the Jura mountains, where he was joined by his brother Lupicinus. Disciples gathered around them and they founded the monastery of Condat, later called Saint-Claude, and other communities; he died around 463.

name: St. Romuald of Camaldoli
title: Venerable, Monastic Founder
bio: A nobleman of Ravenna who, after his father killed a kinsman in a duel, did penance at the monastery of Sant'Apollinare in Classe and became a monk there. A tireless reformer, he founded many hermitages across Italy, most famously Camaldoli in the Apennines (c. 1012), and reposed in 1027.

locations.label: Monastic vows — Sant'Apollinare in Classe, Ravenna

name: St. Romylos of Vidin
title: Hesychast
bio: A Bulgarian-Serbian hesychast monk who studied under Gregory of Sinai and spread hesychast practice through the Balkans.

name: Apostle Rufus
title: Apostle of the Seventy
bio: A son of Simon of Cyrene, who carried the Cross of Christ (Mark 15:21), and greeted by Paul as "chosen in the Lord" (Romans 16:13). Counted among the Seventy, he is remembered as bishop of Thebes in Greece.

name: St. Rupert of Salzburg
title: Bishop, Enlightener of Bavaria
bio: A Frankish bishop of Worms who went as a missionary to Bavaria around 696. At the ruins of the Roman town of Iuvavum he founded St. Peter's Abbey and the convent of Nonnberg, laying the foundations of the city and Church of Salzburg; he died around 710.

name: Holy Royal Martyrs of Russia
title: Martyrs
bio: Tsar Nicholas II and his family, executed by Bolshevik forces at Yekaterinburg in 1918 and glorified for their patient faith.

name: St. Sabbas Stratelates
title: Martyr
bio: A Goth by birth who rose to command in the Roman army under Emperor Aurelian, Sabbas visited Christians in prison and gave generously to the poor. Refusing to sacrifice to the gods, he endured torture unharmed; seventy soldiers who witnessed this came to faith and were beheaded, and Sabbas was drowned in a river near Rome around 272.

name: St. Sabbas the Sanctified
title: Venerable
bio: A Cappadocian monastic who settled in the Judean desert and founded the Great Lavra (Mar Saba), composing the Jerusalem Typikon that shaped monastic and liturgical practice across the Orthodox world.

locations.label: Monastery and relics — Mar Saba, Judean Desert

name: St. Sampson the Hospitable
title: Venerable, Unmercenary Physician
bio: A wealthy Roman physician who settled in Constantinople, healed the sick without payment and, after curing Emperor Justinian, built a great hospital near Hagia Sophia; he died around 530.

name: St. Samson of Dol
title: Bishop
bio: Welsh-born monk and bishop who evangelized Cornwall and Brittany and founded the monastery of Dol.

name: Holy Prophet Samuel
title: Prophet and Judge
bio: Last of the judges of Israel, given to God from childhood by his mother Hannah and raised at the tabernacle in Shiloh, who anointed Saul and then David as kings.

locations.label: Traditional tomb — Nabi Samwil, near Jerusalem

name: St. Sarah of the Desert
title: Ascetic
bio: A desert mother of Egypt who lived sixty years by the Nile in fierce asceticism, overcoming demonic temptation through humility.

name: St. Saturninus of Toulouse
title: Hieromartyr, Bishop
bio: First bishop of Toulouse, who refused to sacrifice to the pagan gods and was tied to a bull and dragged to death around 250; the Basilica of Saint-Sernin stands over his tomb.

name: St. Sava of Serbia
title: Archbishop
bio: First Archbishop of the autocephalous Serbian Church and founder of Hilandar Monastery on Mount Athos.

name: St. Sava of Vatopedi
title: Monk
bio: A Serbian prince who abandoned royal life to become a monk at Vatopedi Monastery on Mount Athos.

name: St. Sava the Goth
title: Martyr
bio: A Gothic Christian drowned in the Buzău River for his faith, one of the earliest saints venerated in Romania.

locations.label: Place of martyrdom — Buzău River, Romania

name: St. Savva of Storozhevsk
