title: Venerable, Monastic Founder
bio: Disciple of St. Sergius of Radonezh and confessor of Prince Yury of Zvenigorod, who founded the Savvino-Storozhevsky Monastery near Zvenigorod in 1398.

name: St. Savvas the New of Kalymnos
title: Venerable
bio: A monk of Kalymnos in the 19th century known for his extreme asceticism and care for the sick.

name: St. Savvatii of Solovki
title: Venerable
bio: A monk who, seeking solitude, settled on the remote Solovetsky Islands and co-founded the monastery that became a beacon of Russian monasticism.

name: St. Scholastica
title: Venerable
bio: Twin sister of St. Benedict of Nursia who led a community of nuns near Monte Cassino; at their last meeting her prayer brought a storm that kept her brother talking with her through the night.

name: The Scillitan Martyrs
title: Martyrs
bio: Twelve Christians from Scillium in Roman Africa — among them Speratus, Nartzalus, Cittinus, Donata, Secunda and Vestia — tried at Carthage by the proconsul Saturninus in 180. The record of their trial, in which they answered the death sentence with "Thanks be to God," is the oldest surviving Christian document in Latin.

name: The Forty Martyrs of Sebaste
title: Martyrs
bio: Forty Roman soldiers who froze to death on a lake for refusing to renounce Christianity, encouraging one another to the end.

name: St. Sebastian
title: Martyr
bio: A Roman soldier martyred for aiding imprisoned Christians, shot with arrows and later clubbed to death.

name: St. Sebastian of Jackson
title: Archimandrite, Apostle to the Americas
bio: The first Orthodox priest born in the United States, who founded parishes across America before returning to Serbia, where he reposed at the monastery of Zica.

locations.label: Place of repose — Zica Monastery, Serbia

name: St. Seiriol of Penmon
title: Venerable, Abbot
bio: A 6th-century Welsh monk who led a community at Penmon on Anglesey and later withdrew to the island of Ynys Seiriol (Puffin Island). Tradition tells of his friendship with St. Cybi of Holyhead, whom he met each week in the middle of Anglesey.

locations.label: Monastery and holy well — Penmon, Anglesey

name: St. Senan of Scattery
title: Abbot, Bishop
bio: A 6th-century Irish monk who founded several monasteries along the Shannon, the most famous on Scattery Island (Inis Cathaig) at the mouth of the river. The island, with its round tower and ruined churches, remained a place of pilgrimage for centuries; he died around 544.

name: St. Seraphim (Chichagov) of Moscow
title: Metropolitan and Martyr
bio: A former military officer turned bishop who compiled the chronicle of St. Seraphim of Sarov and was shot by Soviet authorities at age 82.

name: St. Seraphim (Sobolev) of Sofia
title: Archbishop, Wonderworker
bio: Born in Ryazan in 1881, he served as a bishop in Russia before emigrating and becoming Archbishop of Bogucharsk in Sofia, where he shepherded the Russian community and taught Orthodox theology. He reposed in 1950 and was glorified in 2016; his relics rest in the Russian Church of St. Nicholas in Sofia.

name: St. Seraphim of Phanar
title: Hieromartyr, Bishop
bio: Bishop of Phanari and Neochorion in Thessaly who was accused of supporting a revolt against the Ottomans; refusing to deny Christ, he was tortured and impaled in 1601.

name: St. Seraphim of Sarov
title: Venerable, Wonderworker
bio: A monk of Sarov in Russia who spent years in hermitage and later opened his cell to thousands of pilgrims, greeting each with the words “My joy!” He taught that the aim of the Christian life is the acquisition of the Holy Spirit, and remains one of the most beloved saints of the Russian Church.

locations.label: Monastic life and death — Sarov, Russia

name: St. Seraphim of Shanghai's Companion Ionna
title: Righteous
bio: A laywoman associated with the Shanghai Orthodox community under the care of St. John Maximovitch during the Chinese Civil War.

name: St. Seraphim of Vyritsa
title: Venerable
bio: A successful merchant who became a monk and elder, known for prayer and prophecy during Soviet persecution.

name: St. Serf of Culross
title: Abbot
bio: A 6th-century missionary in Fife who founded a monastery at Culross on the Firth of Forth and a cell on an island in Loch Leven. According to legend he took in and raised the infant St. Kentigern (Mungo) and his mother Teneu after they came ashore at Culross.

locations.label: Island cell — St Serf's Inch, Loch Leven

name: Sts. Sergius and Bacchus
title: Great Martyrs
bio: Roman officers and close companions in the imperial army who were exposed as Christians for refusing to sacrifice to idols. Bacchus died under the lash and Sergius was beheaded at Resafa in Syria.

name: Sts. Sergius and Herman of Valaam
title: Venerable, Monastic Founders
bio: Founders of the Valaam Monastery on the islands of Lake Ladoga, probably between the 10th and 12th centuries, who brought the Gospel to the peoples of Karelia; their relics rest in the monastery's cathedral.

name: St. Sergius of Optina, Confessor
title: Confessor
bio: A twentieth-century monk of Optina who preserved the eldership tradition through Soviet persecution and exile.

name: St. Sergius of Radonezh
title: Venerable
bio: Founder of the Holy Trinity Monastery near Moscow, one of the most beloved monastic saints of Russia.

name: St. Servatius of Tongeren
title: Bishop
bio: Bishop of Tongeren who defended the Nicene faith at the Council of Serdica and died at Maastricht in 384, where his basilica stands over his tomb.

locations.label: Tomb — Basilica of St. Servatius, Maastricht

name: The Seven Sleepers of Ephesus
title: Venerable Confessors
bio: Seven young Christians of Ephesus who hid in a cave on Mount Celion during the persecution of Decius and, according to tradition, were walled in and fell asleep, awakening some two centuries later under Theodosius II as a witness to the resurrection of the dead.

locations.label: Cave of the Seven Sleepers — Ephesus

name: St. Severinus of Noricum
title: Venerable
bio: A monk of unknown origin who, in the chaos after Attila's death, cared for the Roman population along the Danube in Noricum, organizing relief and ransoming captives; he died at Favianis in 482.

name: St. Sexburga of Ely
title: Venerable, Abbess
bio: Queen of Kent and sister of St. Etheldreda, who founded the convent of Minster-in-Sheppey and succeeded her sister as abbess of Ely; she died around 699.

name: St. Shio of Mgvime
title: Monastic Founder
bio: A Syrian Father who founded the cave monastery of Mgvime near Mtskheta, living as a strict hermit in his final years.

name: St. Shushanik
title: Martyr, Queen of Kartli
bio: Armenian-born queen of Kartli who suffered imprisonment and death rather than follow her husband into apostasy; the account of her passion is the oldest surviving work of Georgian literature.

name: St. Sidonia of Mtskheta
title: Righteous
bio: A Georgian noblewoman converted by St. Nino, buried with a robe of Christ said to be enshrined at Svetitskhoveli Cathedral.

name: Apostle Silas
title: Apostle of the Seventy, Bishop of Corinth
bio: A leader of the early Jerusalem church and missionary companion of St. Paul, who endured persecution together with him before serving as Bishop of Corinth.

name: St. Silouan the Athonite
title: Venerable
bio: A Russian monk of Mount Athos known for his profound humility and the teaching 'keep your mind in hell and despair not.'

name: St. Silvanus of Emesa
title: Bishop and Martyr
bio: Bishop of Emesa thrown to wild beasts in the amphitheater along with members of his flock.

name: St. Simeon of Jerusalem, Kinsman of the Lord
title: Hieromartyr, Bishop of Jerusalem
bio: Son of Cleopas and a kinsman of Christ, he succeeded James, the Brother of the Lord, as second bishop of Jerusalem and led the Christian community to safety at Pella before the Roman destruction of the city in 70. At the age of about 120 he was tortured and crucified under Trajan.

locations.label: Refuge of the Jerusalem church — Pella

name: St. Simeon of Persia
title: Hieromartyr, Bishop
bio: Bishop of Seleucia-Ctesiphon who refused to levy a double tax on Christians or to worship the sun, and was beheaded with many clergy on Good Friday 344 under Shapur II.

name: St. Simeon of Verkhoturye
title: Righteous
bio: A man of noble birth from European Russia who wandered to Siberia and lived as a humble travelling tailor near Verkhoturye, teaching the faith to the local peoples; his incorrupt relics were found in 1692.

name: St. Simeon the God-Receiver
title: Righteous
bio: Righteous elder who, promised he would not see death before beholding the Messiah, received the infant Christ in the Temple and proclaimed the Nunc Dimittis.

name: St. Simeon the Myrrh-Gusher, Founder of Hilandar
title: Monastic Founder
bio: The former Serbian ruler Stefan Nemanja who became a monk and, with his son St. Sava, founded Hilandar Monastery.

name: St. Simon of Ustyug
title: Fool-for-Christ
bio: A seventeenth-century Russian fool-for-Christ who exposed hidden sins and predicted future events with holy boldness.

name: St. Simon of Vladimir and Suzdal
title: Bishop
bio: A bishop and chronicler who authored the Kiev Caves Patericon, preserving the lives of early Russian monastic saints.

name: St. Simon the Myrrh-streamer of Simonopetra
title: Venerable, Monastic Founder
bio: A 13th-century hermit of Mount Athos who, on the night of the Nativity, saw a star come to rest over a great rock above the sea. On that rock he founded the monastery of Simonopetra, built on the cliff edge; after his death his relics streamed myrrh.

name: Apostle Simon the Zealot
title: Apostle
bio: One of the Twelve Apostles, formerly a Zealot, who preached in Egypt, Africa and the Caucasus before being martyred in Abkhazia.

name: St. Sisinnius the Confessor
title: Confessor
bio: A Byzantine cleric who suffered imprisonment for the veneration of icons under the iconoclast emperors.

name: St. Sisoes the Great
title: Venerable, Desert Father
bio: Egyptian desert father who succeeded St. Anthony the Great's disciple at the mountain of Anthony, renowned for his humility and profound sayings preserved in the Apophthegmata.

name: St. Sophia and her Daughters Faith, Hope and Love
title: Martyrs
bio: A widow martyred in Rome alongside her three young daughters, Faith, Hope, and Love, for refusing to worship idols.

name: St. Sophia of Suzdal
title: Venerable
bio: Solomonia Saburova, first wife of Grand Prince Vasily III, who was forced into the convent when she bore no heir and lived out her life in holiness at the Intercession Convent in Suzdal.

name: St. Sophronius of Jerusalem
title: Patriarch of Jerusalem
bio: Monk, hymnographer and patriarch who defended Orthodoxy against Monothelitism and surrendered Jerusalem peacefully when the city fell.

name: St. Sophronius of Vratsa
title: Bishop
bio: Bishop of Vratsa and a leader of the Bulgarian national revival, who copied St. Paisius of Hilendar's history, preached and wrote in everyday Bulgarian and published in 1806 the first printed book in modern Bulgarian.

name: St. Sophrony of Essex
title: Elder of Essex
bio: Disciple of St. Silouan the Athonite who brought hesychast monastic tradition to Western Europe, founding the Monastery of St. John the Baptist in Essex, England.

name: St. Sophrony of Irkutsk
title: Bishop
bio: Bishop of Irkutsk renowned for extensive missionary journeys across Siberia to Kamchatka and the Aleutian Islands.

name: Apostle Sosthenes
title: Apostle of the Seventy, Bishop of Colophon
bio: Ruler of the synagogue at Corinth who was beaten before the proconsul Gallio and is named by St. Paul as co-author of the First Epistle to the Corinthians; tradition makes him bishop of Colophon.

name: St. Sozon of Cilicia
title: Martyr
bio: A shepherd of Lycaonia who broke the hand off a golden idol at Pompeiopolis in Cilicia and gave the gold to the poor; he was burned under Maximian around 304.

name: St. Spyridon of Trimythous
title: Bishop, Wonderworker
bio: A simple Cypriot shepherd who became Bishop of Trimythous and attended the First Ecumenical Council of Nicaea, where he famously explained the Holy Trinity using a piece of brick; his incorrupt relics are now venerated in Corfu, of which he is patron saint.

locations.label: Episcopal see and death — Trimythous, Cyprus

name: Apostle Stachys
title: Apostle of the Seventy, Bishop of Byzantium
bio: Greeted by St. Paul as 'my beloved', he was ordained by St. Andrew as the first bishop of Byzantium, where he served for sixteen years.

name: St. Stefan Lazarević, Despot of Serbia
title: Ruler
bio: A Serbian despot celebrated for his patronage of the Church, literature, and monastic life amid Ottoman pressure.

name: St. Stefan Milutin, King of Serbia
title: Righteous
bio: A medieval Serbian king renowned for founding numerous monasteries and churches across the Balkans.

name: St. Stefan of Dečani
title: King and Martyr
bio: King Stefan Uroš III of Serbia, blinded in his youth on his father's orders and later healed, who founded the Visoki Dečani Monastery; he was strangled at Zvečan in 1331, and his incorrupt relics rest at Dečani.

locations.label: Monastery and relics — Visoki Dečani, Kosovo

name: St. Stefan Štiljanović
title: Righteous, Despot
bio: A 16th-century Serbian despot in Slavonia renowned for his charity in a time of famine; his incorrupt relics were long kept at Šišatovac Monastery and now rest in Belgrade's Cathedral of St. Michael.

locations.label: Relics — Cathedral of St. Michael, Belgrade

name: St. Stefan the First-Crowned
title: King
bio: Son of St. Simeon (Stefan Nemanja) and brother of St. Sava, he became the first crowned King of Serbia in 1217, founded the Žiča Monastery and took monastic vows as Simon shortly before his death.

name: St. Stefan Uroš V of Serbia
title: Emperor
bio: Son of Tsar Dušan and the last Nemanjić ruler of Serbia, reigning from 1355 to 1371. Gentle and pious, he was unable to hold together his father's empire against the ambitions of the nobility and is called "the Weak"; he died childless in 1371, and his relics rest in Belgrade's cathedral.

locations.label: Relics — Cathedral of St. Michael, Belgrade

name: St. Stephen of Hungary
title: King
bio: First king of Hungary, crowned in 1000, who established the Church in his realm, founded bishoprics and monasteries, and was recognized as a saint by the Ecumenical Patriarchate in 2000.

name: St. Stephen of Perm
title: Bishop
bio: Missionary bishop who created an alphabet for the Zyrian people and translated Scripture into their language.

name: St. Stephen of Perm's Disciple Gerasimus
title: Bishop
bio: A successor bishop who continued St. Stephen of Perm's mission of translating scripture for the Zyrian peoples.

name: St. Stephen of Surozh
title: Archbishop and Confessor
bio: A Cappadocian-born archbishop of Sougdaia (Sudak) in the Crimea who defended the holy icons before the iconoclast emperor, was imprisoned, and after his release shepherded his flock until his death in the late 8th century.

name: St. Stephen the Great
title: Right-believing Voivode of Moldavia
bio: Prince of Moldavia who defended his land against repeated invasions and founded dozens of churches and monasteries.

name: St. Stephen the New
title: Venerable Martyr
bio: An Athonite-trained monk martyred in Constantinople for his outspoken defense of holy icons.

name: St. Stephen the Protomartyr
title: Archdeacon and Protomartyr
bio: The first of the seven deacons and the first Christian martyr, stoned to death in Jerusalem.

name: St. Stephen the Sabaite
title: Venerable, Hymnographer
bio: A nephew of St. John of Damascus who entered the Lavra of St. Sabbas as a boy and lived there as a monk and hymnographer until his death in 794.

locations.label: Lavra of St. Sabbas — Judean Desert

name: St. Sturm of Fulda
title: Abbot
bio: A Bavarian noble entrusted as a boy to St. Boniface, who sent him to find a site for a monastery in the forests of Hesse. In 744 he founded the Abbey of Fulda, which he led as its first abbot, and which became a great centre of learning and mission; he died in 779.

name: St. Stylianos of Paphlagonia
title: Venerable
bio: Hermit in Paphlagonia who lived in extreme asceticism and received from God the gift of healing, especially for children. He is invoked as protector of children and expectant mothers.

name: St. Sunniva of Selja
title: Virgin Martyr
bio: According to legend, an Irish princess who fled by sea with companions to the island of Selja in Norway and died in a cave there; she is a patron saint of western Norway and of Bergen.

name: St. Susanna of Rome
title: Virgin Martyr
bio: A Roman noblewoman martyred under Diocletian for refusing marriage to the emperor's adopted son and rejecting idolatry.

name: St. Swithun of Winchester
title: Bishop of Winchester
bio: Anglo-Saxon bishop of Winchester renowned for humility and charitable works, whose relics became a major pilgrimage site.

name: St. Sylvester of Rome
title: Pope
bio: Bishop of Rome (314–335) during the reign of Constantine the Great, when the persecutions ended and the first great basilicas of Rome were built; his legates attended the First Ecumenical Council.

name: St. Symeon Metaphrastes
title: Hagiographer of Constantinople
bio: A tenth-century Byzantine official and hagiographer who compiled and rewrote the lives of many saints into a widely used collection of the Menologion.

name: St. Symeon of Thessalonica
title: Archbishop of Thessalonica
bio: Archbishop and liturgical theologian whose explanations of the services are a principal source for late Byzantine worship.

name: St. Symeon Stylite the Younger
title: Venerable
bio: Ascetic who spent decades atop a pillar on the Wondrous Mountain near Antioch, drawing pilgrims seeking healing and counsel.

name: St. Symeon the Fool-for-Christ
title: Venerable, Fool-for-Christ
bio: After long years in the desert he returned to the city and feigned madness, hiding his prayer and his charity beneath scandalous behaviour for the sake of his neighbours' salvation.

name: St. Symeon the New Theologian
title: Venerable
bio: A Byzantine monk and mystic whose writings on the vision of divine light influenced Orthodox spirituality.

name: St. Symeon the Stylite
title: Venerable
bio: A Syrian ascetic who spent decades living atop a pillar in prayer and fasting, becoming a renowned spiritual guide visited by pilgrims from across the ancient world.

name: St. Symphorian of Autun
title: Martyr
bio: A young nobleman of Autun in Gaul who refused to honour the statue of the goddess Cybele during her procession. He was condemned and beheaded outside the city around 180, while his mother called to him from the walls to lift his heart to heaven.

name: St. Synkletike of Alexandria
title: Venerable
bio: A desert mother whose sayings on ascetic discipline were preserved among the Apophthegmata Patrum.

name: St. Tabitha of Joppa
title: Righteous
bio: Disciple in Joppa known for her charitable works, raised from the dead by the Apostle Peter as recounted in the Acts of the Apostles.

name: St. Tamar the Great of Georgia
title: Queen
bio: Queen of Georgia during the kingdom's golden age, celebrated for wisdom, piety, and patronage of the arts and Church.

name: Sts. Tarachus, Probus and Andronicus
title: Martyrs
bio: Three Christians of different ages and homelands — a veteran soldier, a plebeian and a young nobleman — tried together in Cilicia under Diocletian; after repeated tortures at Tarsus, Mopsuestia and Anazarbus they were thrown to the beasts and then beheaded. The records of their trial survive.

name: St. Tarasios of Constantinople
title: Patriarch
bio: Patriarch who presided over the Seventh Ecumenical Council, restoring the veneration of holy icons.

name: St. Tatiana of Rome
title: Deaconess and Martyr
bio: A Roman deaconess tortured extensively and martyred for her faith under Emperor Alexander Severus.

name: St. Teilo of Llandeilo
title: Bishop
bio: A 6th-century Welsh bishop and companion of St. David who founded the monastery of Llandeilo Fawr and is honoured at Llandaff Cathedral.

name: Apostle Tertius
title: Apostle of the Seventy
bio: The scribe who wrote down Paul's Epistle to the Romans at Corinth and added his own greeting to it (Romans 16:22). Tradition counts him among the Seventy and records that he succeeded Sosipater as bishop of Iconium, where he ended his life as a martyr.

locations.label: Writing of the Epistle to the Romans — Corinth

name: Apostle Thaddeus of Edessa
title: Apostle of the Seventy
bio: Sent to Edessa after the Ascension with the Mandylion, the image of Christ 'not made by hands', he healed King Abgar and baptized the city, then preached in Syria and Mesopotamia; he reposed in Beirut.

name: St. Thaddeus of Tver, Hieromartyr
title: Archbishop and Martyr
bio: A Russian archbishop, professor, and spiritual father executed by Soviet authorities in 1937.

name: St. Thaisia of Egypt
title: Venerable
bio: A wealthy courtesan of Alexandria who was brought to repentance by Abba Paphnutius, burned her riches, and spent three years enclosed in a cell in prayer before reposing in peace.

name: Sts. Thalassios and Limnaios
title: Ascetics of Syria
bio: Two fifth-century ascetics of Syria associated with the region of Cyrrhus, remembered for strict open-air asceticism and spiritual counsel.

name: St. Thalelaeus the Unmercenary
title: Unmercenary Martyr
bio: A young physician from Lebanon who treated the sick without payment and was beheaded at Aegae in Cilicia under Numerian around 284.

name: St. Thecla the Protomartyr
title: Protomartyr Equal-to-the-Apostles
bio: A young woman of Iconium converted by hearing St. Paul preach, surviving multiple attempted martyrdoms.

name: St. Theoctiste the Lesbian
title: Ascetic
bio: A woman of Lesbos who fled Arab raiders and lived unknown for decades as a hermit on the island of Paros.

name: St. Theoctistus of Palestine
title: Venerable, Abbot
bio: Companion of St. Euthymius the Great, with whom he settled around 411 in a cave in a ravine of the Judean Desert. A community gathered around them, and while Euthymius sought greater solitude, Theoctistus led the monastery as abbot until his death in 467.

name: Sts. Theodora and Didymus
title: Martyrs
bio: A virgin of Alexandria condemned to a brothel for refusing to sacrifice, and the Christian soldier Didymus who rescued her by exchanging clothes with her; both were beheaded around 304.

name: St. Theodora of Alexandria
title: Venerable
bio: A repentant woman who lived disguised as a monk in the desert for years to atone for her sins.

name: St. Theodora of Arta
title: Venerable
bio: Empress of Epirus who, after enduring slander and exile, was reconciled with her husband and later became a nun, known for her charity and patience in suffering.

name: St. Theodora of Sihla
title: Venerable
bio: A Moldavian noblewoman who, with her husband's consent, became a nun and lived for decades as a hermit in a cave in the Sihla forest near Neamț in the 17th–18th centuries; her relics rest at the Kiev Caves Lavra.

name: St. Theodora of Thessaloniki
title: Nun of Thessaloniki
bio: A widow from Aegina who became a nun in Thessaloniki, renowned for her ascetic life; her myrrh-streaming relics are still venerated in the city.

name: St. Theodora of Vasta
title: Righteous
bio: A pious woman of Arcadia whose body upon death became the site of a church, with a tree said to grow from her tomb.

name: St. Theodora the Empress
title: Righteous
bio: A Byzantine empress who restored the veneration of icons, ending the second period of iconoclasm.

name: St. Theodore Graptos, the Branded
title: Confessor
bio: Brother of Theophanes the Branded, tortured and exiled for defending icon veneration under Emperor Theophilos.

name: St. Theodore of Byzantium, New Martyr
title: Martyr
bio: A young Constantinopolitan tradesman martyred for openly professing Christ before Ottoman authorities.

name: St. Theodore of Chernigov, Boyar and Martyr
title: Martyr
bio: The faithful boyar of Prince Michael of Chernigov who was martyred alongside him in the Golden Horde.

locations.label: Place of martyrdom — Golden Horde encampment

name: St. Theodore of Kythera
title: Venerable
bio: A widowed deacon from the Peloponnese who lived as a hermit on the then-deserted island of Kythera in the 10th century, among the ruins of a church of Sts. Sergius and Bacchus.

name: St. Theodore of Mytilene
title: New Martyr
bio: A young Christian of Lesvos martyred for his faith after being falsely accused before Ottoman authorities.

name: St. Theodore of Perge
title: Martyr
bio: A martyr of Perge in Pamphylia venerated for miracles worked in the pagan temple before his execution.

name: St. Theodore of Sykeon
title: Bishop, Wonderworker
bio: Byzantine bishop of Anastasioupolis renowned for extreme asceticism and healing miracles, whose life is preserved in one of the richest hagiographies of the era.

name: St. Theodore of Tarsus
title: Archbishop of Canterbury
bio: A Greek monk from Tarsus sent by Rome at the age of 66 to be Archbishop of Canterbury; he organized the English Church into dioceses, convened the Synod of Hertford and founded a renowned school at Canterbury.

name: St. Theodore Stratelates
title: Great Martyr
bio: A military commander of Heraclea Pontica beheaded for his faith after destroying an idol of Artemis.

name: St. Theodore the Sanctified of Tabennisi
title: Venerable, Abbot
bio: Beloved disciple of St. Pachomius the Great who led the Pachomian koinonia after him, guiding thousands of monks in Upper Egypt until his death in 368.

name: St. Theodore the Studite
title: Venerable Confessor
bio: Abbot of the Stoudios Monastery who defended the veneration of icons against iconoclast emperors.

name: St. Theodore the Studite's Companion Theophanes
title: Confessor
bio: A monastic confessor of the iconoclast era exiled for refusing to abandon the veneration of holy icons.

name: St. Theodore the Tyro
title: Great Martyr
bio: A young Roman soldier burned to death for setting fire to a pagan temple, remembered for the miracle of kolyva.

name: St. Theodore Ushakov
title: Righteous, Admiral
bio: Admiral of the Russian Black Sea Fleet, undefeated in battle. In 1798–1800 he freed the Ionian Islands from the French, taking the fortress of Corfu, and helped found the Septinsular Republic, the first self-governing Greek state of modern times. In retirement he lived devoutly near Sanaxar Monastery, gave generously to the poor, and was glorified by the Russian Church in 2001.

locations.label: Liberation of the Ionian Islands — Corfu

name: St. Theodore, Prince of Smolensk and Yaroslavl
title: Prince
bio: A pious thirteenth-century prince of Smolensk and Yaroslavl remembered for his charity and monastic repose.

name: St. Theodosia of Constantinople
title: Martyr
bio: A nun martyred in Constantinople for defending the holy icon of Christ over the Chalke Gate during the Iconoclast persecution.

name: St. Theodosia of Tyre
title: Virgin Martyr
bio: A young virgin of Tyre who was tortured and martyred at Caesarea for encouraging condemned Christians during the persecution of Diocletian.

name: St. Theodosius of Chernigov
title: Archbishop
bio: A seventeenth-century archbishop of Chernigov celebrated for pastoral zeal and posthumous miracles of healing.

name: St. Theodosius of Tarnovo
title: Hesychast
bio: A fourteenth-century Bulgarian hesychast monk who founded a monastic center near Tarnovo devoted to spiritual renewal.

name: St. Theodosius of the Kiev Caves
title: Venerable
bio: Co-founder of the Kiev Caves Lavra known for his humility, hospitality, and organization of communal monastic life.

name: St. Theodosius of Totma
title: Venerable, Monastic Founder
bio: A Vologda-born monk who founded the Monastery of the Saviour at Totma in 1554, wearing a heavy iron chain beneath his habit; he died in 1568.

name: St. Theodosius the Cenobiarch
title: Abbot, Founder of Communal Monasticism
bio: Cappadocian monk known as the father of communal (cenobitic) monasticism in Palestine, founding a great lavra near Bethlehem.

name: St. Theodotus of Ancyra
title: Martyr
bio: An innkeeper of Ancyra who secretly buried martyrs and was himself martyred during the persecution of Diocletian.

name: St. Theodotus of Cyrenia
title: Bishop and Confessor
bio: Bishop of Cyrenia in Cyprus who suffered torture during the Diocletianic persecution but survived to continue his ministry.

name: St. Theodoulos of Thassos
title: Ascetic
bio: A hermit-monk of the Thassos region revered locally for miracles of healing granted through prayer at his hermitage.

name: St. Theognostus of Moscow
title: Metropolitan
bio: A Greek from Constantinople who became Metropolitan of Kiev and All Rus' in 1328 and made Moscow his residence, continuing the work of St. Peter. He built the first stone churches of the Kremlin, defended the rights of the Church at the court of the Golden Horde, and blessed St. Alexis as his successor before dying of the plague in 1353.

locations.label: Metropolitan see and burial — Moscow Kremlin

name: St. Theophan the Recluse
title: Bishop, Recluse of Vysha
bio: Bishop who withdrew into seclusion to write and translate, giving Russia its own Philokalia and countless letters of spiritual direction.

name: St. Theophanes the Branded
title: Confessor and Hymnographer
bio: A Palestinian monk branded on the face with insulting verses by an iconoclast emperor, later Metropolitan of Nicaea.

name: St. Theophanes the Confessor of Sigriane
title: Venerable Confessor
bio: A wealthy official of Constantinople who, with his wife's consent, became a monk and founded the monastery of Megas Agros on Mount Sigriane near Cyzicus. He took part in the Seventh Ecumenical Council in 787 and wrote the Chronographia, a key source for Byzantine history; imprisoned by the iconoclast Leo V, he died in exile on Samothrace around 818.

locations.label: Megas Agros Monastery — Mount Sigriane, near Cyzicus

name: St. Theophano the Empress
title: Righteous
bio: A pious Byzantine empress known for her charity to the poor and devotion to prayer despite palace intrigue.

name: St. Theophylact of Nicomedia
title: Bishop and Confessor
bio: Bishop of Nicomedia renowned for his care of the sick and poor, who was exiled for some thirty years for defending the holy icons and died in exile around 845.

name: St. Theophylact of Ohrid
title: Archbishop and Biblical Commentator
bio: Byzantine Archbishop of Ohrid in the late 11th and early 12th centuries, best known for his commentaries on the Gospels and Epistles. He also wrote the Life of St. Clement of Ohrid and defended his flock against abuses.

name: St. Theosebia the Deaconess
title: Deaconess
bio: A sister of St. Gregory of Nyssa who served as a deaconess renowned for her ascetic life and charitable works.

name: St. Theotimus of Tomis
title: Bishop
bio: Bishop of Tomis at the end of the 4th century, called "the Philosopher" for his learning and his ascetic life. He preached to the Huns beyond the Danube, who called him "the god of the Romans" for his holiness, and he defended St. John Chrysostom when others turned against him.

name: St. Therapon of Sardis
title: Hieromartyr, Bishop
bio: Bishop of Sardis in Lydia, martyred around 259 during the persecution of Valerian after cruel tortures. Tradition says that an oak tree sprang up where his blood had fallen, and that its bark and leaves brought healing to the sick.

name: The Thirteen Martyrs of Kantara
title: Venerable Martyrs
bio: Orthodox monks of the Monastery of the Panagia Kantariotissa in the Pentadaktylos mountains of Cyprus. During the Latin rule of the island they refused to accept the Latin use of unleavened bread in the Eucharist, were imprisoned for three years, and in 1231 were executed in Nicosia by being dragged behind horses and burned.

locations.label: Monastery — Panagia Kantariotissa, near Kantara, Cyprus

name: The Thirty-Three Martyrs of Melitene
title: Martyrs
bio: Hieron, a strong farmer of Tyana in Cappadocia, and thirty-two companions who were forcibly conscripted into the Roman army under Diocletian. Refusing to sacrifice to the idols, they were tortured and beheaded at Melitene around 300.

name: St. Thomais of Lesbos
title: Righteous
bio: A tenth-century laywoman of Lesbos venerated for patient endurance of an unjust husband and her generosity to the poor.

name: Apostle Thomas
title: Apostle
bio: One of the Twelve Apostles, who doubted the Resurrection until he touched Christ's wounds, later evangelized India.

name: St. Thomas of Mount Athos
title: Monk
bio: An early monastic father associated with the founding communities of the Holy Mountain of Athos.

name: The Three Holy Youths Ananias, Azarias and Misael
title: Righteous
bio: Young Hebrew exiles at the court of Nebuchadnezzar in Babylon, companions of the Prophet Daniel. They refused to worship the king's golden image and were cast into a fiery furnace, where an angel kept them unharmed; their hymn of praise from the flames is sung in the Church's services to this day.

name: St. Tikhon of Moscow
title: Patriarch and Confessor
bio: Patriarch of Moscow during the Bolshevik Revolution, who steadfastly guided the Church through severe persecution.

locations.label: Archbishop of North America — New York

name: St. Tikhon of Zadonsk
title: Bishop
bio: A Russian bishop who retired to Zadonsk Monastery, where he wrote spiritual works and became known for his humility and care for the poor.

name: Apostle Timon
title: Apostle of the Seventy, Deacon
bio: One of the seven deacons chosen by the apostles in Jerusalem to serve the community (Acts 6:5). Tradition records that he became bishop of Bostra in Arabia, where he was seized by opponents of the faith; cast into fire, he is said to have come out unharmed before being put to death.

locations.label: Episcopal see and martyrdom — Bostra (Bosra), Arabia

name: Apostle Timothy
title: Apostle of the Seventy, Bishop of Ephesus
bio: Beloved disciple and co-worker of the Apostle Paul, and first Bishop of Ephesus, martyred for opposing pagan idolatry.

name: Sts. Timothy and Maura
title: Martyrs
bio: A reader and his young wife of only twenty days, from the Thebaid in Egypt, crucified facing each other at Antinoë under Diocletian after Timothy refused to surrender the sacred books.

name: St. Timothy of Prusa
title: Hieromartyr, Bishop
bio: Bishop of Prusa in Bithynia, known for his learning, his care for his flock and his gift of healing. Under Julian the Apostate he was imprisoned for converting pagans and was beheaded around 362.

name: Apostle Titus
title: Apostle
bio: A companion of the Apostle Paul who became the first bishop of Crete, guiding its early Christian community.

name: St. Triphyllius of Leucosia
title: Bishop
bio: A disciple of St. Spyridon of Trimythous who, after studying law in Beirut, became Bishop of Leucosia (Ledra, modern Nicosia) in the 4th century. Renowned for his eloquence and learning, praised by St. Jerome, he took part in the Council of Sardica in 343 in defence of Nicene Orthodoxy.

name: Apostle Trophimus
title: Apostle of the Seventy, Martyr
bio: A Gentile companion of St. Paul from Ephesus whose presence in Jerusalem sparked the riot that led to Paul's arrest; Paul later left him sick at Miletus. Tradition holds he was beheaded in Rome under Nero.

locations.label: Left sick by St. Paul — Miletus

name: Sts. Trophimus, Sabbatius and Dorymedon
title: Martyrs
bio: Trophimus and Sabbatius were arrested at Antioch in Pisidia under Emperor Probus in the late 3rd century; Sabbatius died under torture, and Trophimus was sent to Synnada. There the senator Dorymedon visited him in prison, was himself denounced as a Christian, and the two were beheaded together.

name: St. Tryphaena of Cyzicus
title: Martyr
bio: A noblewoman of Cyzicus on the Sea of Marmara who confessed Christ in the 1st century. After surviving fire and other tortures, she was gored to death by a wild bull in the arena; a spring is said to have flowed where she died, and she has long been invoked by nursing mothers.

name: St. Tryphon of Campsada
title: Martyr
bio: A young goose-herder martyred under Emperor Decius, later venerated as protector of crops and vineyards.

name: St. Tryphon of Pechenga
title: Venerable, Enlightener of the Lapps
bio: A Novgorodian who became missionary to the Sami (Lapp) people of the Kola Peninsula, built a church on the Pasvik River and founded the Pechenga Monastery, one of the northernmost in the world; he died in 1583.

locations.label: Church of Sts. Boris and Gleb — Pasvik River

name: St. Tryphon of Vyatka
title: Venerable, Missionary
bio: A monk from the far north of Russia who preached to the pagan Ostyaks and Voguls along the Kama River, cutting down their sacred trees and baptizing many. In 1580 he founded the Dormition Monastery at Khlynov (Vyatka), where he died in 1612.

name: The Twenty-Six Martyrs of Zographou
title: Venerable Martyrs
bio: Monks of the Bulgarian Zographou Monastery on Mount Athos who refused to accept the union with Rome imposed by Emperor Michael VIII Palaiologos. In 1275 Latin soldiers burned them alive in the monastery tower, where they had shut themselves in with their abbot Thomas.

name: Apostle Tychicus
title: Apostle of the Seventy
bio: A companion of the Apostle Paul from the province of Asia who carried his epistles to the Ephesians and Colossians and was sent on missions to Ephesus and Crete (2 Timothy 4:12; Titus 3:12). Tradition counts him among the Seventy and makes him bishop of Colophon in Ionia.

name: St. Tychon of Amathus
title: Bishop
bio: Fourth-century bishop of Amathus in Cyprus famed for miracles connected with viticulture and care for the poor.

name: St. Tysilio of Meifod
title: Venerable, Abbot
bio: A 7th-century prince of Powys who chose the monastic life, founding a cell on Church Island in the Menai Strait (Llandysilio) and later leading the mother church of Meifod. Breton tradition holds that he afterwards crossed to Brittany, where he is venerated as St. Suliau.

name: St. Ulrich of Augsburg
title: Bishop
bio: Bishop of Augsburg for fifty years (923–973), educated at the monastery of St. Gall. He rebuilt his city after Magyar raids and led its defence in the siege that preceded the Battle of Lechfeld in 955, and was devoted to the poor and the sick; in 993 he became the first saint formally canonized by a pope.

name: St. Vakhtang Gorgasali
title: King
bio: King of Kartli in the 5th century who strengthened the Georgian Church, founded Tbilisi according to tradition, and died of wounds fighting the Persians around 502.

name: St. Valentine
title: Martyr
bio: A priest of Rome martyred under Claudius II for secretly marrying Christian couples and aiding persecuted believers.

name: St. Varlaam of Khutyn
title: Monastic Founder
bio: Founder of the Transfiguration Monastery at Khutyn near Novgorod, celebrated for miracles of healing.

name: St. Varlaam of Moldavia
title: Metropolitan
bio: Metropolitan of Moldavia (1632–1653) who published the 'Cazania' of 1643, a landmark of early Romanian printing, and defended Orthodoxy against Calvinist catechisms.

name: St. Varus of Egypt
title: Martyr
bio: A Roman soldier in Egypt who visited imprisoned monks; when one of them died, he took his place before the judge and was tortured to death. A pious widow, Cleopatra, buried his body in her home village, and the Church prays to him for those who died unbaptized.

name: St. Vasilko of Rostov
title: Prince and Martyr
bio: Prince of Rostov taken captive by the Mongols after the Battle of the Sit River in 1238; refusing to serve Batu Khan or abandon his faith, he was killed in the Sherensky forest.

name: St. Vedast of Arras
title: Bishop
bio: A priest of Toul who instructed King Clovis in the faith as he returned from his victory over the Alemanni, preparing him for baptism at Reims around 496. Consecrated by St. Remigius as bishop of Arras, he restored the Church there and reposed in 540.

name: St. Venantius Fortunatus
title: Bishop of Poitiers, Hymnographer
bio: Italian-born poet and bishop of Poitiers whose Latin hymns on the Cross remain part of Western liturgical tradition.

name: St. Verena of Zurzach
title: Venerable
bio: A Christian woman from Thebes in Egypt who, according to tradition, followed the Theban Legion to the Alps. After the legion's martyrdom she lived as a hermit near Solothurn and later at Zurzach on the Rhine, where she cared for the poor and the sick until her death in the 4th century.

name: St. Victor of Glazov, Hieromartyr
title: Bishop and Martyr
bio: A bishop of Glazov repeatedly imprisoned by Soviet authorities, dying in a labor camp for his refusal to compromise the faith.

locations.label: Place of martyrdom — Northern Russia labor camp

name: St. Victor of Marseille
title: Martyr
bio: A Roman soldier at Marseille who refused to offer incense to the idols around 290 and was tortured and crushed under a millstone. St. John Cassian later founded the Abbey of St. Victor over the crypt where he was buried.

locations.label: Martyrdom and tomb — Abbey of St. Victor, Marseille

name: St. Vincent of Lérins
title: Venerable
bio: Monk of the island monastery of Lérins who wrote the Commonitorium, defining the Orthodox faith as 'what has been believed everywhere, always and by all'.

name: St. Vincent of Saragossa
title: Deacon and Martyr
bio: A deacon of Saragossa arrested with his bishop Valerius under Diocletian; tortured on a gridiron at Valencia, he died in prison in 304.

name: St. Virgil of Salzburg
title: Bishop
bio: An Irish-born abbot and bishop of Salzburg, a learned geographer who built the first cathedral there and sent missionaries to Carinthia; he died in 784.

name: Sts. Visarion, Sofronie and Oprea
title: Confessors
bio: Three 18th-century confessors of Transylvania — the monk Visarion Sarai, the hieromonk Sofronie of Cioara and the peasant Oprea Miclăuș — who defended Orthodoxy against forced union with Rome; Visarion and Oprea died in Habsburg prisons.

name: St. Vitus of Lucania
title: Martyr
bio: A Sicilian boy raised in the faith by his tutor Modestus and nurse Crescentia, with whom he fled to Lucania in southern Italy and was martyred under Diocletian; he is invoked against 'St. Vitus' dance'.

name: St. Vladimir of Kiev, Hieromartyr
title: Metropolitan and Martyr
bio: Metropolitan of Kiev killed by revolutionary soldiers in 1918, the first hierarch martyred in the Russian Revolution.

name: St. Vladimir of Novgorod
title: Prince
bio: Eldest son of Yaroslav the Wise and St. Anna, prince of Novgorod, who built the stone Cathedral of St. Sophia there (1045–1050), where he is buried; he died in 1052.

name: St. Vladimir, Equal-to-the-Apostles
title: Equal-to-the-Apostles
bio: Grand Prince of Kiev who converted from paganism and brought Christianity to the Rus' people.

name: St. Vsevolod of Pskov
title: Prince
bio: Prince Vsevolod-Gabriel, grandson of Vladimir Monomakh, who was expelled from Novgorod and welcomed by Pskov, where he built the first Trinity Cathedral before his death in 1138.

name: St. Walburga of Heidenheim
title: Venerable, Abbess
bio: Sister of St. Willibald, an English nun who joined St. Boniface's mission and became abbess of Heidenheim; her relics at Eichstätt are said to exude a healing oil.

name: St. Wandrille of Fontenelle
title: Abbot
bio: A Frankish noble at the court of King Dagobert who left his career and his marriage, both he and his wife entering monastic life. After years as a pilgrim and monk, including at Bobbio, he founded the Abbey of Fontenelle in Normandy in 649 and died there in 668.

name: St. Wenceslaus of Bohemia
title: Right-Believing Prince, Martyr
bio: Duke of Bohemia, raised in the faith by his grandmother St. Ludmila, who was known for his charity and was murdered by his brother Boleslav.

name: St. Werburgh of Chester
title: Venerable, Abbess
bio: A Mercian princess and abbess who reformed the convents of Mercia; her relics were later enshrined at Chester, whose cathedral was originally dedicated to her.

name: St. Wilfrid of York
title: Bishop
bio: Bishop of York who championed the Roman reckoning of Easter at the Synod of Whitby in 664, founded monasteries at Ripon and Hexham and evangelized the South Saxons.

locations.label: Mission to the South Saxons — Selsey

name: St. Willehad of Bremen
title: Bishop, Missionary
bio: A Northumbrian priest who preached among the Frisians and Saxons, narrowly surviving several attacks by pagans. Charlemagne made him the first bishop of Bremen in 787, where he built the first cathedral before his repose in 789.

name: St. Willibald of Eichstätt
title: Bishop
bio: An English monk who made a long pilgrimage to the Holy Land, helped restore Monte Cassino and was made by St. Boniface the first bishop of Eichstätt; he died around 787.

name: St. Willibrord of Frisia
title: Archbishop of Utrecht, Apostle of the Frisians
bio: Northumbrian monk known as the Apostle of the Frisians, who became the first Bishop of Utrecht and founded the abbey of Echternach, where he is buried.

name: St. Winifred of Holywell
title: Virgin Martyr
bio: A Welsh maiden beheaded by a chieftain whose advances she refused; according to tradition a spring rose where her head fell and she was restored to life by her uncle St. Beuno, later becoming an abbess at Gwytherin.

name: St. Winwaloe of Landévennec
title: Venerable, Monastic Founder
bio: Son of a British prince settled in Brittany, he studied under St. Budoc on the island of Lavret and around 485 founded the abbey of Landévennec on the Aulne estuary, which he led in strict asceticism until his repose in the early 6th century. Many churches in Brittany and Cornwall bear his name (Guénolé, Gunwalloe).

name: St. Wite of Whitchurch Canonicorum
title: Martyr
bio: A Saxon holy woman of Dorset, perhaps killed in a Viking raid. Her relics still lie in a medieval stone shrine in the church of Whitchurch Canonicorum — one of the very few English shrines to survive the Reformation with their saint's relics inside — and pilgrims still leave prayers in the openings of the tomb.

locations.label: Shrine — Church of St. Candida and Holy Cross, Whitchurch Canonicorum

name: St. Withburga of Dereham
title: Venerable, Abbess
bio: The youngest daughter of King Anna of East Anglia and sister of St. Etheldreda, she founded a convent at East Dereham in the 7th century; tradition says the Theotokos sent two does to give milk to feed her builders. Her well still flows in the churchyard where she was first buried, before her relics were taken to Ely in 974.

locations.label: Convent and holy well — East Dereham

name: St. Wolfgang of Regensburg
title: Bishop
bio: A Swabian monk of Einsiedeln who went as a missionary to the Magyars before becoming bishop of Regensburg in 972. He reformed monasteries, cared for the poor and taught the future Emperor Henry II; for a time he withdrew as a hermit beside the lake now called the Wolfgangsee, and he reposed at Pupping in 994.

name: St. Wystan of Repton
title: Prince and Martyr
bio: A prince of Mercia, grandson of King Wiglaf, who opposed the marriage of his widowed mother to his kinsman Beorhtfrith as contrary to the Church's canons. He was murdered by Beorhtfrith in 849 and buried in the royal crypt at Repton, which still survives.

locations.label: Burial — crypt of St. Wystan's Church, Repton

name: St. Xenia of Rome
title: Venerable, Deaconess
bio: Eusebia, daughter of a Roman senator, who fled on her wedding day, took the name Xenia ('stranger') and founded a convent at Mylasa in Caria, where she served as a deaconess until her death in the 5th century.

name: St. Xenia of St. Petersburg
title: Fool-for-Christ
bio: A widow who gave away all her possessions and lived as a homeless fool-for-Christ, beloved for her clairvoyance and charity.

locations.label: Grave and chapel — Smolensk Cemetery, St. Petersburg

name: Sts. Xenophon, Maria, John and Arcadius
title: Righteous Family of Constantinople
bio: A wealthy Constantinopolitan family separated by shipwreck and reunited by divine providence in Jerusalem, after which they gave away their riches and embraced monastic life.

name: St. Yaroslav the Wise
title: Grand Prince
bio: Son of St. Vladimir and Grand Prince of Kiev, who built the Cathedral of St. Sophia, founded schools and libraries, issued the first law code of Rus' and joined his house by marriage to much of Europe; he died in 1054.

name: St. Yuri II of Vladimir
title: Grand Prince and Martyr
bio: Grand Prince of Vladimir who fell fighting Batu's Mongol army at the Sit River in 1238, after his capital had been sacked and his family killed; his relics rest in Vladimir's Dormition Cathedral.

name: Apostle Zacchaeus
title: Apostle of the Seventy
bio: The chief tax collector of Jericho who climbed a sycamore tree to see Jesus and, after receiving Him into his house, gave half of his goods to the poor and repaid fourfold all he had wronged (Luke 19:1–10). Tradition records that he followed the Apostle Peter and became bishop of Caesarea in Palestine.

name: Sts. Zacharias and Elizabeth
title: Righteous, Parents of the Forerunner
bio: Priest and his wife, the aged and childless couple granted a son, John the Baptist, in fulfillment of the angel Gabriel's promise.

name: Holy Prophet Zechariah
title: Prophet
bio: One of the twelve minor prophets, who after the return from Babylon encouraged the rebuilding of the Temple and foretold the King entering Jerusalem humble and riding on a donkey.

name: Sts. Zenaida and Philonella
title: Unmercenary Physicians
bio: Sisters from Tarsus, kinswomen of St. Paul, who studied medicine and settled near Demetrias in Thessaly, treating the sick free of charge from a cave on Mount Pelion; they are regarded as the first women unmercenaries.

name: St. Zeno of Verona
title: Bishop
bio: Born in North Africa, he became bishop of Verona around 362 and laboured to convert the remaining pagans and to defend the Nicene faith against Arianism. Many of his sermons survive; the great Romanesque basilica of San Zeno stands over his tomb.

locations.label: Episcopal see and tomb — Basilica of San Zeno, Verona

name: Sts. Zenobius and Zenobia
title: Martyrs
bio: A physician bishop and his sister martyred together in Cilicia under Diocletian's persecution.

name: Holy Prophet Zephaniah
title: Prophet
bio: Minor prophet in the days of King Josiah who proclaimed the coming 'day of the Lord' and the joy of the restored daughter of Zion.

name: St. Zlata (Chryse) of Meglen
title: Virgin Martyr
bio: A peasant girl from the village of Slatino in Moglena who refused to convert to Islam and marry her abductor, and after months of torture was hanged in 1795.

name: St. Zosimas of Palestine
title: Monk of the Jordan
bio: A monk of a monastery near the Jordan River who encountered St. Mary of Egypt in the wilderness, heard her life's story, and gave her Holy Communion.

name: St. Zosimas of Solovki
title: Venerable
bio: Co-founder of the Solovetsky Monastery in the White Sea, whose ascetic labors established one of Russia's great centers of monasticism.

name: St. Zosimas the Wanderer
title: Ascetic
bio: A wandering ascetic of Cilicia who lived among wild beasts unharmed, an example of restored paradise cited by later Church writers.

name: St. Zoticus the Feeder of Orphans
title: Priest and Confessor
bio: A priest of Constantinople who founded hospitals and orphanages, surviving persecution to die peacefully in old age.

name: Sts. Zoticus, Attalus, Camasis and Philip
title: Martyrs
bio: Christians martyred at Noviodunum on the lower Danube during the persecution of Diocletian (c. 304). Their relics, with their names inscribed in Greek, were found in 1971 in a crypt beneath an early Christian basilica at Niculițel in Romania, and are now venerated at the nearby Cocoș Monastery.
